His saying: ﴿So marry what is good for you of women﴾. Since the intended meaning is the attribute, and the attribute is what motivates the command to marry and is its aim, namely goodness (*tayyib*), so that the woman described by it is the one married, he used *ma* rather than *man*. This is a principle that never fails, and it is among the most refined features of the Arabic language.

(Section)

Al-Shafi'i said: "[It means] that your dependants not be many. This shows that having few dependants is closer [to the desired outcome]."

It is said: al-Shafi'i said this, but the majority of the exegetes, from the early and later generations, disagreed and said: the meaning of the verse is, "That is nearer to your not being unjust or deviating."

It is said that *ʿāla al-rajulu yaʿūlu ʿawlan* means the man deviated and acted unjustly. From this comes *ʿawl al-farāʾiḍ* (the increase in the shares of the inheritance), because its shares increased. It is also said *ʿāla yaʿīlu ʿaylatan* when one is in need. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾ [9:28].

And a poet said:

"The poor man does not know when his wealth will come, and the rich man does not know when he will become needy."

That is, when he will be in need and impoverished. As for the multiplicity of dependants, it is neither of these, but is from *afʿala*. It is said *aʿāla al-rajulu yuʿīlu* when his dependants become many, like *albana* and *atmara*, when he becomes one who has milk and dates. This is the view of the linguists. Al-Wahidi said in his *al-Basit*: "The meaning of *taʿūlū* is *tamīlū* (you incline) and *tajūrū* (you act unjustly), according to all the exegetes and linguists. This was also transmitted as a prophetic report."

ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, related from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning "that you not be unjust" [4:3], that he said: "Do not act unjustly." And it is related: "that you not incline." He said: "This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Rabiʿ, al-Suddi, Ibn Malik, ʿIkrima, al-Farraʾ, al-Zajjaj, Ibn Qutayba and Ibn al-Anbari."

I say: That this meaning is the one required by the verse is shown, even though what al-Shafi'i mentioned is a valid linguistic usage, which al-Farraʾ related from al-Kisa'i, who said: "Some of the Companions said: *ʿāla yaʿūlu* when his dependants increase." Al-Kisa'i said: "This is an eloquent dialect that I heard from the Arabs." But the first meaning is the one that is determined, for several reasons.

First: it is the well-known meaning in the language, and almost nothing else is known. *ʿāla yaʿūlu* meaning "his dependants increased" is not known except from al-Kisa'i's report, while the rest of the linguists disagree with it.

Second: this has been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ), and even if it were rare, it would still be suitable for preference.

Third: it has been transmitted from ʿĀʾisha and Ibn ʿAbbas, and no exegete is known to oppose them. Al-Hakim Abu ʿAbd Allah said: "The exegesis of the Companions is, in our view, equivalent to a report traced to the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Fourth: the evidence we have cited for the recommendation of marrying fertile women, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) statement that he will outnumber the nations with his community on the Day of Resurrection, refutes this interpretation.

Fifth: the context of the verse concerns moving them from what they fear as injustice and oppression in that matter to something else. He said at its beginning: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly towards orphans, then marry of the women what is good for you, two, three, or four﴾ [4:3]. So Allah showed them how to free themselves from wronging orphans, namely by marrying the women who are of age and whom they find good, and He permitted them up to four of them. Then He showed them how to free themselves from injustice and oppression in failing to treat them equally, saying: ﴿But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry] one, or what your right hands possess﴾ [4:3]. Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that one wife or a slave-woman is nearer to avoiding inclination and injustice. This is clear evidence of the intended meaning.

Sixth: the statement ﴿But if you fear that you will not be just﴾ does not fit with "so marry one, or take concubines as you wish," because that is not closer to your dependants becoming many. Rather, this is unrelated to the first part. Consider it carefully.

Seventh: it is impossible to say to them: "If you fear that you will not be just among four, then you may take a hundred concubines or more, for that is nearer to your dependants not being many."

Eighth: His statement ﴿That is nearer to your not being unjust﴾ is the reason for each of the two preceding rulings, namely moving them from marrying orphans to marrying women who are of age, and from four wives to one wife or what the right hand possesses. It does not befit that this be justified by having few dependants.

Ninth: He, glorified is He, said ﴿But if you fear that you will not be just﴾ and did not say "if you fear that you will not become poor and in need." If the meaning were having few dependants, this would have been the more appropriate wording.

Tenth: when Allah, glorified is He, mentions a prohibited ruling and gives the reason for the prohibition, or permits something and ties its permission to a cause, the cause must be the opposite of the contrary of the ruling it justifies. Allah has justified the permission to marry women other than orphans, and limiting oneself to one wife or the right hand's possession, by saying that it is closer to not being unjust. It is known that having many dependants is not the opposite of the absence of the ruling being justified. So it is not fitting to justify it by that. And Allah knows best.

(Section: The Prophet's (ﷺ) prevention of ʿAli from combining Fatima and the daughter of Abu Jahl)

The sons of Hisham ibn al-Mughira asked his permission for them to marry ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, to the daughter of Abu Jahl. He did not grant permission for that and said: "Unless Ibn Abi Talib wants to divorce my daughter and marry their daughter. Fatima is only a part of me. What troubles her troubles me, and what hurts her hurts me. I fear that Fatima may be tested in her religion. I do not make lawful what is unlawful, nor make unlawful what is lawful, but by Allah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah and the daughter of the enemy of Allah will never be together in one place."

In another wording, he mentioned a son-in-law of his and praised him, and said: "He spoke to me and was truthful with me, and he promised me and fulfilled his promise to me."

This ruling includes several matters.

The first: if a man stipulates to his wife that he will not marry another woman over her, he is bound to fulfil the condition, and if he marries another over her, she has the right to annul. The way the hadith implies this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that this hurts Fatima and troubles her, and that it hurts him (ﷺ) and troubles him. It is certain that the Prophet (ﷺ) married Fatima, may Allah be pleased with her, on the basis that he would not hurt her, trouble her, hurt her father (ﷺ), or trouble him. Even if this was not stipulated in the body of the contract, it is known by necessity that he entered upon [the matter] when he mentioned his other son-in-law and praised him for speaking truthfully and keeping his promise. That was an indirect reference to ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, and an incitement for him to follow that example. This suggests that a promise was given to her that he would not trouble or hurt her, and so he urged him to fulfil it, just as his other son-in-law had fulfilled it to him.

From this it is derived that what is customarily stipulated is like what is stipulated verbally, and that its absence gives the party who stipulated it the right to annul. So if it were assumed that it was the custom of a people not to take their women out of their homes and not to allow their husbands to do this at all, and this custom persisted, it would be like what is stipulated verbally. This is consistent with the principles of the people of Medina and the principles of Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, that a customary condition is equal to a verbal one. For this reason they required payment from one who gave his garment to a launderer or a fuller, or his dough to a baker, or his food to a cook, who work for pay, or who entered the bathhouse or hired someone to wash him, from those whose custom is to wash for pay, and similar cases, even if he did not stipulate a fee; he is liable for the customary fee.

On this basis, if it were assumed that the woman comes from a household in which a man does not marry a co-wife over their women and they never allow him to do so, and their custom is constant in this, it would be like what is stipulated verbally.

Likewise, if she is one who is known to not allow a co-wife to be introduced to her customarily because of her nobility, lineage and dignity, then leaving marriage over her would be the same as what is stipulated verbally.

On this basis, the lady of the women of the worlds and the daughter of the master of all the children of Adam are most deserving of this. So if ʿAli had stipulated it in the body of the contract, it would have been a confirmation, not an establishment of a new ruling.

In the Prophet's (ﷺ) prevention of ʿAli from combining Fatima, may Allah be pleased with her, with the daughter of Abu Jahl, there is a wondrous wisdom: a woman with her husband is in his rank, following him. If she is herself of a high rank and her husband is likewise, she is in a high rank by herself and by her husband. This was the case of Fatima and ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with them both. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, would not have placed the daughter of Abu Jahl with Fatima, may Allah be pleased with her, in one rank, neither by herself nor by following. And there is as much difference between them as there is. So her marriage over the lady of the women of the worlds was neither commendable in law nor in standing.

The Prophet (ﷺ) indicated this by his saying: "By Allah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah and the daughter of the enemy of Allah will never be together in one place." Thus this either encompasses the rank of the other by its wording or by its indication.

(Section: The wisdom in limiting wives to four but not concubines)

As for his saying: "He limited the number of women married to four, and permitted ownership by right hand without limit," this is part of His complete blessing, the perfection of His law, and its agreement with wisdom, mercy and benefit. Marriage is intended for intercourse and fulfilling one's need. Among people there are those whose desire dominates so that one wife does not satisfy them, so He permitted for him a second, a third and a fourth. This number suits the number of his temperaments and elements, and the number of the seasons of his year. It also allows him to return to one wife after patiently abstaining from the others for three [periods], and three is the first degree of plurality. The Lawgiver has attached several rulings to it: He allowed the emigrant to remain in Mecca three days after completing his rites; He permitted the traveller to wipe over his leather socks for three [days]; He made the limit of the recommended or obligatory hospitality three days; and He permitted a woman to mourn for someone other than her husband for three days. He showed mercy to the co-wife by making the limit of her husband's absence from her three [days], after which he returns. This is pure mercy, wisdom and benefit.

As for concubines, since they were like all other property such as horses, slaves and other things, there was no meaning in restricting the owner to four of them or any other number. Just as it is not part of Allah's wisdom and mercy that a master be restricted to four slaves or four animals, clothes or the like, so it is not part of His wisdom to restrict him to four concubines. Also, a wife has a right over her husband arising from the marriage contract, which the husband must uphold. If another shares her, he must be just between them. So restricting husbands to a number in which justice is closer is more appropriate than exceeding it. Even so, they cannot be just, however much they strive for it. Their concubines have no right over him in this matter, and for this reason they are not owed a turn. This is why Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry] one, or what your right hands possess﴾ [4:3]. And Allah knows best.

(Section: The wisdom in permitting men plurality but not women)

As for his saying: "He permitted a man to marry four wives, but did not permit a woman to marry more than one husband," this is part of the perfect wisdom of the Lord, the Exalted, toward them, His kindness and mercy toward His creation, and His care for their interests. He is exalted above the opposite of that, and His law is far removed from bringing anything other than this. If a woman were permitted to be with two or more husbands, the world would be corrupted, lineages would be lost, husbands would kill one another, calamity would grow, trial would intensify, and the marketplace of war would be set up on its legs. How could the affairs of a woman with several partners in dispute be sound? And how could the affairs of partners in her be sound?

Thus the Law coming with the opposite of this is among the greatest proofs of the wisdom, mercy and care of the Lawgiver for His creation.

If it is said: "How was the man's side taken into account, and he was allowed to cast his gaze, fulfil his need, and move from one wife to another according to his desire and need, while the woman's motive is his motive and her desire is his desire?"

It is said: Since the custom of women is to be hidden behind veils and concealed within the inner rooms of their homes, and their temperament is cooler than the man's, and their outward and inward movement is less than his, and the man has been given more strength and heat, which is the dominion of desire, than woman has been given, and he has been tested with what she has not been tested with, He allowed him from the number of wives what He did not allow the woman. This is among the things by which Allah has favoured men and preferred them over women, just as He preferred them over women with prophethood, messengership, the caliphate, sovereignty, leadership, the authority of rule, jihad and other things. He made men guardians over women, striving for their interests, toiling in the means of their livelihood, facing dangers, traversing deserts, and exposing themselves to every calamity and trial for the sake of their wives' interests. The Lord, the Exalted, is Most Thankful and Most Forbearing. So He thanked them for that and compensated them by enabling them with what He did not enable wives with. And if you compare the toil, hardship, exertion and fatigue of men in securing women's interests with what women are tested with, namely jealousy, you will find that men's share in bearing that toil, fatigue and exertion is greater than women's share in bearing jealousy. This is from the perfection of Allah's justice, wisdom and mercy. So to Him belongs all praise, as He is worthy of it.

As for the claim of the one who says, "The desire of a woman exceeds the desire of a man," it is not as he said. Desire springs from heat, and where is the heat of the female compared to the heat of the male? Rather, the woman, because of her leisure, idleness, and lack of occupation that would distract her from her desire and from fulfilling her need, is overwhelmed by the power of desire, which takes control over her. Nothing in her opposes it. Rather, it finds a empty heart and a vacant soul, so it becomes firmly established in her. Thus the one who thinks this supposes that her desire is many times the desire of a man, and it is not so.

Among what indicates this is that when a man has intercourse with his wife, he is able to have intercourse with another immediately. "The Prophet (ﷺ) would go around to his wives in one night." Sulaymān (Solomon) went around to ninety women in one night, and it is known that for each woman he had desire and heat that moved him to intercourse. When a man has fulfilled his need, the woman's desire cools, her soul is subdued, and she does not seek its fulfillment from another at that time. Thus the wisdom of qadar (divine decree), the Law, creation, and command agree. And to Allah belongs all praise.

Also: the husband has the authority to provide maintenance for his wife, just as he has the authority to restrain her and prevent her from leaving his house. The Lawgiver placed this in his hands and commanded him to take charge of the woman, not to hand her his wealth, but to provide for her and clothe her from it. Allah, glorified is He, placed her in this respect in the position of the child and the insane person under their guardian, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not give the foolish your property, which Allah has made a means of support for you, but provide for them from it and clothe them﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Do not intend your property, which Allah has entrusted to you and made your means of livelihood, and then give it to your wife and your sons, so that they become the ones who take charge of you in their clothing, provision and maintenance.

The foolish (al-sufahaʾ) are women and children. Allah, glorified is He, has made husbands guardians (qawwamun) over them, just as He made the child's guardian a guardian over him, and the one in charge of another is trustworthy with respect to him. Accepting the word of the wife or the child after reaching maturity regarding their not having received the maintenance, he has made them guardians over the husbands and the guardians. If the husband's word were not accepted, he would not be a guardian over the woman. For if the woman, when she is a debtor, is accepted as credible over the husband, she would be the one in charge.

In sum, the husband has authority over his wife, even over her property. He may prevent her from giving it away in charity, because he only paid her the dower on account of her property and her person. So she has no right to dispose of it in a way that prevents the husband from fully enjoying her. The Prophet (ﷺ) equated the maintenance of wives with the maintenance of slaves, and made the woman a captive (ʿaniyah) with the husband. The ʿani is the captive, and this is a kind of bondage. He said regarding the woman: "You feed her from what you eat, and clothe her from what you wear."

He said the same regarding the slave. The husband is thus the commander over the maintenance of his wife, his slave, and his children, by virtue of his being their guardian. Allah, glorified is He, did not obligate husbands to make women owners of food, condiments, or dirhams at all; He only obligated feeding and clothing them in a reasonable manner. Obligating transfer of ownership is something no Book, Sunnah, or consensus (ijmaʿ) has indicated.

(Fāʾidah)

It is legally prescribed that a father's gift to his children be in proportion to their shares of inheritance, because Allah the Exalted has forbidden what leads to severing of the ties of kinship and to equalizing between male and female in a manner that contradicts the detailed distinction laid down by the Sharia, and this leads to enmity. Also, the Sharia knows better our interests, so if preferring the male over the female were not the more beneficial course, it would not have prescribed it. Also, the male's need for wealth is greater than the female's need, and because Allah the Exalted made the female half of the male in testimony, inheritance and blood-money, and in the ʿaqīqah (the sacrifice made for a newborn) by the Sunnah.

Also, because Allah the Exalted made men qawwāmūn (protectors and maintainers) over women. So when the male knows that the father has given the female more than the gift Allah gave her, and has equalized her with one whom Allah has preferred over her, this leads to enmity and severing, just as when he is preferred over someone else whom Allah has made equal to him.

So what difference is there between preferring one whom Allah has commanded to be treated equally with his brother, and equalizing between those whom Allah has commanded to be distinguished from one another?

Ibn ʿAqīl raised an objection to the argument for preference and said: "The gift during life, in health and with one's own wealth, is a right of no one; for this reason it is not permissible for him to make gifts and grants to an heir, and what exceeds one-third for non-heirs is taken into account at the time of his health and cut off from the state of terminal illness, let alone death.

Likewise, sisters are given (something) in the presence of a son and a father, even though they have no right in the inheritance, and that is a gift from Allah by way of arbitrary decree, in which no one has a choice. Whereas this is a gift from a responsible, unrestricted person, so it is in accordance with his choice, whether preference or equality.

This is the correct view in my opinion."

I say: This argument is very weak, for it is invalidated by what he himself conceded regarding the prohibition of preferring among children who are equal in maleness and femaleness. How can his statement be valid that it is a gift from a responsible, unrestricted person, so it is permissible according to his choice, when you have restricted him in preferring between equals?

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on surah 4, verse 12:

For Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned the bequest before the inheritance, provided it does not cause harm to the heirs. If a bequest is a harmful bequest (wasiyyat dirar), it is forbidden. The heirs may then nullify it, and the legatee is forbidden to take it without the heirs' consent. Allah, glory be to Him, emphasised this with His words: ﴿These are the limits set by Allah, so do not transgress them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229].

Consider how Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned harm (dirar) in this verse but not in the one before it. The first verse dealt with the inheritance of the ascendants and descendants, and the second dealt with the inheritance of collateral relatives: the spouses and the siblings.

It is customary for a deceased person to harm his wife and his siblings, while he rarely harms his parents and children.

Harm (dirar) is of two kinds: deviation (janf) and sin (ithm). A person may intend harm, which is sin, or he may cause harm without intending it, which is deviation. Whoever bequeaths more than one third is a harmer, whether he intended it or not, and so the heir may reject that bequest. If he bequeaths one third or less, and it is not known that he intended harm, then it must be carried out.

If the legatee knows that the testator bequeathed out of harm, it is not lawful for him to take it. And if the testator admits that he bequeathed out of harm, it is not permissible to assist in carrying out that bequest.

Allah, glory be to Him, has permitted the nullification of a bequest involving deviation or sin, and permitted the executor (wasi) or another person to reconcile between the heirs and the legatee. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But whoever fears from a testator deviation or sin and reconciles between them, there is no sin upon him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 182].

Likewise, if the judge (hakim) or the executor sees deviation or sin in the endowment (waqf), in its disbursement, or in some of its conditions, and nullifies that, he is a reconciler, not a corrupter.

He may not help the founder (waqif) to carry out deviation and sin, nor may he validate this condition or rule by it, for the Lawgiver has rejected and nullified it.

It is therefore not permissible for him to validate what the Lawgiver has rejected and forbidden, for that is opposition to Him and contradiction of Him.

[Section: The secret of giving priority to the distant agnatic heirs (al-'asabah al-bu'ada') over the uterine relatives (dhawu al-arham), even if they are close]

As for his statement: "The son of a paternal uncle inherits, even if his degree is distant, in preference to the maternal aunt who is a full sister of the mother," then yes, and this is from the perfection and majesty of the Shariah. The son of a paternal uncle is among his 'asabah, those who stand by him in support, allegiance, defence, and bearing the blood-money (al-'aql) on his behalf. So the sons of his father are his protectors, his 'asabah, and those who defend him. As for the kin of the mother, they are in the position of strangers, and they are only related to their fathers. They are in the position of the relatives of daughters, as the poet said:

"Our sons are the sons of our sons, and our daughters' sons are the sons of distant men."

From the perfection of the Lawgiver's wisdom is that He made the inheritance for the paternal relatives, and gave them priority over the maternal relatives. He only let some of the maternal relatives inherit alongside them: those who were conceived with the deceased in the womb of the mother, namely his full siblings, or those whose kinship is very close, namely his grandmothers, because of the strength of their begetting and the closeness of their offspring to him. So when the paternal relatives are absent, the inheritance passes to the maternal relatives, and they have precedence over strangers. This, which the Shariah has brought, is the most complete, most just, and most excellent of things.

The ignorance here is ignorance of action, even if the one who commits the sin knows it is forbidden. Qatadah said: The Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ agreed that whatever is disobeyed through, it is ignorance, whether done deliberately or not, and whoever disobeys God is ignorant.

As for "repentance soon after" (tawbah min qarib), the majority of the exegetes (mufassirun) hold that it means repentance before witnessing (al-mu'ayanah, i.e., seeing the signs of death).

'Ikrimah said: "Before death." al-Dahhak said: "Before witnessing the Angel of Death." al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: "That one repents while still healthy, before the illness of death."

In the Musnad and elsewhere, it is related from Ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Indeed God accepts the repentance of the servant so long as he has not begun the death rattle (yughargir)." In the version of Darraj Abi al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, raised to the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed Satan said: 'By Your might, my Lord, I will not cease to lead Your servants astray as long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord, mighty and majestic, said: 'By My might, My majesty, and the loftiness of My station, I will not cease to forgive them whenever they seek My forgiveness.'"

This is the state of one who repents soon. But if one reaches the death throes (al-siyaq) and says, "Now I repent," his repentance is not accepted, because it is a repentance of compulsion, not of choice. It is like repentance after the sun rises from the west, on the Day of Resurrection, and at the witnessing of God's punishment.

They (the scholars) said: Because the reality of repentance is restraining the self from the act that is the object of the prohibition, and restraint is only possible concerning something within one's power. As for what is impossible, restraint from it is not conceivable. Also, repentance is abandoning sin, and that cannot be imagined from one who is unable to commit it, so that abandoning it could be possible for him.

They said: Also, sin is a firm resolve to do what is forbidden, joined by the act itself, which is within one's power; and repentance from it is a firm resolve to abandon what is within one's power, joined by the abandonment. A resolve concerning what is not within one's power is impossible, and the abandonment in this case is necessary, not a resolve about something beyond one's power. Rather, it is like abandoning flying to the sky, or moving mountains, and the like.

The second opinion, which is the correct one, is that his repentance is valid, possible, and indeed actual, for the pillars of repentance are gathered in him. What is within his power of them is regret. In the Musnad, it is related as a marfu' report: "Regret is repentance." So when his regret for the sin is established, and he blames himself for it, this is repentance. How can repentance be denied him, given the intensity of his regret for the sin and his self-reproach? Especially with what follows from that: his weeping, his sorrow, his fear, his firm resolve, and his intention that, if he were healthy and the act were within his power, he would not commit it.

And since the Lawgiver (al-Shari') has treated the one incapable of obedience as though he were doing it, when his intention is sound, as in His saying in the authentic hadith: "When the servant falls ill or travels, there is recorded for him what he used to do while healthy and resident." And also in the Sahih, from him: "There are people in Medina; you have not journeyed any journey nor crossed any valley except that they were with you." They said: "While they are in Medina?" He said: "While they are in Medina; the excuse has detained them." And there are parallels to this in the hadith. So treating one who is incapable of sin and abstains from it by compulsion, while intending to abstain by choice had he been able, as one who abstains by choice, is more fitting.

This is clarified by the fact that the corruption of sin, which entails the threat of punishment, arises sometimes from the resolve to it and sometimes from doing it. The source of corruption is absent in the case of this incapable person, both in deed and in resolve, and punishment follows corruption.

Also, this person has been prevented from the act just as he has been prevented from wishing and desiring it. So when he wishes and desires that he had committed the sin, and intends that, had he been sound, he would have engaged in it, his repentance consists of giving up this desire and wish, and sorrow over its loss. For persistence (al-israr) is certainly conceivable in his case, so its opposite is conceivable in his case as well, which is repentance. Indeed, it is more possible and conceivable for him than persistence. This is clear.

The difference between this person and the one who witnesses (death) and the one who arrives at the Resurrection is that obligation has ended with the witnessing and with the arrival of the Resurrection, while repentance occurs only within the time of obligation. This incapable person has not been released from obligation: the commands and prohibitions still bind him, and restraint from wishing and desiring it, and from grief over its loss, is conceivable for him, along with replacing that with regret and sorrow over having done it. And God knows best.

(Section)

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "I asked the companions of Muhammad about His saying: ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon God for those who do evil out of ignorance and then repent soon﴾

They said: Everyone who disobeys God is ignorant, and whoever repents before death has repented soon."

Qatadah said: "The companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ agreed that whatever is disobeyed through is ignorance, whether deliberately or not, and whoever disobeys God is ignorant."

Mujahid said: "Whether an elder or a youth, he is in ignorance."

He also said: "Whoever disobeys his Lord is ignorant until he desists from his sin."

He and 'Ata' said: "Ignorance means deliberate sin."

Mujahid also said: "Whoever commits evil, by mistake or deliberately, is ignorant until he desists from it."

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned these reports, then said: It is also related from Qatadah, 'Amr ibn Murrah and al-Thawri something similar: by mistake or deliberately. And it is related from Mujahid and al-Dahhak: "It is not part of his ignorance that he does not know what is lawful or unlawful, but part of his ignorance is when he enters into it."

'Ikrimah said: "All blood (sins) are ignorance." What makes this clear is His saying: ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear God﴾. And whoever fears Him and obeys Him by performing His commands and abstaining from His prohibitions is a knower, as the Exalted said: ﴿Is one who worships devoutly during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾

A man said to al-Sha'bi: "O scholar!" He said: "We are not scholars; the scholar is only one who fears God."

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Fear of God is sufficient as knowledge, and being deceived by God is sufficient as ignorance."

His saying ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear God﴾ implies exclusivity from both sides: none fear Him except the knowledgeable, and none is knowledgeable except one who fears Him. So none fears Him except a knower, and every knower fears Him. When knowledge is absent, fear is absent; and when fear is absent, this indicates the absence of knowledge. But confusion has arisen about the meaning of the knowledge that necessarily accompanies fear, as it is thought that it can be obtained without it. This is impossible, for it is not in human nature that one who knows the Fire, the lion, and the enemy, and faces them, does not fear them, or that one who throws himself from a height does not fear death. His security in these situations is evidence of his lack of knowledge, and at best he has a supposition that does not reach the rank of certain knowledge.

If it is said: This is refuted against you by the disobedience of Iblis, for it was from knowledge, not from ignorance; and by His saying: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾; and He said: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾; and He said of the people of Pharaoh: ﴿They denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾; and He said: ﴿And 'Ad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their dwellings. Satan made their deeds seem fair to them and barred them from the path, though they were discerning﴾; and Musa said to Pharaoh: ﴿He said: You know that none sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as insights﴾; and He said: ﴿And God would not send astray a people after He had guided them until He has made clear to them what they should beware of﴾; and He said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recognize him as they recognize their own sons﴾, meaning the Qur'an or Muhammad ﷺ; and He said: ﴿O People of the Book, why do you mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?﴾; and He said: ﴿Indeed, they do not deny you, but the wrongdoers deny the signs of God﴾. And denial (al-juhud) is rejecting the truth after knowing it, and this is frequent in the Qur'an.

It is said: The proofs of God do not contradict one another; rather, all of them are true, and some confirm others. When He, glory be to Him, has affirmed ignorance for one who commits evil, while that person acknowledges Him, His messenger, and that He has forbidden that, and has threatened punishment for it, and yet he is judged to be in the ignorance that led him to commit evil, then how about one who associates others with Him, disbelieves in His signs, and opposes His messengers? Is that not the most ignorant of the ignorant? God, the Exalted, has indeed called His enemies ignorant after establishing the proof against them, when He said: ﴿Take what is easy, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾. So He commanded him to turn away from them after establishing the proof against them, and they knew he was truthful. And He said: ﴿When the ignorant address them, they say: Peace﴾. So the ignorant here are the disbelievers who knew that he was the Messenger of God. Thus knowledge does not contradict judging its possessor to be ignorant; rather, knowledge is affirmed for him, and negated in one respect, as the Exalted said about the sorcerers among the Jews: ﴿They certainly knew that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter, and wretched is that for which they sold their souls, if only they knew﴾. So He affirmed for them the knowledge by which the proof is established against them, and negated from them the beneficial knowledge that necessitates avoiding harm. This is the crux of the matter and the secret of the answer. No one enters the Fire except one who has knowledge, and no one enters it except one who is ignorant. This knowledge does not combine with ignorance in one person.

It is clarified that heedlessness, aversion, and turning away prevent one from its perfection, from keeping it present, and from knowing its detailed requirements; they establish for its possessor doubts and interpretations that oppose it. So the motivating factor keeps weakening, and the obstructing factor keeps working until it is as if it had never been, and its possessor becomes in every respect like the ignorant. If Iblis had known that abstaining from prostrating to Adam would bring him what it brought him, and that it would bring him the greatest punishment, and had been certain of that, he would not have abstained. But God came between him and this knowledge, so that His decree could be carried out and His destiny executed. And if Adam and Eve had thought that when they ate from the tree they would be expelled from the Garden and that what befell them would befall them, they would not have approached it. And if the enemies of the messengers knew the details of what would happen to them and what would befall them on the Day of Resurrection, and were certain of it, they would not have opposed them. God, the Exalted, said of the people of Pharaoh: ﴿And We had already warned them of Our seizure, but they disputed the warnings﴾. And He said: ﴿And between them and what they desired was placed a barrier, as was done to their likes before; indeed, they were in disquieting doubt﴾. And He said of the hypocrites, who had witnessed the signs of the Messenger and the proofs of his truthfulness with their own eyes: ﴿Their hearts were in doubt, so they wavered in their doubt﴾. And He said: ﴿But you tempted yourselves, waited, and doubted﴾. And He said: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾, which is doubt. And if this were due to the absence of the knowledge by which the proof is established against them, they would not be in the lowest depth of the Fire. Rather, this is after the proof has been established against them and their knowledge, which did not benefit them. So knowledge certainly weakens through heedlessness, aversion, following desire, preferring appetites, and these matters produce doubts and interpretations that oppose it. Reflect deeply upon this point, for it is among the secrets of destiny, law, and justice. Knowledge may refer to complete knowledge that necessarily produces its effect, and it may refer to a motivating factor even if it is not complete for lack of its conditions or the presence of its obstacles. The second can coexist with ignorance, but the first cannot. It has thus become clear that the root of evil deeds is ignorance and the absence of knowledge. And if that is so, the absence of knowledge is not an existent matter; rather, it results from the absence of hearing, sight, power, and will. Absence is not a thing that requires an agent who produces it. It suffices for it that the opposite is not willed and that the cause of the opposite is absent. Pure absence is not attributed to God, for it is an evil, and evil is not attributed to Him. So when this decisive knowledge is absent from the servant, and his self by its nature is moving and willing, and that is among the necessities of its condition, it moves by the inclination of nature and desire, and that inclination prevails over the call of knowledge and recognition, so it falls into causes of evil, inevitably.

The ignorance here is ignorance of action, even if the one who commits the sin knows it is forbidden. Qatadah said: The Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ agreed that whatever is disobeyed through, it is ignorance, whether done deliberately or not, and whoever disobeys God is ignorant.

As for "repentance soon after" (tawbah min qarib), the majority of the exegetes (mufassirun) hold that it means repentance before witnessing (al-mu'ayanah, i.e., seeing the signs of death).

'Ikrimah said: "Before death." al-Dahhak said: "Before witnessing the Angel of Death." al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: "That one repents while still healthy, before the illness of death."

In the Musnad and elsewhere, it is related from Ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Indeed God accepts the repentance of the servant so long as he has not begun the death rattle (yughargir)." In the version of Darraj Abi al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, raised to the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed Satan said: 'By Your might, my Lord, I will not cease to lead Your servants astray as long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord, mighty and majestic, said: 'By My might, My majesty, and the loftiness of My station, I will not cease to forgive them whenever they seek My forgiveness.'"

This is the state of one who repents soon. But if one reaches the death throes (al-siyaq) and says, "Now I repent," his repentance is not accepted, because it is a repentance of compulsion, not of choice. It is like repentance after the sun rises from the west, on the Day of Resurrection, and at the witnessing of God's punishment.

They (the scholars) said: Because the reality of repentance is restraining the self from the act that is the object of the prohibition, and restraint is only possible concerning something within one's power. As for what is impossible, restraint from it is not conceivable. Also, repentance is abandoning sin, and that cannot be imagined from one who is unable to commit it, so that abandoning it could be possible for him.

They said: Also, sin is a firm resolve to do what is forbidden, joined by the act itself, which is within one's power; and repentance from it is a firm resolve to abandon what is within one's power, joined by the abandonment. A resolve concerning what is not within one's power is impossible, and the abandonment in this case is necessary, not a resolve about something beyond one's power. Rather, it is like abandoning flying to the sky, or moving mountains, and the like.

The second opinion, which is the correct one, is that his repentance is valid, possible, and indeed actual, for the pillars of repentance are gathered in him. What is within his power of them is regret. In the Musnad, it is related as a marfu' report: "Regret is repentance." So when his regret for the sin is established, and he blames himself for it, this is repentance. How can repentance be denied him, given the intensity of his regret for the sin and his self-reproach? Especially with what follows from that: his weeping, his sorrow, his fear, his firm resolve, and his intention that, if he were healthy and the act were within his power, he would not commit it.

And since the Lawgiver (al-Shari') has treated the one incapable of obedience as though he were doing it, when his intention is sound, as in His saying in the authentic hadith: "When the servant falls ill or travels, there is recorded for him what he used to do while healthy and resident." And also in the Sahih, from him: "There are people in Medina; you have not journeyed any journey nor crossed any valley except that they were with you." They said: "While they are in Medina?" He said: "While they are in Medina; the excuse has detained them." And there are parallels to this in the hadith. So treating one who is incapable of sin and abstains from it by compulsion, while intending to abstain by choice had he been able, as one who abstains by choice, is more fitting.

This is clarified by the fact that the corruption of sin, which entails the threat of punishment, arises sometimes from the resolve to it and sometimes from doing it. The source of corruption is absent in the case of this incapable person, both in deed and in resolve, and punishment follows corruption.

Also, this person has been prevented from the act just as he has been prevented from wishing and desiring it. So when he wishes and desires that he had committed the sin, and intends that, had he been sound, he would have engaged in it, his repentance consists of giving up this desire and wish, and sorrow over its loss. For persistence (al-israr) is certainly conceivable in his case, so its opposite is conceivable in his case as well, which is repentance. Indeed, it is more possible and conceivable for him than persistence. This is clear.

The difference between this person and the one who witnesses (death) and the one who arrives at the Resurrection is that obligation has ended with the witnessing and with the arrival of the Resurrection, while repentance occurs only within the time of obligation. This incapable person has not been released from obligation: the commands and prohibitions still bind him, and restraint from wishing and desiring it, and from grief over its loss, is conceivable for him, along with replacing that with regret and sorrow over having done it. And God knows best.
