(Excellent benefit)

His Exalted saying: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing while it is good for you, and perhaps you love a thing while it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not.﴾

And His Majestic and Mighty saying: ﴿And if they dislike you, perhaps you dislike a thing while Allah has placed in it much good.﴾ (19)

The first verse concerns jihad, which is the perfection of the irascible power (al-quwwa al-ghadabiyya), and the second concerns marriage, which is the perfection of the appetitive power (al-quwwa al-shahwaniyya). The servant dislikes confronting his enemy with his irascible power, out of fear for himself from it, and this disliked thing is good for him in his livelihood and his hereafter; and he loves truce and disengagement, and this loved thing is bad for him in his livelihood and his hereafter. Likewise, he dislikes a woman because of one of her attributes, while in retaining her there is much good for him that he does not know; and he loves a woman because of one of her attributes, while in retaining her there is much evil for him that he does not know. Man is as his Creator described him: a wrongdoer, ignorant. So it is not fitting that the criterion for what harms and benefits him be his inclination, his love, his aversion and his hatred. Rather, the criterion in this is what Allah has chosen for him through His commands and prohibitions. The most beneficial thing for him, absolutely, is obedience to his Lord outwardly and inwardly, and the most harmful thing for him, absolutely, is disobedience to Him outwardly and inwardly. So when he stands in obedience and servitude to Him, sincerely for Him, then everything that befalls him of what he dislikes becomes good for him; and when he abandons His obedience and servitude, then everything he has of what he loves is evil for him. Whoever has sound knowledge of his Lord and understanding of His names and attributes knows with certainty that the disliked things that befall him and the trials that descend upon him contain kinds of interests and benefits that his knowledge and thought cannot enumerate. Rather, the servant's interest in what he dislikes is greater than in what he loves. For most of the interests of souls lie in what they dislike, just as most of their harms and causes of destruction lie in what they love. Consider the gardener of a garden, expert in cultivation, who planted a garden and tended it with watering and improvement until its trees bore fruit. He then approaches it, cutting its branches and pruning its boughs, because he knows that if it were left as it is, its fruit would not be good. He feeds it from a tree of good fruit. Then, when it has grafted onto it and united with it and given its fruit, he comes with his blade and cuts its weak branches that take away its strength, and makes it taste the pain of cutting and of iron for its benefit and perfection, so that its fruit may be fit to be in the presence of kings. Then he does not leave it to the dictates of its nature for drinking at all times; rather he makes it thirst at times and waters it at times, and does not leave water on it constantly, even though that would be more refreshing to its leaves and faster for its growth. Then he purposefully targets that adornment with which it was adorned by leaves, and casts off much of it, because that adornment comes between its fruit and the completion of its ripening and maturity, as in the case of grape vines and the like. So he cuts its limbs with iron and casts off much of its adornment, and that is the very essence of its benefit. Were it discerning and perceptive like an animal, it would imagine that this is corruption of it and harm to it, when in fact it is the very essence of its benefit.

Likewise, the compassionate father toward his child, who knows his interest: when he sees his interest in drawing out corrupt blood from him, he cuts his skin and severs his veins and makes him taste severe pain; and if he sees healing in amputating one of his limbs, he removes it from him; that is mercy toward him and compassion upon him. And if he sees his interest in withholding giving to him, he does not give him and does not widen provision for him, knowing that this is the greatest cause of his corruption and destruction. Likewise he restrains him from many of his desires out of protectiveness for him and for his benefit, not out of stinginess toward him. So the Most Wise of judges, the Most Merciful of the merciful, and the Most Knowing of the knowing, who is more merciful to His servants than they are to themselves, and than their fathers and mothers are, when He sends down upon them what they dislike, it is better for them than if He did not send it down upon them, out of His consideration for them, His kindness to them and His gentleness toward them. And if they were empowered to choose for themselves, they would be unable to attend to their own interests in knowledge, will and action. But He, glorified be He, has taken charge of their affairs in accordance with the requirement of His knowledge, wisdom and mercy, whether they love it or dislike it. Those who are certain of His names and attributes recognize this, so they do not accuse Him regarding any of His rulings; whereas this is hidden from the ignorant who do not know Him and His names and attributes, so they dispute His management, cast doubt upon His wisdom, do not submit to His judgment, and oppose His judgment with their corrupt intellects, their false opinions and their unjust policies. Thus they have known neither their Lord nor obtained their own interests. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Whenever the servant attains this knowledge, he dwells in this world before the next in a paradise that resembles only the bliss of the Hereafter, for he is never without being content with his Lord. Contentment is the paradise of this world and the resting place of the knowers, for he is content in soul with what befalls him of decrees, which is in fact Allah's choice for him, and his tranquility rests in His religious rulings. This is contentment with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad (ﷺ) as Messenger. Whoever has not attained this has not tasted the flavor of faith. This contentment is in proportion to his knowledge of Allah's justice, wisdom, mercy and good choosing; so the more he knows of that, the more content he is with it. The decree of the Lord, glorified be He, regarding His servant revolves between justice, benefit, wisdom and mercy, and never departs from that at all, as He said in the well-known supplication: "O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your handmaid; my forelock is in Your hand, Your judgment over me is executed, Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every name You have named Yourself with, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You, to make the Qur'an the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the departure of my sorrow and the going of my worry and grief." No one ever said it except that Allah removed his worry and grief and replaced them for him with relief. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not learn them?" He said: "Yes; it is fitting for whoever hears them to learn them."

What is intended is His saying "Your decree concerning me is just." This encompasses every decree He issues upon His servant, of punishment or pain, and its cause. He who decreed the cause and decreed the effect is just in this decree, and this decree is good for the believer, as He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, Allah does not decree for the believer a decree except that it is good for him, and this is not so except for the believer." The scholar Ibn al-Qayyim said: "I asked my Shaykh whether this includes the decree of sin, and he said: 'Yes, with its condition.'" By his phrase "with its condition" he summarized what follows from sin of effects beloved to Allah, such as repentance, humbling oneself, remorse, submission, abasement, weeping, and other such things.

This is an exception whose time-frame concerns the excepted matter, while the time-frame of the excepted-from matter is different, so it is not included in it. Whoever does not require that the exception be included in what is excepted from has nothing to estimate. Whoever says that its inclusion is necessary must estimate its inclusion within the content of the prohibitive imperative clause, because the content of His saying, ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married﴾, is sin and liability to account: that is, whoever marries a woman whom his father married is sinful and accountable, except what had already passed before the prohibition and the establishment of proof, for liability does not attach to it.

Better than this, in my view, is to say: when He, glorified be He, forbade marrying the women whom fathers had married, this indicates that intercourse with them after the prohibition is not a marriage at all, but rather is only fornication (sifah). Therefore the rulings of marriage do not follow from it, such as the establishment of the marital bed (firash) and the attribution of lineage (lahiq al-nasab). Rather, a child born from it is the child of fornication. This is not the ruling for what had passed before the prohibition, for the marital bed was established in that case and the lineage was attributed. Thus the exception conveys a great and magnificent benefit: that the child of one who married what his father had married before the prohibition has established lineage and is not the child of unlawful intercourse. And God knows best.

**Section: The wisdom in distinguishing between the daughter of a brother, the daughter of a paternal uncle, and the like, in marriage**

As for his statement, "He forbade him to marry the daughter of his brother and the daughter of his sister, and permitted him to marry the daughter of his father's brother and the daughter of his mother's sister, and they are equal," the first premise is true and the second is false. They are not equal in reality, nor in custom, nor in intellect, nor in the Sharia. Allah, glory be to Him, has distinguished between the near and the distant in law, in decree, in reason, and in natural disposition. If kinship were equal, there would be no difference between a daughter and the daughter of a maternal aunt or the daughter of a paternal aunt, and this is among the most corrupt of notions. Distant kinship is in the position of strangers, so it is not part of wisdom or benefit to give it the ruling of close kinship. This is something Allah has instilled in sensible people. Whatever contradicts His law in this matter is either a Magian-like practice (*majusiyyah*) that equates the daughter with the mother and with the daughters of paternal uncles and maternal aunts in marrying all of them, or a great hardship upon the servants by forbidding them to marry the daughters of their paternal uncles, paternal aunts, maternal uncles, and maternal aunts. People, especially the Arabs, are mostly cousins to one another, whether the cousin relationship is near or far. If they were prevented from this, it would be a great hardship and constriction upon them. Therefore, what the Sharia brought is the best of matters and the closest to sound reason and upright natural disposition. ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 4, Verse 24 (Part 1 of 2)**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And [forbidden are] married women, except those whom your right hands possess﴾.

This is among the most difficult places of exception (istithna'). If a female slave of his is chaste through marriage (ihsan al-tazwij), she is forbidden to him. The chastity meant here is undoubtedly chastity through marriage, since it cannot mean chastity of purity (ihsan al-'iffah), nor chastity of freedom (ihsan al-hurriyyah), nor chastity of Islam. It is certainly chastity through marriage. So how is she excepted from those forbidden by marriage, namely his slave? Many people said that the exception here is disjunctive (munqati'), and the meaning is: "But those whom your right hands possess, they are lawful for you." This was refuted on the ground that it is an exception from an affirmed statement (mujib), and disjunction occurs only where the sentence is left without a complete object (tafrigh). This refutation was itself refuted, on the ground that disjunction occurs in an affirmed statement and in other than it. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment, except those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾.

Another group said: the exception is in its proper place, continuous (muttasil), and ﴿those whom your right hands possess﴾ is excepted from the married women. Then they differed:

A group of the Companions, among them Ibn 'Abbas and others, and some of the Successors, said: if he marries his female slave and then sells her, her sale is a divorce, and she becomes lawful to her master, because she is his property by right of possession. They argued for this view from the verse.

This view was refuted on several grounds:

First: if it were valid, then her intercourse would be lawful to her master when he has married her, since she is his property by right of possession. Just as her master's ownership and her lawfulness to the husband coexist, so too the ownership of her buyer and her lawfulness to the husband would coexist. The wording applies to both as long as she is married, and what the seller owned passes to the buyer. So the buyer owns her with her sexual usufruct (manfa'at al-bid') removed.

Second: the buyer is the successor (khalifah) of the seller. What the seller owned passed to him by the contract of purchase. The seller owned her body while her sexual usufruct was removed. When her husband separates from her, the sexual usufruct returns to him just as it returned to the seller. This is pure jurisprudence and analogy.

Third: it is established in the two Sahihs that "'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, bought Barirah, who was married, and she freed her, and the Prophet (ﷺ) (ﷺ) gave her the choice." This is related by al-Bukhari. Had the marriage been annulled by the purchase, he would not have given her the choice. This is one of the matters on which the four Imams and others relied on the narration of Ibn 'Abbas, and they abandoned his opinion, although he was the narrator of the hadith and he was among those who held that the sale of a slave-girl is her divorce.

Another group said: the verse is specific to captives (sabaya). Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: "It was revealed concerning the captives of Awtas." They said: Allah, the Exalted, permitted the Muslims to have intercourse with those they possess from among the captives, even if they are chaste.

Then these differed as to when intercourse with a captive woman is permitted.

Al-Shafi'i, Abu al-Khattab and others said: her intercourse is permitted once her istibra' (establishing that she is not pregnant) is complete, whether her husband is present or absent. They argued with three proofs:

The first: Allah, glory be to Him, permitted intercourse with captives by right of possession, excepting them from the chaste women.

The second: what Muslim related in his Sahih from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: "The Messenger of Allah sent an army to Awtas. They met an enemy, fought them, prevailed over them, and took captives. Some of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) seemed to refrain from intercourse with them because of their husbands among the polytheists. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning this: ﴿And [forbidden are] married women, except those whom your right hands possess﴾." That is, "they are lawful to you once their waiting period is over." And in al-Tirmidhi, from Abu Sa'id: "We took captives on the day of Awtas who had husbands among their people. They mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this was revealed: ﴿And [forbidden are] married women, except those whom your right hands possess﴾." This is explicit in permitting them even if they have husbands. In al-Tirmidhi and the Musnad of Ahmad, from the hadith of al-'Irbad ibn Sariyah: "The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade intercourse with captives until they give birth to what is in their wombs." This prohibition is limited by an endpoint, which is the delivery of the child, so the lawfulness must occur after that endpoint. Had the existence of their husbands been a barrier to intercourse, the prohibition would have had two endpoints: the absence of the husband, and the delivery of the child. This contradicts the apparent meaning of the hadith.

They also said: the disbelieving combatant's ownership of the sexual usufruct has no sanctity or bond left, since the Muslims have acquired over him what he owned, and they own his wife's person. How can it be said that the bond remains in the ownership of the sexual usufruct, especially since the Muslims are entitled to own his person, his children and all his property? Why should the ownership of the sexual usufruct alone remain bound? This has neither textual proof, nor analogy, nor meaning.

They said: the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted intercourse with captives after their waiting period without restriction. Had the continuing existence of the husband been a barrier, he would not have permitted intercourse with them except after knowing of the husband's death. As you see, this view is strong and sound.

Our companions, the qadi and others, said: intercourse is permitted only if she is captured alone. If she is captured together with her husband, they remain married, and intercourse is not permitted. They said: if she is captured alone, the husband's survival is unknown, and the unknown is like the non-existent, so she is treated as one who has no husband, and intercourse with her is lawful. This is not the case when her husband is with her.

Then they raised an objection against themselves: what if she is captured alone and it is known that her husband remains in the territory of war? This is a question from which they have no escape, and nothing saves them from it except saying that it is lawful, even if the husband's survival is known, on the basis that the marriage bond is removed by capture. For if they answer by committing to prohibition, they clearly contradict the texts. If they answer by permitting it while affirming the husband's survival, they undermine their own principle, since they attributed lawfulness to the captive's being free of a husband, treating the unknown as the non-existent. Thus the view of Abu al-Khattab is more jurisprudentially sound and more correct, and the verse and the hadiths are to be understood in accordance with it. This shows that the exception is continuous, and that Allah, the Exalted, permitted from among the chaste women those whom the Muslims captured.

If it is said: according to what you have established, chastity is removed by capture, so they do not enter among the chaste women, and thus the exception becomes disjunctive?

It is said: since she was chaste before capture, it is correct that the term includes her, so the exception removes her.

If it is said: what do you say about the married slave-girl who is sold while chaste, having owned herself? Is she specifically excluded from this general statement, or does she not enter it?

It is said: there are two approaches among people here.

One: she is excluded from the general statement by the evidences that a sale does not annul a marriage, and that a private part cannot be lawful to two persons at the same time.

The second approach: she does not enter the thing excepted from, because when her master marries her, he has removed the sexual usufruct from his ownership. When he sells her, what the seller had passes to the buyer, so the buyer owns her with the sexual usufruct removed. This usufruct did not enter his ownership by the contract of sale, so the verse does not cover it. This approach is more subtle and more precise than the first, and Allah knows best.

[Section: When the temporary marriage (mut'ah) of women was forbidden]

Among the events of this raid (ghazwah) was the permission of temporary marriage (mut'at al-nisa') for women, and then its prohibition before his departure from Makkah. Scholars differed about the time when mut'ah was forbidden, giving four opinions:

The first: it was on the day of Khaybar. This is the view of a group of scholars, among them al-Shafi'i and others.

The second: it was in the year of the Conquest of Makkah. This is the view of Ibn 'Uyaynah and a group.

The third: it was in the year of Hunayn. In reality this is the second view, because the raid of Hunayn is connected to the Conquest.

The fourth: it was in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage. This is an error by some narrators, whose error travelled from the Conquest of Makkah to the Farewell Pilgrimage, just as the error of Mu'awiyah travelled from the 'umrah of al-Ji'ranah to the Farewell Pilgrimage, when he said: "I shortened the hair of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a sharp instrument at al-Marwah in his pilgrimage," which has been mentioned in the chapter on Hajj. The travelling of an error from one time to another, from one place to another, and from one event to another, often occurs to the memorizers (huffaz) and those below them.

The correct view is that mut'ah was forbidden only in the year of the Conquest, because it is established in Sahih Muslim that they enjoyed mut'ah in the year of the Conquest with the Prophet (ﷺ) by his permission. Had the prohibition been at the time of Khaybar, the abrogation would have occurred twice, and no such thing has ever been known in the Shari'ah, nor does its like occur in it. Also: Khaybar had no Muslim women; they were Jewish women. The permission of the women of the People of the Book had not yet been established. They were permitted only afterward, in Surah al-Ma'idah, by His saying: ﴿This day the good things have been made lawful for you, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them; and [lawful are] chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 5]. This is connected to His saying: ﴿This day I have perfected for you your religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3], and to His saying: ﴿This day those who disbelieved have despaired of your religion﴾. This was at the end of the matter, after the Farewell Pilgrimage or during it. So the permission of the women of the People of the Book was not established at the time of Khaybar, nor did the Muslims have desire for enjoying the women of their enemy before the Conquest. After the Conquest, whoever was enslaved among them was enslaved, and they became slave-girls to the Muslims.

If it is said: what do you do with what is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade mut'ah of women on the day of Khaybar, and the eating of the flesh of domestic donkeys," and this is sound and explicit?

It is said: this hadith has been soundly related in two wordings. This is one of them. The second: restricting the report to the Prophet's (ﷺ) prohibition of the marriage of mut'ah and the flesh of domestic donkeys on the day of Khaybar. This is the narration of Ibn 'Uyaynah from al-Zuhri. Qasim ibn Asbagh said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: he means that he forbade the flesh of domestic donkeys at the time of Khaybar, not the marriage of mut'ah. Abu 'Umar mentioned this, and in al-Tamhid he said: "Then most people said this." Thus some narrators assumed that "the day of Khaybar" was the time frame for both prohibitions, so they related it as: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade mut'ah and domestic donkeys at the time of Khaybar." Some related only part of the hadith and said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade mut'ah at the time of Khaybar," and this is a clear error.

If it is said: what is the benefit of combining the two prohibitions if they did not occur at the same time, and where is mut'ah in relation to the prohibition of donkeys?

It is said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, related this hadith as evidence against his cousin 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas concerning both matters, for he used to permit mut'ah and the flesh of donkeys. 'Ali debated him on both matters, related both prohibitions to him, restricted the prohibition of donkeys to the time of Khaybar, and left the prohibition of mut'ah unrestricted, saying: "You are a wanderer (ta'ih). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade mut'ah and forbade the flesh of domestic donkeys on the day of Khaybar," as Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said, and as most people hold. So he related both matters, using them as evidence against him, not restricting them to the day of Khaybar. And Allah is the Granter of success.

But here there is another consideration: did He forbid it with the prohibition of indecencies (fawahish) which are never permitted in any circumstance, or did He forbid it when one can do without it, and permit it for the one under necessity? This is what Ibn 'Abbas considered, and he said: "I permitted it only for one under necessity, like carrion and blood." When some people extended its permission and did not stop at necessity, Ibn 'Abbas refrained from issuing fatwas permitting it, and retracted. Ibn Mas'ud used to hold its permission, and he would recite: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 87].

In the two Sahihs, from him, he said: "We used to fight with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and we had no women, so we said: shall we not castrate ourselves? He forbade us, then he permitted us to marry a woman with a garment for a fixed term." Then 'Abd Allah recited: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress; indeed, Allah does not love transgressors﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 87].

'Abd Allah's recitation of this verse immediately after this hadith admits of two matters:

One: a rebuttal of those who forbid it, meaning that if it were not among the good things, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not have permitted it.

The second: that he intended the end of this verse, which is a rebuttal of those who permit it absolutely, and that such a person is a transgressor. For the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only granted a concession regarding it for necessity, during raids, when women are absent, and when there is strong need for a woman. Whoever permits it in settled life, while women are plentiful and the customary marriage is possible, has transgressed, and Allah does not love transgressors.

If it is said: what do you do with what Muslim related in his Sahih from the hadith of Jabir and Salamah ibn al-Akwa', who both said: "The herald of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us and said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has permitted you to enjoy' — meaning the mut'ah of women"?

It is said: this was at the time of the Conquest, before the prohibition, and then he forbade it after that, as evidenced by what Muslim related in his Sahih from Salamah ibn al-Akwa': "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) granted us a concession in mut'ah for three days in the year of Awtas, and then he forbade it." The year of Awtas is the year of the Conquest, because the raid of Awtas is connected to the Conquest of Makkah.

If it is said: what do you do with what Muslim related in his Sahih from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "We used to enjoy a handful of dates and flour during the days of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr, until 'Umar forbade it concerning the matter of 'Amr ibn Huraith"; and what is established from 'Umar, that he said: "There were two mut'ahs during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I forbid them: the mut'ah of women and the mut'ah of Hajj"?

It is said: People on this matter are of two groups. One group says: It was Umar who prohibited it and forbade it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded following what the Rightly-Guided Caliphs (al-Khulafa' al-Rashidun) established. This group did not find the hadith of Sabra ibn Ma'bad concerning the prohibition of temporary marriage (al-mut'ah) on the Conquest day to be authentic, for it comes through the narration of Abd al-Malik ibn al-Rabi' ibn Sabra from his father from his grandfather, and Ibn Ma'in has spoken about it. Al-Bukhari did not consider it appropriate to include a hadith in his Sahih despite the great need for it and its being a foundation of the religion. Had it been authentic according to him, he would not have refrained from narrating it and citing it. They said: Even if the hadith of Sabra were authentic, it would not have been hidden from Ibn Mas'ud, so that he would narrate that they practiced it, and would cite the verse. Also, even if it were authentic, Umar would not have said: "It was during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I forbid it and punish for it," but rather he would have said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prohibited it and forbade it." They said: Even if it were authentic, it would not have been practiced during the time of Abu Bakr, which was truly the era of the Prophethood's Caliphate.

The second group: They regarded the hadith of Sabra as authentic, and even if it were not, the hadith of Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) is authentic that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "prohibited the mut'ah of women." Therefore, it is necessary to interpret the hadith of Jabir as meaning that the one who reported its practice had not reached the knowledge of its prohibition, and it had not become widely known until the time of Umar (may Allah be pleased with him). When disputes arose over it, its prohibition became apparent and widely known. By this, the hadiths related on this subject are reconciled. And success is from Allah.

[Section: God made the slave and the free person equal in some rulings and differentiated between them in others]

As for his statement: "He made the legal penalty for the slave half that of the free person, though their need for deterrence is the same," there is no doubt that the Lawgiver (al-Shari') differentiated between the free person and the slave in some rulings and made them equal in others. He made them equal in faith (iman) and submission (Islam), and in the obligation of bodily acts of worship such as purification (taharah), prayer (salah) and fasting (sawm), because they are equal in their cause. He differentiated between them in financial acts of worship such as the pilgrimage (hajj), zakat, and expiation by means of wealth, because their causes differ.

As for the hudud (prescribed penalties), since committing a sin is more heinous when done by a free person than when done by a slave, for two reasons: first, the completeness of God's blessing upon him through freedom, and that He made him an owner and not owned, and did not place him under the subjugation and disposal of another; and second, his ability, through the means of power, to refrain from sin by means of the permissible things God has given in its place. He thus repaid the complete blessing with its opposite, and used his power for disobedience, and so he deserves a greater punishment than one who is lower in rank and station. For a man, whenever God's blessing upon him is complete, his punishment when he commits crimes is more complete. Therefore God, Exalted, said concerning those of the women upon whom He had completed His blessing: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold, and that is ever easy for God﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30] ﴿And whoever of you is devoutly obedient to God and His Messenger and does righteousness, We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾ [al-Ahzab: 31]. This accords with the judgments and approvals of reason: whenever God's blessing upon a servant is complete, it is fitting that his obedience to Him be more complete, his gratitude more perfect, and his disobedience more heinous, and the severity of the punishment follows the ugliness of the sin. For this reason, the people who will suffer the greatest punishment on the Day of Resurrection is a scholar whom God did not benefit by his knowledge, for God's blessing upon him through knowledge is greater than His blessing upon the ignorant, and his committing sin is more heinous than the ignorant person's committing it. Kings and chiefs do not treat equally one who disobeys them from among their close associates, attendants and those near to them, and one who disobeys them from among the distant provinces and remote people. So He made the penalty for the slave lighter than that of the free person, combining the wisdom of deterrence with the wisdom of his deficiency. For this reason, his share is half in marriage, divorce and the waiting period ('iddah), to manifest the honor and worth of freedom, and to give each rank its right in the command just as He gave it its right in the decree. This wisdom is not invalidated by giving the slave two rewards in the Hereafter; rather, this is the pure essence of wisdom, for the slave had in the world two rights, a right of God and a right of his master, so for his fulfilment of each right he is given a reward in return. Thus the wisdom of the Shari'ah, the decree and the recompense are in harmony. And praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.

[Section: God's wisdom in differentiating between the free woman and the slave-woman regarding a man's chastity (ihsan)]

As for his statement: "He made the ugly, disfigured free woman sufficient to make a man chaste (muhsin), while the beautiful slave-woman does not make him chaste," this is a poor expression of a correct meaning. The wisdom of the Lawgiver required that the penalty for fornication (zina) be obligatory upon one on whom God's blessing has been completed through what is lawful, so that he transgresses to what is unlawful. For this reason, He did not impose the full penalty upon one who is not muhsan, and He took as the criterion of ihsan its most complete state, which is that he marry a free woman whom people desire the like of, not a slave-woman whom God has permitted to marry only in cases of necessity; the blessing through her is not complete. Nor does it refer to concubinage (tasarri), which is in rank below marriage; for a slave-woman, even if she is what she may be, does not reach the rank of a wife, neither in the Shari'ah, nor by custom, nor by habit. Rather, God has given each of the two a rank, and the slave-woman is not sought for what a wife is sought for. For this reason, he may own those whom it is not permitted for him to marry, and there is no rotation (qasm) owed to them in his ownership, so his slave-woman is treated in terms of service, humiliation and use in the manner of his beast or his servant, unlike free women. And it is among the excellences of the Shari'ah that, regarding the completion of blessing upon one who is liable to the hadd, it has taken into account that he has contracted marriage with a free woman and consummated it, for by that he fulfils the completeness of his need and gives his desire its due and places it in its proper place. This is the principle and the origin of the wisdom.

It is not required of every single individual among the muhsanin, and his deviation in many cases does no harm, since the nature of universal laws is to take account of general, regulated matters, and the deviation of wisdom in particular instances does not invalidate them, just as is the nature of creation. This is what necessitates the wisdom of God in His creation and His command, in His decree and His legislation. And success is from God.

[Section: Marrying a slave-woman who is a People of the Book]

If it is said: If His statement "And chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you" (al-Ma'idah: 5) means chastity (iffah) and not the chastity of freedom, then from where do you derive the prohibition of marrying a slave-woman who is a People of the Book?

It is said: The answer is in two respects:

The first: The prohibition of marrying a slave-woman who is a People of the Book has not been established as an ijma' (consensus). Abu Hanifah permits it, and Ahmad said in the narration of Ibn al-Qasim: "The disapproval (karahah) regarding the slave-women of the People of the Book is not a strong one; it is only something that al-Hasan and Mujahid interpreted." This is his wording.

From his own wording this is almost explicit that it is not prohibited, and at least it indicates that he refrained from prohibiting it. But al-Khallal said: Ahmad's hesitation in the narration of Ibn al-Qasim does not override the view of one who decided definitively. More than twenty persons have narrated from him this issue, that it is not permitted.

So the matter is therefore one of disagreement, and proof decides between those who disagree.

Those who permit said: God, Exalted, said: ﴿So marry what is good for you of women﴾ [al-Nisa': 3]. So if a slave-woman who is a People of the Book is good for him, then He has permitted him to marry her. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿And lawful to you is what is beyond that﴾ [al-Nisa': 24], and did not mention a slave-woman who is a People of the Book among the forbidden ones. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿And marry the single among you and the righteous of your male and female slaves﴾ [al-Nur: 32]. The meaning of "the righteous" is one who is fit for marriage; this is the more correct of the two interpretations. Another group held it means "faith", but the first is more correct, for God, glory be to Him, did not command them to marry off only the righteous and the religious among their male and female slaves, just as He did not single them out for the obligation of maintaining them. Rather, it is obligatory upon the master to provide chastity for his male and female slave just as it is obligatory upon him to maintain them, for that is part of their welfare and their rights upon their master. He has therefore issued the command to marry off slave-women absolutely, whether they are Muslims or disbelievers, and did not forbid marrying a disbelieving slave-woman to a Muslim.

They said: And He has said: ﴿And a believing slave-woman is better than a polytheist, even if she pleases you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 221]. This indicates the permissibility of marrying both types, and that this is better than that.

They said: And God, glory be to Him, has permitted intercourse with them through right of possession (milk al-yamin); so likewise intercourse with them should be permitted through the contract of marriage. And the reverse, the Magian and idolatrous women, is not permitted.

They said: So every category whose free women may be married may have its slave-women married, like Muslim women.

They said: And because it is permitted to marry her after her manumission, so it is permitted to marry her before it, like a Muslim slave-woman.

They said: And because it is permissible for a dhimmi to marry her, so it is permissible for a Muslim to marry her, like a free Scripturary woman; and the reverse, an idolatrous woman, is not.

They said: And because her slaughtered animal is permitted, so her marriage is permitted, like a free woman.

Those who prohibit said: God, Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾ [al-Nisa': 25]. Thus God permitted marrying a slave-woman under three conditions:

The first: inability to afford marriage to a free woman (tawl).

The second: the slave-woman being married is a believer.

The third: fear of committing sin (al-'anat).

The permission is not established without these three conditions, because the private part was unlawful before that, and it was permitted only in this way and under this condition. So when that is absent, it remains on the original prohibition.

Those who permit said: At most this is a conditional implication (mafhum al-shart), and implication is not evidence according to us.

Those who prohibit said: We grant you that implication is not evidence, but the original ruling regarding private parts is prohibition, and nothing from them is permitted except what God and His Messenger have permitted. God, glory be to Him, only permitted marrying a believing slave-woman, so the rest remain on the original prohibition. Moreover, if faith were not a condition for permissibility, there would be no benefit in mentioning it; it would be an addition to the wording and a deficiency in meaning, and a suggestion that permissibility is restricted to some of its objects. The speech of the wise, let alone the speech of the Lord of earth and heaven, is protected from this. It is clarified by the fact that the attribute of faith is an intended attribute, so linking the ruling to it indicates that it is the cause (illah) of its establishment. Had the attributes to which rulings are linked been disregarded, the Shari'ah would be corrupted, as in His statement: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ [al-Nur: 4], and His statement: ﴿And chaste women from among women﴾ [al-Nisa': 24], and their like are more than can be enumerated.

Those who permit said: You cannot derive proof from the verse, for God, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then from what your right hands possess﴾ [al-Nisa': 25]. He did not permit marrying a slave-woman except when one cannot afford to marry a free believing woman. And you said: It is not permitted for him to marry a slave-woman if he is able to marry a free Scripturary woman. So you disregarded the attribute of faith in the original, so how do you deny it to one who disregards it in the substitute?

Those who prohibit said, and the wording is that of Abu Ya'la: Were we to leave the text to its apparent meaning, we would say: the faith of the chaste women is a condition, but the consensus established abandoning it, and no proof has established abandoning its condition regarding the young women.

I say: There is no consensus regarding the slave-woman, and it is not agreed that faith is not a condition for the chaste women. Rather, one of the two opinions of the Shafi'is is that if one is able to marry a free Scripturary woman but not a free Muslim woman, then he may move to a slave-woman. This is a strong view, and the apparent meaning of the Qur'an requires it. It may also be said that the verse of al-Nisa' precedes the verse of al-Ma'idah in which the chaste women from among the People of the Book are permitted. God, Exalted, said: ﴿This day the good things are made lawful for you, and the food of those given the Book is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them, and chaste women from among the believing women and chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 5]. At that point the marrying of Scripturary women was permitted.

Those who prohibit said: God, Exalted, said: ﴿And chaste women from among those who were given the Book﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 5], and ihsan here means the ihsan of freedom.

Qadi Isma'il said in "Ahkam al-Qur'an": "Ihsan applies to chastity and applies to freedom, and by this context only freedom is meant, for if chastity were meant it would not be permissible for a Muslim to marry a Christian or Jewish woman until he established her chastity, nor would it be permissible for him, by this verse, to marry a Muslim woman until he established her chastity, since the word came in both places with one meaning. It is known that they are free believing women, and the free women are the People of the Book, because God, Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾ [al-Nisa': 25]."

And 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: Ibn Abi Najih informed us, from Mujahid: It is not lawful to marry the slave-women of the People of the Book, because God, Exalted, said: ﴿From your believing young women﴾ [al-Nisa': 25].

'Ali narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Yunus narrated to us: al-Hasan used to dislike marrying a Jewish or Christian slave-woman, and said: God only granted leniency regarding the Muslim slave-woman, as He said: ﴿From your believing young women﴾ [al-Nisa': 25]. Then he mentioned the prohibition of marrying a Scripturary slave-woman from Ibrahim, Makhul, Qatadah, Yahya ibn Sa'id, and from the seven jurists.

And the highest-ranking narration on this from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.

"The judge (al-Qadi) said: 'Ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, Ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Abu al-Zubayr who said: I asked Jabir about a man who has a Muslim slave and a Christian slave-girl; may he marry her to him? He said: No.'"

Those who permit said: People have not agreed that ihsan (chastity, marital protection) here means ihsan of freedom (hurriyyah).

Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated from Mutarrif, from Amir, regarding ﴿And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 5], that he said: "When she guards her private part and performs ghusl from janabah."

It is authentically reported from Mujahid regarding ﴿And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 5] that he said: "They are the chaste ones (al-afaif)."

They said: "Even if you were challenged to produce a single passage of the Qur'an in which ihsan is intended to mean freedom and which does not suit any other meaning, you would not find a way to it. What the Qur'an has consistently used this word to mean is two things: chastity ('iffah) and marriage (tazwij). As for Islam and freedom, neither of them has been specified by the wording."

As for your statement that if it meant chastity, marriage to a woman of the Scripture, or to a Muslim woman, would not be permissible except after her chastity is established, then this is what the Book and the Sunnah indicate in more than one place.

Among the excellences of the Shari'ah is the prohibition of marrying prostitutes (al-baghaya), for it is among the most abominable matters. When people wish to shame a man, they say: "Husband of a prostitute." This is a natural disposition (fitrah) upon which God created creation, so no Shari'ah comes to permit it.

The prostitute is a corrupt (khabitha) woman, and God, glorified is He, prohibited the corrupt things in marriage just as He prohibited them in food. He did not permit marrying a woman except on condition of her chastity, and He said regarding marrying adulteresses: ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾ [al-Nur: 3]. Nothing has abrogated this verse (naskh). For marrying a free woman it is sufficient that her fornication is not publicly known, since the original state is her chastity; her chastity is established by default, so requiring it is not burdensome. When her fornication becomes publicly known, marrying her becomes forbidden. If she repents, then one who repents from a sin is like one who has no sin.

As for what you have cited from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, and the Tabi'in regarding prohibition, others have opposed them.

Ibn Abi Shayba said: Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from Mughira, from Abu Maysara who said: "The slave-girls of the People of the Book have the same status as their free women."

Those who prohibit said: As for your analogy of marrying a Scripturist slave-girl to having intercourse with her, it is a very corrupt analogy. For the one who has intercourse with a slave-girl by right of ownership (milk al-yamin) has a child born free and Muslim, so intercourse with a disbelieving slave-girl by right of ownership does no harm. But one who has intercourse with a slave-girl by marriage contract has a child born enslaved to the owner of the slave-girl, and in that there is a causing of the establishment of a disbeliever's ownership over a Muslim. Thus the two differ.

For this reason, intercourse with a Muslim slave-girl by right of ownership is permitted, but intercourse with her by marriage contract is not permitted except in cases of necessity, upon the existence of the two conditions. What is established by necessity is limited to its measure and may not be extended beyond it. The necessity ceases with marrying a Muslim slave-girl, so it is restricted to that, just as permission to eat carrion and pork is restricted to the measure of necessity.

Those who permit said: This is refuted against you by the case where the disbelieving slave-girl is elderly and of an age when such a woman does not bear children, or where she belongs to a Muslim, for then no disbeliever's ownership is established over the child.

Those who prohibit said: Does not permissibility lead to this in the case where the slave-girl belongs to a disbeliever and is of an age to bear children? No one has made a distinction; rather there are two positions: one permitting absolutely, and one prohibiting absolutely. When the Lawgiver prohibits something because of a feared corruption (mafsada) arising from it, he closes the door to that corruption entirely. For this reason, when he prohibited marrying a slave-girl except when one lacks the means (tawl) and fears sinning (khashyat al-'anat), out of concern for enslaving the child, he did not permit marrying a barren woman who does not bear or give birth without both conditions.

They said: As for your statement, "It is not permissible to marry her after manumission, so it was permissible before it," its essence is analogy of the Scripturist slave-girl to the free woman, and this is an invalid analogy because of the known difference.

As for your statement, "It is permissible for a disbeliever to marry her, so it is permissible for a Muslim," whoever rejects analogy: the Magian woman may be married by a Magian, but may not be married by a Muslim, and wine and pork are property (mal) in their view but not in the view of Muslims.

As for your analogy of the permissibility of marriage to the permissibility of slaughtered animals, it is an invalid analogy, for slavery has no effect on slaughter but has an effect on marriage.

They said: As for His statement, exalted is He, ﴿So marry what is good for you of women﴾ [al-Nisa: 3], what is meant by it is what is lawful and permitted. He, glorified is He, permitted only three categories of women: free Muslim women, free Scripturist women, and Muslim slave-girls. The Scripturist slave-girls remained without permission, so they remain on the original basis of prohibition.

And when He permitted intercourse with them by right of ownership, we said it is permitted.

As for His statement, exalted is He, ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾ [al-Nisa: 24], the verse contains what indicates prohibition, namely His statement: ﴿chaste, not fornicating﴾ [al-Nisa: 24], i.e., not adulterers.

Marrying one whom Allah has not permitted to be married is unlawful and void, and thus it would be fornication (zina). Moreover, it is a general text (amm) specified by consensus (ijma'), and whoever is a general text that has been specified, some people do not take it as evidence, while most hold it as evidence; yet when specification enters it, its force weakens.

It has also been said: the specification is by implication (mafhum), by analogy (qiyas), by the statement of a Companion (qawl al-sahabi), and other things.

As for His statement, exalted is He, ﴿And a believing slave-girl is better than a polytheist﴾ [al-Baqara: 221], whoever uses it as evidence has gone very far astray, and it is closer to being evidence against him.

They said: The wisdom of the Shari'ah requires its prohibition, because two deficiencies are combined in her: deficiency of religion and deficiency of slavery. This contrasts with the Scripturist free woman and the Muslim slave-girl, for one of the two deficiencies is compensated by the absence of the other.

They also said: The principle of equality in suitability (kafa'a) would require that the woman be a match for the man just as the man is a match for her. But since men are guardians over women (qawwamun 'ala al-nisa') and women are, in their view, 'awan (captives under men's authority), suitability was not required for women to be matched to men, and a man may marry one who is not his equal, due to his need for that. However, when she lacks the attributes of suitability altogether, such that no single attribute of religion, freedom, or chastity is found in her, the excellences of the Shari'ah require protecting him from her by prohibiting her to him. This is the furthest that can be said on this question, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verses 26–28:

After mentioning what has been made lawful to us of women and what has been made unlawful of them, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you and to guide you to the ways of those before you, and to turn to you in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. And Allah desires to turn to you in forgiveness, while those who follow desires want you to deviate into a tremendous deviation. Allah desires to lighten for you [your burdens], and mankind was created weak.﴾ [al-Nisa': 26–28].

Sufyan al-Thawri mentioned in his tafsir, from Ibn Tawus, from his father: "Whenever he (Tawus) looked at women, he could not be patient."

In the Sahih, from the hadith of Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that "he saw a woman, so he went to Zaynab and fulfilled his need with her, and said: 'Indeed the woman approaches in the form of a devil and withdraws in the form of a devil. So when one of you sees a woman and she pleases him, let him go to his wife, for that will repel what is in his soul.'" In this hadith there are several benefits:

Among them: guidance to consoling oneself regarding the desired thing with its like, just as food takes the place of food and clothing the place of clothing.

And among them: the command to treat the infatuation with a woman, which inherits desire for her, with the most beneficial of remedies, which is fulfilling one's need with one's own wife. That breaks his desire for her. This is just as he guided those who love each other to marriage, as in the Sunan of Ibn Majah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Nothing has been seen for those who love one another like marriage."

So marrying the beloved is the remedy for passionate love, which Allah made a legislated remedy. Dawud (peace be upon him) treated himself with it, and the Prophet of Allah did not commit a prohibited act; he married the woman and included her among his wives because of his love for her, and his repentance was in accordance with his station with Allah and the loftiness of his rank. It does not befit us to add more to this.

As for the story of Zaynab bint Jahsh: Zayd had resolved to divorce her and she did not agree with him, and he kept consulting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about separating from her, while he was instructing him to keep her. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knew that he would certainly separate from her, so he concealed in himself that he would marry her once Zayd divorced her, and he feared the people's saying: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married his son's wife," for he had adopted Zayd before prophethood. The Lord, the Exalted, wanted to legislate a general law containing the interests of His servants. When Zayd divorced her and her waiting period ended, he sent someone to propose to her on his own behalf. Zayd came and turned his back to the door, and what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had mentioned about her grew great in his heart, so he called to her from behind the door: "O Zaynab, indeed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposes to you." She said: "I will not do anything until I consult my Lord," and she stood at her prayer niche and prayed. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Himself arranged her marriage to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and concluded the marriage for him above His Throne, and the revelation came with that: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then immediately rose and entered upon her. She used to boast over the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) about this, saying: "Your guardians married you off, but Allah married me from above seven heavens." This is the story of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with Zaynab.

There is no doubt that the Prophet (ﷺ) had women made beloved to him, as in the Sahih from Anas, from him (ﷺ): "Women and perfume have been made beloved to me from your world, and the coolness of my eyes has been placed in prayer." This is the wording of the hadith, not what some of them narrate: "Three things have been made beloved to me from your world," which Imam Ahmad added in the Kitab al-Zuhd to this hadith: "I am patient with food and drink, but I am not patient with them." The enemies of Allah, the Jews, envied him for this and said: "His only concern is marriage." So Allah, glorified is He, rejected this about His Messenger (ﷺ) and defended him, saying: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? Indeed, We gave the family of Ibrahim the Scripture and wisdom and gave them a great kingdom﴾ [al-Nisa': 54].

This is the Friend of Allah, Ibrahim, who had with him Sarah, the most beautiful of the women of the worlds, and he loved Hajar and took her as a concubine.

This is Dawud (peace be upon him), who had ninety-nine women, then he loved that woman and married her, thus completing the hundred. And this is his son Sulayman (peace be upon him), who used to go around in one night to ninety women.

"The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the person most beloved to him, and he said: 'Aisha' (may Allah be pleased with her), and he said regarding Khadijah: 'I have been provided with her love.'"

So love of women is among the perfections of humanity. Ibn Abbas said: "The best of this Ummah is the one with the most wives." Imam Ahmad mentioned that Abdullah ibn Umar, on the day of Jalula', had fallen to his share a slave-girl whose neck was like a silver ewer. Abdullah said: "I could not be patient with her, so I kissed her while the people were looking." By this Imam Ahmad argued for the permissibility of enjoying a captive woman before her istibra' (purification period) without intercourse, unlike a purchased slave-girl.

The difference between them is that the termination of ownership is not presumed in the case of a captive, unlike the purchased one, for in her case ownership may be terminated, so he would be enjoying the slave-girl of another.

The Prophet (ﷺ) also interceded for a lover that his beloved should join him by marrying him, but she refused. This was in the story of Mughith and Barirah: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him walking behind her with tears flowing down his cheeks, he said to her: 'If only you would return to him?' She said: 'Are you ordering me, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No, I am only interceding.' She said: 'I have no need for him.' Then he said to his uncle: 'O Abbas, are you not amazed at Mughith's love for Barirah, and her hatred for him?' and he did not object to his love for her, even though she had separated from him."

The Prophet (ﷺ) used to treat his wives equally in the division, and he would say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what I do not possess," meaning in love. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ [al-Nisa': 129], meaning in love and intercourse.

The rightly-guided caliphs and compassionate people among mankind continued to intercede for lovers with their beloved whose union is permissible, as previously mentioned regarding the actions of Abu Bakr and Uthman. Likewise Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) was brought a young Arab man who had been found in a people's house at night. He said to him: "What is your story?" He said: "I am not a thief, but I will tell you the truth:"

I became attached in the house of al-Riyahi to a fair maiden, before whose beauty the full moon humbles itself,

Among the daughters of Rome she has beauty and a form; when she boasts of her beauty, the pride of others is frightened of her.

When I came to the house from the heat of my heart, I stayed the night while in her the embers of her burning were ablaze,

The people of the house hurried at me, then cried out: "He is the thief, for whom death or capture is decreed."

When Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) heard his poetry, he was moved, and said to al-Muhallab ibn Rabah: "Allow him to have her." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, ask him who he is." He said: "Al-Nahhas ibn Uyaynah." He said: "Take her, for she is yours."

Mu'awiyah bought a slave-girl and was greatly infatuated with her. One day he heard her reciting verses of hers:

And I parted from him like a branch swaying in the dust, fresh and handsome after his moustache had sprouted.

He asked her, and she informed him that she loved her master. So he returned her to him, and in his heart there remained something of her.

Al-Zamakhshari mentioned concerning Rabi'ah that Zubaydah read on a wall on the road to Makkah:

Is there not, among the servants of Allah or among His maidservants, a generous one who relieves the distress of one whose mind has gone?

He has an eye: as for its lids, they are weeping; as for the inner heart, the fire within it stands on one foot.

She vowed to devise a way for its author, if she knew him, to bring him together with the one he loved. Then while she was at Muzdalifah, she heard someone reciting them, so she sought him. He claimed that he had composed them concerning a cousin of his whose family had vowed not to marry her to him. She directed herself to the tribe and kept offering them money until they married her to him. And behold, the woman was more infatuated with him than he with her. She used to count this among her greatest good deeds, and she would say: "I am not anything more delighted than my bringing together that youth and that young woman."

Al-Kharaʼiti said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik had a young man and a slave-girl who loved each other. One day the young man wrote to her:

I saw you in a dream as if you had given me to drink from the cool saliva of your mouth,

And as if your hand were in my hand, and as if we had spent the night together on one bed.

So I spent my whole day drowsing, wishing to see you in my sleep, though I was not sleeping.

The slave-girl replied to him:

Good is what you saw, and all that you have seen, you will attain from me, despite the envious.

Indeed I hope that you will embrace me, so that you may spend the night with me upon a rounded breast,

And that I may see you between my anklets and my bracelets, and that I may see you upon my ribs and my body.

When this reached Sulayman, he married her to the young man and treated their situation well, despite his intense jealousy.

Jami' ibn Birkhiyyah said: I asked Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, the mufti of Madinah: "Is there any sin in a love that has overtaken us?"

Sa'id said: "One is blamed only for what one is able to control." Then Sa'id said: "By Allah, no one has asked me about this, and if someone had asked me, I would not have answered except with this."

Divisions of love for women

Love for women is of three kinds. One kind is an act of nearness and obedience, which is the love of one's wife and concubine. This love is beneficial, for it leads more to the aims for which Allah legislated marriage, and it restrains the eye and the heart from looking toward other than one's own people. For this reason, such a lover is praised by Allah and by people.

And a love which is hateful in the sight of Allah and a distancing from His mercy, and it is the most harmful thing to the servant in his religion and his worldly life, and it is the love of beardless youths. No one is afflicted with it except one who has fallen from the eye of Allah, been driven from His door, and whose heart has been made distant from Him. It is among the greatest veils that cut one off from Allah. As some of the early generations said: "When a servant falls from the eye of Allah, He afflicts him with love for beardless youths." This love is what brought upon the people of Lut what it brought, for they were not led astray except through this passion. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿By your life, indeed they were wandering blindly in their intoxication﴾ [al-Hijr: 72].

The remedy for this disease is seeking help from the Turner of hearts, sincerely turning to Him, occupying oneself with His remembrance, substituting love of Him and nearness to Him, and reflecting on the pain that this passion leads to, and the pleasure that is lost through it. Thus there follows the loss of the greatest beloved and the occurrence of the greatest hated. When his soul advances toward this and prefers it, let him pronounce takbir over himself as over a funeral, and let him know that affliction has encompassed him.

The third kind is permissible love, which occurs without intent, such as the love of one who is described a beautiful woman, or who sees her suddenly without intending to, so that his heart becomes attached to her, and that love does not lead him into any act of disobedience. This is not blameworthy and is not punished. The most beneficial course for him is to resist it and occupy himself with what is more beneficial to him than it. Concealment, chastity and patience in it under trial are obligatory, so Allah will make him steadfast in that, reward him for his patience for Allah's sake, his chastity, and his abandoning obedience to his desire, and his preferring the pleasure of Allah and what is with Him.

He asked her, and she informed him that she loved her master. So he returned her to him, and in his heart there remained something of her.

Al-Zamakhshari mentioned concerning Rabi'ah that Zubaydah read on a wall on the road to Makkah:

Is there not, among the servants of Allah or among His maidservants, a generous one who relieves the distress of one whose mind has gone?

He has an eye: as for its lids, they are weeping; as for the inner heart, the fire within it stands on one foot.

She vowed to devise a way for its author, if she knew him, to bring him together with the one he loved. Then while she was at Muzdalifah, she heard someone reciting them, so she sought him. He claimed that he had composed them concerning a cousin of his whose family had vowed not to marry her to him. She directed herself to the tribe and kept offering them money until they married her to him. And behold, the woman was more infatuated with him than he with her. She used to count this among her greatest good deeds, and she would say: "I am not anything more delighted than my bringing together that youth and that young woman."

Al-Kharaʼiti said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik had a young man and a slave-girl who loved each other. One day the young man wrote to her:

I saw you in a dream as if you had given me to drink from the cool saliva of your mouth,

And as if your hand were in my hand, and as if we had spent the night together on one bed.

So I spent my whole day drowsing, wishing to see you in my sleep, though I was not sleeping.

The slave-girl replied to him:

Good is what you saw, and all that you have seen, you will attain from me, despite the envious.

Indeed I hope that you will embrace me, so that you may spend the night with me upon a rounded breast,

And that I may see you between my anklets and my bracelets, and that I may see you upon my ribs and my body.

When this reached Sulayman, he married her to the young man and treated their situation well, despite his intense jealousy.

Jami' ibn Birkhiyyah said: I asked Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, the mufti of Madinah: "Is there any sin in a love that has overtaken us?"

Sa'id said: "One is blamed only for what one is able to control." Then Sa'id said: "By Allah, no one has asked me about this, and if someone had asked me, I would not have answered except with this."

Divisions of love for women

Love for women is of three kinds. One kind is an act of nearness and obedience, which is the love of one's wife and concubine. This love is beneficial, for it leads more to the aims for which Allah legislated marriage, and it restrains the eye and the heart from looking toward other than one's own people. For this reason, such a lover is praised by Allah and by people.

And a love which is hateful in the sight of Allah and a distancing from His mercy, and it is the most harmful thing to the servant in his religion and his worldly life, and it is the love of beardless youths. No one is afflicted with it except one who has fallen from the eye of Allah, been driven from His door, and whose heart has been made distant from Him. It is among the greatest veils that cut one off from Allah. As some of the early generations said: "When a servant falls from the eye of Allah, He afflicts him with love for beardless youths." This love is what brought upon the people of Lut what it brought, for they were not led astray except through this passion. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿By your life, indeed they were wandering blindly in their intoxication﴾ [al-Hijr: 72].

The remedy for this disease is seeking help from the Turner of hearts, sincerely turning to Him, occupying oneself with His remembrance, substituting love of Him and nearness to Him, and reflecting on the pain that this passion leads to, and the pleasure that is lost through it. Thus there follows the loss of the greatest beloved and the occurrence of the greatest hated. When his soul advances toward this and prefers it, let him pronounce takbir over himself as over a funeral, and let him know that affliction has encompassed him.

The third kind is permissible love, which occurs without intent, such as the love of one who is described a beautiful woman, or who sees her suddenly without intending to, so that his heart becomes attached to her, and that love does not lead him into any act of disobedience. This is not blameworthy and is not punished. The most beneficial course for him is to resist it and occupy himself with what is more beneficial to him than it. Concealment, chastity and patience in it under trial are obligatory, so Allah will make him steadfast in that, reward him for his patience for Allah's sake, his chastity, and his abandoning obedience to his desire, and his preferring the pleasure of Allah and what is with Him.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verses 26–28:

After mentioning what has been made lawful to us of women and what has been made unlawful of them, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you and to guide you to the ways of those before you, and to turn to you in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. And Allah desires to turn to you in forgiveness, while those who follow desires want you to deviate into a tremendous deviation. Allah desires to lighten for you [your burdens], and mankind was created weak.﴾ [al-Nisa': 26–28].

Sufyan al-Thawri mentioned in his tafsir, from Ibn Tawus, from his father: "Whenever he (Tawus) looked at women, he could not be patient."

In the Sahih, from the hadith of Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that "he saw a woman, so he went to Zaynab and fulfilled his need with her, and said: 'Indeed the woman approaches in the form of a devil and withdraws in the form of a devil. So when one of you sees a woman and she pleases him, let him go to his wife, for that will repel what is in his soul.'" In this hadith there are several benefits:

Among them: guidance to consoling oneself regarding the desired thing with its like, just as food takes the place of food and clothing the place of clothing.

And among them: the command to treat the infatuation with a woman, which inherits desire for her, with the most beneficial of remedies, which is fulfilling one's need with one's own wife. That breaks his desire for her. This is just as he guided those who love each other to marriage, as in the Sunan of Ibn Majah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Nothing has been seen for those who love one another like marriage."

So marrying the beloved is the remedy for passionate love, which Allah made a legislated remedy. Dawud (peace be upon him) treated himself with it, and the Prophet of Allah did not commit a prohibited act; he married the woman and included her among his wives because of his love for her, and his repentance was in accordance with his station with Allah and the loftiness of his rank. It does not befit us to add more to this.

As for the story of Zaynab bint Jahsh: Zayd had resolved to divorce her and she did not agree with him, and he kept consulting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about separating from her, while he was instructing him to keep her. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knew that he would certainly separate from her, so he concealed in himself that he would marry her once Zayd divorced her, and he feared the people's saying: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married his son's wife," for he had adopted Zayd before prophethood. The Lord, the Exalted, wanted to legislate a general law containing the interests of His servants. When Zayd divorced her and her waiting period ended, he sent someone to propose to her on his own behalf. Zayd came and turned his back to the door, and what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had mentioned about her grew great in his heart, so he called to her from behind the door: "O Zaynab, indeed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposes to you." She said: "I will not do anything until I consult my Lord," and she stood at her prayer niche and prayed. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Himself arranged her marriage to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and concluded the marriage for him above His Throne, and the revelation came with that: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then immediately rose and entered upon her. She used to boast over the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) about this, saying: "Your guardians married you off, but Allah married me from above seven heavens." This is the story of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with Zaynab.

There is no doubt that the Prophet (ﷺ) had women made beloved to him, as in the Sahih from Anas, from him (ﷺ): "Women and perfume have been made beloved to me from your world, and the coolness of my eyes has been placed in prayer." This is the wording of the hadith, not what some of them narrate: "Three things have been made beloved to me from your world," which Imam Ahmad added in the Kitab al-Zuhd to this hadith: "I am patient with food and drink, but I am not patient with them." The enemies of Allah, the Jews, envied him for this and said: "His only concern is marriage." So Allah, glorified is He, rejected this about His Messenger (ﷺ) and defended him, saying: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? Indeed, We gave the family of Ibrahim the Scripture and wisdom and gave them a great kingdom﴾ [al-Nisa': 54].

This is the Friend of Allah, Ibrahim, who had with him Sarah, the most beautiful of the women of the worlds, and he loved Hajar and took her as a concubine.

This is Dawud (peace be upon him), who had ninety-nine women, then he loved that woman and married her, thus completing the hundred. And this is his son Sulayman (peace be upon him), who used to go around in one night to ninety women.

"The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the person most beloved to him, and he said: 'Aisha' (may Allah be pleased with her), and he said regarding Khadijah: 'I have been provided with her love.'"

So love of women is among the perfections of humanity. Ibn Abbas said: "The best of this Ummah is the one with the most wives." Imam Ahmad mentioned that Abdullah ibn Umar, on the day of Jalula', had fallen to his share a slave-girl whose neck was like a silver ewer. Abdullah said: "I could not be patient with her, so I kissed her while the people were looking." By this Imam Ahmad argued for the permissibility of enjoying a captive woman before her istibra' (purification period) without intercourse, unlike a purchased slave-girl.

The difference between them is that the termination of ownership is not presumed in the case of a captive, unlike the purchased one, for in her case ownership may be terminated, so he would be enjoying the slave-girl of another.

The Prophet (ﷺ) also interceded for a lover that his beloved should join him by marrying him, but she refused. This was in the story of Mughith and Barirah: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him walking behind her with tears flowing down his cheeks, he said to her: 'If only you would return to him?' She said: 'Are you ordering me, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No, I am only interceding.' She said: 'I have no need for him.' Then he said to his uncle: 'O Abbas, are you not amazed at Mughith's love for Barirah, and her hatred for him?' and he did not object to his love for her, even though she had separated from him."

The Prophet (ﷺ) used to treat his wives equally in the division, and he would say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what I do not possess," meaning in love. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ [al-Nisa': 129], meaning in love and intercourse.

The rightly-guided caliphs and compassionate people among mankind continued to intercede for lovers with their beloved whose union is permissible, as previously mentioned regarding the actions of Abu Bakr and Uthman. Likewise Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) was brought a young Arab man who had been found in a people's house at night. He said to him: "What is your story?" He said: "I am not a thief, but I will tell you the truth:"

I became attached in the house of al-Riyahi to a fair maiden, before whose beauty the full moon humbles itself,

Among the daughters of Rome she has beauty and a form; when she boasts of her beauty, the pride of others is frightened of her.

When I came to the house from the heat of my heart, I stayed the night while in her the embers of her burning were ablaze,

The people of the house hurried at me, then cried out: "He is the thief, for whom death or capture is decreed."

When Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) heard his poetry, he was moved, and said to al-Muhallab ibn Rabah: "Allow him to have her." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, ask him who he is." He said: "Al-Nahhas ibn Uyaynah." He said: "Take her, for she is yours."

[Chapter on the story of Amr ibn al-As's tayammum from ritual impurity (janabah)]

In this expedition, "the commander of the army, Amr ibn al-As, had a wet dream (ihtalama). It was a cold night, and he feared for his own self from the water, so he performed tayammum (dry ablution) and led his companions in the dawn prayer. They mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: 'O Amr, you led your companions in prayer while you were in a state of janabah?' So he informed him of what had prevented him from washing (ghusl), and said: 'I heard Allah say: ﴿And do not kill yourselves. Indeed Allah is ever Merciful to you.﴾ [An-Nisa: 29].'
