The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said nothing." Those who argued from this story that tayammum does not remove the state of minor impurity (hadath) used it, because the Prophet ﷺ called him junub after his tayammum. Those who disputed with them answered with three responses:

The first: when the Companions complained about him, they said: "He led us in the dawn prayer while he was junub." So the Prophet ﷺ asked him about that and said: "You led your companions in prayer while you were junub?" as a question and an inquiry. When he informed him of his excuse, and that he had performed tayammum because of necessity, he approved of him in that.

The second: the narrations differ about him. In one narration it is related that he washed his private parts (maghabin), performed wudu' as for prayer, and then led them in prayer, and tayammum is not mentioned. It seems this narration is stronger than the narration of tayammum. Abd al-Haqq said, after mentioning it and mentioning the tayammum narration before it: "This one is more connected (awsal) than the first, because it is from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr al-Misri, from Abu al-Qays, the mawla of Amr, from Amr."

As for the first one, in which there is tayammum, it is from the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Amr ibn al-As, and does not mention Abu Qays between them.

The third: the Prophet ﷺ wanted to test the understanding (fiqh) of Amr regarding his leaving the ghusl. So he said to him: "You led your companions in prayer while you were junub?" When he informed him that he had performed tayammum because of necessity, he knew his understanding, and so he did not reject it from him. What indicates this is that what Amr did of tayammum, and Allah knows best, was out of fear of death from the cold, as he reported, and praying with tayammum in this situation is permissible and not disapproved of for the one who does it. So it is known that he intended to test his understanding and knowledge. And Allah knows best.

**(Subtle Point)**

Reflect on the words of the Exalted: ﴿If you avoid the major sins (kaba'ir) that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾.

Observe how, under it, with the most subtle, precise and excellent indication, is that whoever avoids all of shirk (association of partners with God), its major sins are expiated for him. The ratio of major sins to shirk is like the ratio of minor sins (saghair) to major sins. So when minor sins are expiated by avoiding major sins, major sins are expiated by avoiding shirk. You will find that the authentic hadith seems derived from this meaning, which is his saying ﷺ, relating from his Lord, blessed and exalted: "O son of Adam, if you come to Me with earth-full of sins and then meet Me without associating anything with Me, I will meet you with its equal in forgiveness."

And his saying: "God has forbidden the Fire to whoever says, 'There is no god but God,' sincerely from his heart."

Indeed, the erasure of monotheism, which is the monotheism of major sins, is greater than the erasure of minor sins by avoiding major sins.

**[Section: Sins are Major and Minor]**

The Qur'an, the Sunnah, the consensus (ijma') of the Companions, the Followers after them and the Imams have all shown that among sins there are major and minor ones. God the Exalted said: ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to an honourable entry﴾ [An-Nisa: 31].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿Those who avoid the major sins and the grave immoralities, except for minor lapses﴾ [An-Najm: 32].

In the authentic collection, from him ﷺ, that he said: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what lies between them, when major sins are avoided."

These expiating deeds have three degrees:

The first: that they fall short of expiating minor sins, due to their weakness, the weakness of sincerity in them, and the failure to fulfil their rights. This is like a weak medicine that falls short of resisting the disease in quantity and quality.

The second: that they resist minor sins but do not rise to expiating any major sins.

The third: that they are able to expiate minor sins and there remains in them a strength by which some major sins are expiated.

So reflect on this, for it will remove from you many difficulties.

In the two Sahihs, from him ﷺ, that he said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins." It was said: "What are they, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Associating partners with God, sorcery, killing a soul which God has forbidden except by right, consuming the property of orphans, consuming usury, fleeing on the day of battle, and slandering chaste, unaware, believing women."

In the two Sahihs, from him ﷺ, that he was asked: "Which sin is greatest in the sight of God?" He said: "That you set up a rival to God while He created you." It was said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you." It was said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Then God the Exalted revealed its confirmation: ﴿And those who do not invoke with God another god, nor kill the soul which God has forbidden except by right, nor commit adultery﴾ [Al-Furqan: 68].

**[The Number of Major Sins]**

People differed concerning major sins: is there a number that limits them? There are two opinions.

Then those who said they are limited differed about their number. 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said they are four; 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said they are seven; 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As said they are nine; another said they are eleven; and another said they are seventy.

Abu Talib al-Makki said: "I collected them from the sayings of the Companions and found them to be: four in the heart, namely: associating partners with God, persistence in disobedience, despair of God's mercy, and feeling secure from God's plan.

And four in the tongue: false testimony, slander of chaste women, the perjurous oath, and sorcery.

And three in the belly: drinking wine, consuming the property of orphans, and consuming usury.

And two in the private parts: fornication and sodomy.

And two in the hands: killing and theft.

And one in the feet: fleeing from the battle line.

And one which relates to the whole body: disobedience to parents."

Those who did not limit them to a number said: whatever God has forbidden in the Qur'an is a major sin, and whatever the Messenger ﷺ has forbidden is a minor sin.

Another group said: whatever is connected to its prohibition by a threat of curse, wrath or punishment is a major sin, and whatever is not connected to any of that is a minor sin.

It was said: whatever has a prescribed penalty in this world or a threat in the Hereafter attached to it is a major sin, and whatever has neither is a minor sin.

It was said: whatever all the religious laws agree on prohibiting is among the major sins, and whatever is prohibited in one law but not another is a minor sin.

It was said: whatever God or His Messenger has cursed its doer is a major sin.

It was said: all that is mentioned from the beginning of Surat an-Nisa to His saying: ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾ [An-Nisa: 31].

**[Those Who Did Not Divide Them into Major and Minor]**

Those who did not divide them into major and minor said: all sins, in relation to audacity against God the Glorified, disobedience to Him and opposition to His command, are major. Looking at one who disobeys His command and violates His prohibitions requires that all sins be major, since they are equal in this corruption.

They said: this is clarified by the fact that God the Glorified is not harmed by sins and is not affected by them, so some of them are not greater than others in relation to Him. Nothing remains but the mere act of disobedience and opposition, and there is no difference in this between one sin and another.

They said: this is also shown by the fact that the corruption of sins arises only from audacity and assault upon the right of the Lord, blessed and exalted. For this reason, if a man drinks wine, or has intercourse with a forbidden woman, while not believing it to be forbidden, he has combined ignorance with the corruption of committing what is forbidden. But if one who believes it to be forbidden does the same, he has brought one of the two corruptions, and it is he who deserves punishment rather than the first. So this shows that the corruption of a sin follows audacity and assault.

They said: this is also shown by the fact that disobedience contains contempt for the command and prohibition of the one obeyed, and violation of his sanctity, and in this there is no difference between one sin and another.

They said: so the servant should not look at the greatness or smallness of a sin in itself, but should look at the rank of the one he disobeys, his greatness, and the violation of his sanctity through disobedience. In this the condition does not differ between one act of disobedience and another. For if a great, obeyed king ordered one of his two slaves to go on an important errand to a distant land, and ordered the other to go on a small task to the side of the house, and they both disobeyed and opposed his command, they would both be equal in his hatred and in their fall from his regard.

They said: for this reason, the disobedience of one who abandons the pilgrimage while being in Mecca, or abandons Friday prayer while being a neighbour of the mosque, is more hateful in God's sight than the disobedience of one who abandons it from a distant place. The obligation upon the first is greater than the obligation upon the second. And if a man had two hundred dirhams and withheld its zakat, and another had two hundred thousand dirhams and withheld its zakat, they would be equal in withholding what was obligatory upon each of them. It is not far-fetched that they are equal in punishment, if each of them is persistent in withholding the zakat of his wealth, whether the wealth was little or much.

**[Section: The Truth of the Matter]**

The uncovering of the veil over this question is to say:

God the Mighty and Majestic sent His messengers, sent down His books, and created the heavens and the earth so that He might be known, worshipped, and made one, and so that the religion would be entirely for God, all obedience be for Him, and the call be to Him, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 56].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ [Al-Hijr: 85].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof. Command descends among them that you may know that God is over all things competent and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [At-Talaq: 12].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of stability for the people, and the sacred month and the offerings and garlands. That is so you may know that God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and that God is Knowing of all things﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 97].

So He the Glorified informed that the purpose of creation and command is that He be known by His names and attributes, that He be worshipped alone without partner, and that people establish justice (qist), which is the justice by which the heavens and the earth stand, as He the Exalted said: ﴿We sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the Balance so that people may uphold justice﴾ [Al-Hadid: 25].

So He the Glorified informed that He sent His messengers and sent down His books so that people might uphold justice, which is equity. Among the greatest of justice is monotheism, which is the head and pillar of justice. Indeed, associating partners with God is a tremendous injustice. Shirk is the greatest injustice, and monotheism is the most perfect justice. Whatever is most opposed to this purpose is the greatest of the major sins, and their gradations vary according to their opposition to it. And whatever is most in accord with this purpose is the most obligatory of obligations and the most required of acts of obedience.

So reflect upon this principle with true reflection, and consider its details, and you will know through it the wisdom of the Most Wise of judges and the Most Knowing of knowers in what He obligated upon His servants and forbade them, and the variation of the ranks of acts of obedience and acts of disobedience.

Since associating partners with God is by its very nature opposed to this purpose, it is the greatest of major sins absolutely. God forbade Paradise to every polytheist, made lawful his blood, his property and his family for the people of monotheism, and made it lawful for them to take them as slaves, since they abandoned the establishment of His worship. God the Glorified refuses to accept from a polytheist any deed, or to accept intercession for him, or to answer his supplication in the Hereafter, or to pardon his stumble. For the polytheist is the most ignorant of the ignorant regarding God, in that he has set up a rival for Him from among His creation, and that is the utmost ignorance of Him, just as it is the utmost injustice from him. Although the polytheist has not wronged his Lord, he has only wronged himself.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 32:

Do not ask anyone but your Master, for the servant's asking of other than his master is a reproach against him.

Planting seclusion yields the fruit of intimacy.

Feel estranged from what does not remain with you, and find comfort in the One who does not part from you.

The seclusion of the ignorant is corruption, but the seclusion of the scholar comes with its own provisions and its own drink.

When reason and certainty gather in the house of seclusion, thought is summoned, and intimate conversation takes place among them.

"There has come to you a discourse whose hearing never wearies,
Its prose and its verse are sweet to us."

"When the soul recalls it, its toil departs,
And the darkness of its meaning departs from the heart."

When a word of folly comes out from your enemy, do not join it with its like, for that would fertilize it, and the offspring of quarrel is a blameworthy offspring.

Your zeal for yourself is a trace of ignorance of it; for if you knew it truly, you would be helping your opponent against it.

When the spark of vengeance is struck from the fire of anger, it begins by burning the one who strikes it.

Bind your anger with the chain of forbearance, for it is a dog: if it breaks loose, it destroys.

Whoever has been preceded by the prior decree of happiness is guided to the evidence before the seeking.

When the Decree wills for a person, it sows in the soil of his heart the seed of success, then waters it with the water of longing and fear, then keeps watch over it with the stages of vigilance, and appoints for it the guard of knowledge; then behold, the crop stands upon its stalk.

When the star of resolve rises in the darkness of the night of idleness, and the moon of determination follows it, the land of the heart shines with the light of its Lord.

When the night falls, the struggle between sleep and wakefulness begins: fear and longing are at the vanguard of the army of wakefulness, while laziness and lingering are in the battalion of heedlessness. When resolve bears down, it charges the right wing, and the armies of neglect are routed. Dawn does not rise except that the shares have been divided and the spoils have been made cool for their people.

The journey by night is endured only by one whose hunger is concealed: the swift camels at the beginning, and the laden carriers at the end, do not tire of standing at the door, even if they are turned away, and do not cease their apology even if they are rejected. For if the door is opened to those accepted before you, then rush in like the liars, enter like the parasites, and spread out your palm saying: ﴿And be charitable to us﴾.

O you who seek to open the door of livelihood without the key of piety: how will you widen the path of sins and then complain of the narrowness of provision? Had you stopped at what piety desires, what you desire would not have eluded you.

Sins are a barrier in the gate of gain, and the servant is indeed deprived of provision by the sin that befalls him.

"By God, I have not come to you as a visitor
Except that I found the earth folded up for me,
Nor has my resolve turned back from your door
Except that I stumbled over my own skirts."

Spirits in bodies are like birds in towers.

What is prepared for hatching is not like what is prepared for racing.

Whoever among the workers wishes to know his standing with the ruler, let him look at what work he assigns him and with what occupation he occupies him.

Be of the people of the Hereafter and not of the people of this world, for the child follows the mother.

This world is not worth the moving of your feet toward it, so how could you run after it?

This world is a carcass, and the lion does not fall upon carcasses. This world is a crossing place, and the Hereafter is a homeland, and needs are sought only in homelands.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 56 (part 1 of 2)

If it is said: What pleasure and what good arises from a severe, perpetual punishment that never ends and never slackens for its people? Rather, its people remain in it for ever and ever. Whenever their skins are burnt through, they are replaced with other skins. They are not given a decree that would let them die, nor is their punishment lightened for the blink of an eye?

It is said: By the life of God, this is a question that shakes mountains, let alone the hearts of men. Because of this question, some have denied the wisdom of the All-Mighty, the All-Wise. They have referred the matter to a pure will with no cause and no purpose. They have permitted God to punish the people of His obedience and His allies, sending them to the lowest depths of Hell, and to bestow blessing on His enemies, the polytheists, raising them to the highest gardens of Bliss for ever and ever. They have permitted Him to send into the Fire whomever He wills without any cause or deed at all, to make no distinction among its people despite their differing deeds, to make no distinction in punishment among those whose deeds differ, to punish a man for another's sin, and to nullify all of his good deeds so that He does not reward him for them, or rewards another with them. All of this, they say, is permissible for Him, and one cannot know that He will not do it except through a true report, since that report attributes both it and its opposite to Him equally. They say there is no escape from this question except through this principle. Sometimes they cling to an apparent meaning of speech without placing it in its proper context, and without reconciling it with the evidences of justice and wisdom, with the linking of matters to their causes and their ordering by them, and with the effects of balance and correspondence. They have erred in understanding the Qur'an, just as they erred in describing the Lord with what is not fitting for Him and in attributing to Him what is not permissible for Him.

Those who affirm causes and wisdom among the Qadariyya (the Qadariyya, an early school that affirmed human power over action) opposed them. They claimed that they escape the ugly statement by affirming wisdom and causality, but they fell into its counterpart or something worse. They made it obligatory upon God, glorified be He, to make eternal in the Fire, together with His enemies the disbelievers, for ever and ever, one who spent his life in obedience to Him and then committed a single grave sin and died persisting in it. They did not regard his obedience, nor did they uphold his Islam. In this doctrine they are worse in statement than their brethren, the Jabriyya (the Jabriyya, who deny human agency in action). For those did not make that ruling obligatory upon God; they only held it permissible for Him, and permitted that He might not do it. These ones made it obligatory upon Him to eternally punish the people of the grave sins together with the disbelievers, and did not permit Him to bring them out of it. Their error regarding the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and regarding what is permissible for the Lord and what is not, is like the error of their brethren, the Jabriyya.

When other people of speculation and inquiry thought that this was the corruption the Messengers had reported, and knew that it contradicts wisdom, mercy, justice and benefit, they said that this punishment is a warning and an imagining with no reality. It is meant to restrain the bestial and animal souls from their aggression and desires, so that by it the welfare of existence is maintained. The chief causes of the unbelief and atheism of these people, and of their disbelief in God and the Last Day, were their attribution of those false doctrines and corrupt sayings to the Messengers, and their claim that the Messengers called people to believe in them. Likewise, they fell into a generalization concerning the question of the origination of the world. They told people that the Messengers reported from God that He had always been idle with respect to action, that action was impossible for Him, and then He transformed from an essential impossibility to an essential possibility at the beginning, without any renewed cause or matter arising in the Agent. They said: whoever does not believe this is neither a believer nor one who confirms the Messengers. This is the doctrine concerning the beginning; the other concerns the return.

Then another group came and rolled up the carpet of creation and command altogether. They said: all of this is impossible and deception. There are not two existences; rather, all existence is one. There is no Creator and created, no Lord and servant, no obedience and disobedience. The matter is nothing but one uniform order, and distinction is a judgment of illusion and imagination. The heavens and the earth, this world and the Hereafter, pre-eternity and eternity, the good and the bad, are all one thing, from one essence. Then they corrected themselves and said: no, it is the Essence itself.

People, except those whom God wills, grew up between these four sects, knowing nothing but their sayings and doctrines. Therefore the affliction became great, the calamity intense, and the intelligent among mankind became the heretics of the world, while those nearest to salvation are the dull-witted and the simple. Intellect and revelation are far removed from these sects, and their positions are the furthest from both. So we say, and with God is the success, in Him is the help, and upon Him is the reliance.

(Section)

The Qur'an, the Sunnah, the innate nature (fitrah, the natural disposition created in humans) and the evidences of reason all indicate that He, glorified be He, created the heavens and the earth and what is between them with truth. He did not create anything in vain, aimlessly, or falsely. He brought into existence the upper and lower worlds and what is in them through the truth, which is His attribute, His name, His word and His act. He, glorified be He, is the Manifest Truth. Nothing proceeds from Him except truth. He speaks only truth, acts only truth, commands only truth, and recompenses only with truth. Falsehood is not attributed to Him; rather, falsehood is what is not attributed to Him, such as a false judgment, a false religion that He did not permit and did not prescribe through the tongues of His Messengers, or a false object of worship that does not deserve worship and is not worthy of it. Its worship is false, its call is false. False speech is lying, falsehood and absurdity, speech that is not connected to any existing truth, but whose connection is to something unreal with no reality.

He, glorified be He, created creation only to worship Him and to know Him. The root of worship is love for Him for His bounties and blessings, and for His perfection and majesty. This is a matter of innate nature upon which God originated His creation. This is the fitrah with which He created mankind, just as He created them to acknowledge Him. As the Messengers said to their peoples: ﴿Is there doubt about God, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?﴾ (Qur'an 14:10). So creation is created upon knowing Him and affirming His oneness. If they were left to this fitrah, they would grow up knowing Him and worshipping Him alone. This fitrah is a created disposition upon which they were created, and there is no alteration of God's creation. People continued upon this fitrah for many generations. Then something arose that caused its corruption and its departure from soundness and uprightness, like what afflicts a healthy body and a sound nature and causes them to depart from health into deviation. So He sent His Messengers to return people to their original fitrah on which they were created.

With the Messengers, people divided into three categories.

The first: those who responded to them completely and submitted to them completely. Their fitrah returned to what it had been, with the addition of the perfection and completion it gained in the two powers of beneficial knowledge and righteous action. Thus their fitrah increased in perfection beyond its perfection. These do not need in the Hereafter refinement, discipline, or a fire that melts away their foul residues and purifies them from filth and dirt, for their submission to the Messengers removed all of that from them.

The second: those who responded to them in one respect but not in another. Some residues of filth and dirt that contradict the truth for which they were created remained upon them. The All-Knowing, the All-Wise, provided them with remedies suited to the ailments that afflicted them, namely trial and testing. If these were sufficient to free them from it in this world, well and good; if not, then in the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection). If that suffices to free them, well and good; if not, then the standing place of the Resurrection and its terrors will free them from that remainder. If that suffices, well and good; if not, there is no escape from treatment with the greatest remedy, and the last of medicine is cauterization. So they enter the furnace of purification and refinement, until when they are refined and the remedy has no further benefit, they are brought out from the hospital of the sick to the abode of the healthy, as the continuous Sunnah from the Prophet (ﷺ) indicates, and as he stated in his saying: "Until, when they are refined and purified, permission is granted to them to enter Paradise."

Likewise is the saying of the Most High: ﴿You are pure, so enter it, abiding therein﴾ (Qur'an 39:73). He did not permit them to enter it except after their purity, for it is the abode of the pure. There is no impurity in it at all. For this reason, these people remain in the Fire according to their need for purification and the removal of impurity.

The third category: a people who did not respond to the Messengers and did not submit to them, but persisted in departing from the fitrah and did not return to it. Their corruption became firmly established in them to the utmost firmness, and no soundness is hoped for them. The trials of this world, the calamities of death and what follows it, and the terrors of the Resurrection do not suffice to remove their filth and dirt. It is not befitting for the wisdom of the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, to place them alongside the pure in their abode. They were not created for annihilation. So these are the people of the abode of trial and testing, who remain in it as long as the rot of disbelief and polytheism that they carry remains. The Fire was kindled upon them only by their own evil deeds. Their punishment is by means of their very evil deeds. For them, from those deeds, are forms of punishment suited to them and resembling them. The punishment remains upon them as long as the realities of those deeds and what they produce remain. So long as the causes of punishment remain, the punishment remains.

It remains to be asked: has the trace of the original fitrah vanished entirely, so that it has become as though it never was, and been completely nullified, the matter passing to the accidental corruption that destroyed it? In that case there is no path to their deliverance from the punishment, since it is the trace of that corruption which removed the fitrah. Or is it said that the fitrah has not vanished entirely, but its sickness and corruption have become firmly established, while its root remains, as the sickness and corruption of the body become firmly established while life still persists in it, though it is a life that brings no benefit? If a bitter remedy that is hard to take is prescribed, there is no way to health except by repeating its intake many, many times, which removes that accidental sickness, so that the trace of the original fitrah appears, and no further treatment is needed after that. This is the secret of the question. The one who holds this second estimation says: reason does not show that this is impossible, since there is nothing in it that makes it impossible. We reply: rather, reason, revelation and the fitrah have all shown that the Lord, Exalted is He, is All-Wise and Merciful, and that wisdom and mercy refuse to let these souls remain in punishment for ever and ever, such that their punishment endures for as long as God endures. This is not from wisdom and mercy.

They say: the many proofs from the texts and from reflection have shown that what God has legislated and decreed in this world of punishments and penalties is only for refining souls and purifying them of the evil within them, and for achieving the benefit of deterrence and admonition, and of weaning souls from returning to sin, along with other wisdoms. When these are achieved, punishment becomes free of wisdom and benefit, and so it ceases. For it is the punishment of the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, the Merciful, who does not punish without purpose, nor punish for a benefit that returns to Him through the punishment. Both of these matters are impossible. In that case, punishment only occurs for the benefit of the one punished or the benefit of another. It is known that there is no benefit to him or to anyone else in his remaining in punishment for ever and ever.

They say: among what the Qur'an and the Sunnah indicate is that the kind of pains are for the benefit of the children of Adam. The Most High said: ﴿That is because they are not afflicted by thirst, nor fatigue, nor hunger in the way of God, nor do they tread any path that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they inflict on an enemy any harm, but a righteous deed is recorded for them thereby. Indeed God does not waste the reward of the good-doers﴾ (Qur'an 9:120). And His saying: ﴿And that God may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers﴾ (Qur'an 3:141).

So He informed that the pain of killing and wounds in His way is a purification and refinement for the believers. He gave good tidings to those who are patient under the pain of hunger, fear, poverty, the loss of loved ones, and other things, with His blessing, His mercy and His guidance. And the Most High said: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ (Qur'an 4:123).

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: "O Messenger of God, there came a back-breaking affliction, and we did not do any evil." He said: "O Abu Bakr, are you not fatigued? Are you not grieved? Does not hardship befall you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is among what you are recompensed for."

And the Most High said: ﴿Whatever affliction strikes you is for what your hands have earned﴾ (Qur'an 42:30). In this there is both good tidings and warning, for He has informed us that the afflictions of this world are punishments for our sins. He is too merciful to repeat the punishment upon His servant for a sin for which He has already punished him in this world. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is afflicted with any of these filthy things and God conceals it, his affair is with God: if He wills He punishes him, and if He wills He forgives him. And whoever is punished for it in this world, God is too generous to repeat the punishment upon His servant."

In a hadith: "Prescribed penalties (hudud) are expiations for those who receive them." In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ubadah: "Whoever suffers any of that and is punished for it in this world, it is an expiation for him." In the Sahih, from him (ﷺ): "Nothing afflicts the believer of fatigue, weariness, worry, grief, harm, even the thorn that pricks him, but God expiates some of his sins by it." And he said: "Affliction does not cease to befall the believer in his family, his wealth and his children until he meets God with no sin upon him."

In another hadith: "When the believer falls ill, he comes out like a garment in its purity and its colour."

In another hadith: "Fever burns away sins as the furnace removes the impurity from iron."

In another hadith: "Do not revile fever, for it removes the sins of the children of Adam."

Among the names of fever is "the expiator of sins."

In the authentic hadith: "God, Mighty and Majestic, will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My servant, I was ill and you did not visit Me.' He will say: 'How could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds?' He will say: 'My servant so-and-so was ill and you did not visit him. Had you visited him, you would have found Me with him.'"

This is more eloquent than His saying regarding feeding and giving drink: "You would have found that with Me." He, glorified be He, is with the one afflicted by illness as a mercy from Him to him, and as good, and as nearness to Him, through breaking his heart with illness, for He is with those whose hearts are broken. This is too great to be fully mentioned. The Lord of this world and the Hereafter is one, and His wisdom and His mercy are present in this world and the next. Indeed, the manifestation of His mercy in the Hereafter is greater. The punishment of the believers in the Fire in the Hereafter belongs to this category, just as their punishment in this world through afflictions and prescribed penalties does. Likewise, their detention between Paradise and the Fire until they are refined and purified. It has been established by clear, authentic texts that their punishment in the Fire varies in degree and duration according to their sins, and that they do not leave it all at once, but one after another, until there remains one man who is the last of them to come out. Likewise, the punishment of the disbelievers in it varies enormously. The hypocrites are in its lowest depths, while Abu Talib is the least punished of its people, in shallow fire from a well boiling with his brain. The people of Pharaoh are in the most severe punishment.

They say: if punishment in the abode in which there is one mercy out of a hundred is a mercy to its people and a benefit and kindness to them, how much more so in the abode in which a hundred mercies appear, each mercy as wide as the distance between the heaven and the earth? The Most High said: ﴿And We shall surely make them taste the nearer punishment short of the greater punishment, that perhaps they may return﴾ (Qur'an 32:21).

So He informed that He punishes them out of mercy towards them, to bring them back from punishment to Him, just as a compassionate father punishes his child when he flees to his enemy, so that he may return to his kindness and honour. The Most High said: ﴿What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? God is ever Appreciative and All-Knowing﴾ (Qur'an 4:147).

And you find beneath these words that His punishing you does not add to His dominion, nor does He benefit from it, nor is it purposeless and devoid of wisdom and benefit. And that if you exchange gratitude and faith for disbelief, your punishment comes from you, and your disbelief is what you are punished by. Otherwise, what would reach Him from your punishment, and what benefit would reach Him from it?

They say: then wisdom requires that wicked souls must have a punishment that refines them according to their deeds, as hearing and reason indicate. That requires an end, not permanence.

They say: the Most High did not create man in vain. He created him to show him mercy, not to punish him. The acquisition of the cause of punishment came after his creation. So His mercy preceded His wrath, and the cause of mercy is prior to the cause of wrath and dominates it. His punishment is not the purpose of His creation; rather, His punishment is for wisdom and mercy. And wisdom and mercy refuse that His punishment should continue endlessly without termination.

As for mercy, that is evident. As for wisdom, He punishes only for a matter that arose upon the fitrah and altered it, not one fixed in the original creation nor created for it. He did not create them for polytheism or for punishment; He created them for worship and mercy. But there arose upon them the cause of punishment, and so they deserved punishment. That cause has no permanence, for it is false, unlike the truth which is the cause of mercy, which is permanent with the permanence of the Truth, glorified be He. Mercy is the purpose, and the cause of punishment is not a purpose, just as punishment is not a purpose. Mercy, however, is a purpose and its cause is a purpose. So reflect on this with the utmost reflection, for it is the secret of the question.

They say: the Lord, Exalted is He, is named the Forgiving, the Merciful, and He did not name Himself the Punisher or the Chastiser. Rather, He placed punishment and chastisement among His acts, as He said: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ (Qur'an 15:49-50). And He said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (Qur'an 7:167). And He said: ﴿Indeed the seizure of your Lord is severe. It is He who originates and repeats. And He is the Forgiving, the Loving﴾ (Qur'an 85:12-14). And He said: ﴿Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book from God, the Mighty, the All-Knowing, Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment﴾ (Qur'an 40:1-3).

This is abundant in the Qur'an. He, glorified be He, praises Himself with pardon, forgiveness, mercy, generosity and forbearance, and names Himself with them. He does not praise Himself as the Punisher, nor as the Wrathful, nor as the Chastiser, nor as the Afflicter, except in the hadith that enumerates the Most Beautiful Names, and that is not established.

And He has prescribed for Himself a decree that His mercy precedes His wrath. Likewise, toward the people of the Fire, His mercy precedes His wrath. He showed them many kinds of mercy before they angered Him by their polytheism. He showed them mercy in their state of polytheism. He showed them mercy by establishing the proof against them. He showed them mercy by calling them to Him after they had angered Him, harmed His messengers, and denied them. He granted them respite and did not hasten to punish them. Indeed His mercy encompassed them, so His mercy overcame His wrath. Were it not so, the world would be ruined, the heavens would collapse upon the earth, and the mountains would crumble. When mercy prevails over wrath and precedes it, it is impossible that the cause of wrath should persist forever and prevail over His mercy.

They said: Punishment is either pointless or for a purpose and wisdom. That it be pointless is something the Wisest of the wise is exalted above, and attributing it to Him is attributing to Him one of the greatest deficiencies. If it is for a purpose, then the purpose is a benefit, along with what necessarily accompanies it and what it necessarily entails. That benefit either returns to the Lord, may He be exalted, who is far above and beyond that, or it returns to the creature. It returns either to the punished soul itself, or to another, or to both. The first is impossible, for there is no benefit to it in perpetual punishment without end. As for the benefit to another, if it is admonition and deterrence, then it has been achieved. If it is the completion of his pleasure, joy, and delight, by seeing his enemy in that state while he himself is in the utmost bliss, then even the hardest of creatures would have pity on his enemy because of the length of his torment and the continuance of what he endures. Nothing remains but to break those arrogant, obstinate souls and to treat them, so that they may reach the root of their diseases and ailments and eradicate them. That root is an evil that came upon a good, upon which they were created at the beginning of their nature.

They said: The possible categories among creatures are five, and no more can be added: pure good and its opposite; preponderant good and its opposite; and good and evil in equal measure. Wisdom requires the existence of two of these, namely pure good and preponderant good. As for pure evil or preponderant evil, wisdom does not require its existence but rather rejects it. For everything God, glory be to Him, created, He created for a wisdom whose existence is better than its non-existence. He created harmful creatures and acts that are evil, because of the beloved good that results from their creation. He did not create for mere evil that entails no good in any way whatsoever. This is utterly absurd. Good is what is intended in itself, as the primary aim, while evil is intended only as a means and a preliminary, not as an ultimate end or final goal. Therefore, when the intended end for which it was created is achieved, it passes away and ceases, just as means cease once they reach their ends, as is known by sense and reason. Accordingly, punishment is an evil that has an end for which it is sought, and it is a means to that end. When its end is achieved, it stands in the position of a path that leads to the destination. When the traveler has reached his destination by it, there is no further benefit in traversing it.

The essence of the matter is that mercy is the goal of creation and command, not punishment. Punishment is among His creations. This is consistent with His having created it for a praiseworthy end. It is necessary that His names and the effects of His attributes be manifested in general and without restriction, for this is perfection, and the Lord, majestic is His majesty, is described by perfection and exempt from deficiency.

They said: God, may He be exalted, has said: ﴿As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, where for them is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends.﴾ And He said: ﴿The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as Allah wills.﴾

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: "This verse overrides every verse in the Qur'an." It was related by al-Bayhaqi, Harb, and others.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "There will come upon Hell a time when no one will be in it, and that is after they have remained in it for ages (ahqab)."

From Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Hurayra, the like of this was related. It was mentioned by a group of compilers of the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition). This implies that the abode in which no one remains is the one in which its people have remained for ages.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "God has informed us about what He wills for the people of Paradise, saying, ﴿a gift not cut off﴾, but He has not informed us about what He wills for the people of the Fire."

They said: What suffices us is what is in Surah al-An'am, His saying: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all, [He will say], "O company of jinn, you have taken much from mankind." And their allies from mankind will say, "Our Lord, we benefited from one another, and we have reached the term You appointed for us." He will say, "The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing."﴾ up to His saying: ﴿O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "We bear witness against ourselves." And the worldly life deceived them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers.﴾

This is an address to the disbelievers among the jinn and mankind, in several respects.

First, their arrogance toward them, meaning toward those who misled and led them astray. They were arrogant toward the disbelievers.

Second, His saying: ﴿And their allies from mankind will say﴾. Their allies are the disbelievers, as God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe﴾. So the party of Satan are his allies.

Third, His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe﴾. Despite this, He said: ﴿The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as Allah wills.﴾ Then He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.﴾ Thus their punishment is tied to His knowledge and wisdom, and likewise the exception is issued from knowledge and wisdom. He is Knowing of what He does to them and Wise in that.

They said: It has been reported in the Qur'an that when He, glory be to Him, mentions the reward of the people of His mercy and the people of His wrath together, He makes the reward of the people of mercy eternal and leaves the reward of the people of wrath unrestricted in time, as in His saying: ﴿As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, where for them is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends. As for those who are made happy, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills — a gift not cut off.﴾

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein. They are the worst of creation. Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds — they are the best of creation. Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.﴾ And His saying: ﴿On a Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black. As for those whose faces turned black, [it will be said], "Did you disbelieve after your faith? Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve." But as for those whose faces turned white, they will be in the mercy of Allah, abiding therein.﴾

Sometimes the two are mentioned together and the people of wrath are decreed to abide forever, as in His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, indeed for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.﴾ And His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits — He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein, and for him is a humiliating punishment.﴾

But the mere mention of eternity and perpetuity does not necessarily imply the absence of an end, for khuluud (abiding) is a long duration, as in their saying "a long-lived (mukhallad) camel," and the perpetuity of each thing is according to its own measure. Perpetuity may be for the duration of life, and it may be for the duration of the worldly life. God, may He be exalted, said regarding the Jews: ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forth. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ It is known that they will wish for it in the Fire, when they say: ﴿O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!﴾ The non-cessation of the bliss of Paradise is established only by His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision, which has no end (nafad).﴾ And His saying: ﴿a gift not cut off (majdhudh)﴾ and His saying: ﴿for them is a reward never interrupted (mamnun)﴾, that is, cut off. Whoever says it is not bestowed upon them as a favor has erred in the worst possible error. No such thing has come concerning the punishment of the people of the Fire.

And the Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿They will not be removed from the Fire﴾, ﴿and they will not be taken out of it﴾, and His saying: ﴿It will not be decreed for them so that they would die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them.﴾

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned into it﴾, in two places in the Qur'an. And His saying: ﴿Whenever their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins﴾ is not diverted from its apparent and literal meaning according to the correct view.

A group has claimed that the unrestricted statements of these verses are restricted by the verses that qualify them with the exception of God's will. This would be a case of specifying the general. This seems to be the view of some of the early scholars regarding the verse of exception, who said it overrides every threat in the Qur'an. The correct view is that these verses are on their generality and their unrestrictedness. Yet there is nothing in them indicating that the Fire itself will endure as long as God endures, with no end to it. Nothing in the Qur'an or the Sunnah indicates this in any way. There is a difference between the punishment of its people being perpetual for as long as it lasts, and the Fire itself being everlasting, never ending, never perishing, and never ceasing. These are two different matters.

It may be asked: Then is there no difference between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, since each of them perishes and ceases?

It is said: The differences between them are clearer than needing to be explained. Moreover, the punishment of this world ends with the death of the one punished and with the lifting of the punishment from him. But as for the punishment of the Hereafter, the one deserving eternal abiding in it does not die, its punishment is not lifted from him, and no one can repel it from him, as God said: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to befall, there is none to avert it.﴾ It is constant and never departs. God said: ﴿Indeed, its punishment was ever a permanent debt (gharaman)﴾, that is, constant. From this comes the name gharim (debtor, creditor's partner in obligation) because of the constancy of his obligation to his creditor.

[The Gravity of Accepting the Office of Judge]

Concerning the judge, there are warnings and threats that are not found for the mufti (jurisconsult). This is as narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi from the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that judges were mentioned in her presence, and she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"On the Day of Resurrection, a just judge will be brought forth, and he will encounter such severity of reckoning that he will wish he had never judged between two people over a single date."

Al-Sha'bi narrated from Masruq, from 'Abdullah, raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ): "No ruler judges between people except that an angel is appointed over him, seizing him by the nape of the neck, until he brings him to the edge of Hell. Then he raises his head to Allah. If He commands that he be cast down, he is cast into a pit of forty autumns (years)."

In the Sunan (collections) from the hadith of Ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Judges are of three kinds: two are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. A man who knew the truth and judged by it, he is in Paradise. A man who judged between people in ignorance, he is in the Fire. And a man who knew the truth but acted unjustly, he is in the Fire."

'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Woe to the judge of those on earth from the Judge of those in heaven, on the Day they meet Him, except one who commanded justice, judged with truth, did not judge by whim, nor by kinship, nor by desire or fear, and made the Book of Allah a mirror before his eyes."

In the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever seeks the judgeship of the Muslims until he attains it, and then his justice prevails over his injustice, for him is Paradise; and whoever's injustice prevails over his justice, for him is the Fire."

In the Sunan of al-Bayhaqi, from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah is with the judge as long as he does not act unjustly. When he acts unjustly, Allah disowns him and Satan clings to him."

Also in it, from the hadith of Husayn al-Mu'allim, from al-Shaybani, from Ibn Abi Awfa, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah is with the judge as long as he does not act unjustly. When he acts unjustly, He leaves him to himself."

In the Four Sunan, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever installs a judge among the Muslims has slaughtered himself without a knife."

In the Sunan of al-Bayhaqi, from the hadith of Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Woe to the rulers, woe to the 'urafa' (overseers), woe to the trustees! People will surely wish on the Day of Resurrection that their forelocks had been hung from the Pleiades, tossed between heaven and earth, and that they had never held any office."

[The Warning Concerning Issuing Fatwas]

As for the mufti, in the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Muslim ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever speaks falsely against me, let him take his seat in Hell. And whoever gives a fatwa without knowledge, its sin is upon the one who gave it. And whoever advises his brother about a matter while knowing the right course lies elsewhere, has betrayed him."

Thus, every danger that applies to the mufti also applies to the judge, and he bears additional danger specific to himself. However, the danger of the mufti is greater in another respect, for his fatwa is a general ruling that concerns the one who asks and others. The judge's ruling, by contrast, is particular and specific, and does not extend beyond the one against whom or in whose favour it is given. The mufti issues a general, universal ruling: that whoever does such-and-such, such-and-such follows; whoever says such-and-such, such-and-such is binding on him. The judge issues a specific ruling upon a specific person. So his judgement is particular and binding, while the scholar's fatwa is general and not binding. Both carry great reward, and both carry great danger.

(Benefit)

Ibn 'Aqil said: "The payments that judges receive are of four kinds: bribery (rishwa), gift (hadiyya), wage (ujra), and provision (rizq).

Bribery is forbidden and is of two types: a bribe to incline toward one of the parties without right, which is forbidden, a sin for both the taker and the giver. And a bribe given in order to rule with truth, or to secure the giver's right, such as a debt or the like; this is forbidden for the judge but not for the giver, since it is for the rescue of a right. It is like the reward for recovering a runaway slave, and like the fee of agents in litigation. As for gifts, they are of two types: a gift given before the appointment, whose continuation is not forbidden; and a gift that was only given after the appointment. This is of two types: disliked, which is a gift to him from someone who has no case before him; and a gift from someone who has a case before him, which is forbidden for both the judge and the giver.

As for wages: if the judge has a provision from the Imam out of the public treasury, it is forbidden for him to take a wage, by unanimous agreement, because the provision was only assigned to him for devoting himself to judging, so there is no ground for taking a fee from the litigants. If the judge has no provision, there are two views: one is permissibility, because it is lawful work, so it is like the case where both parties appoint him as arbitrator; and because without a provision, judging is not obligatory for him, so he is not prevented from taking a fee, like the guardian of an orphan and the trustee of the judge, who may eat from the orphan's property to the extent of need. As for provision from the Bayt al-mal (public treasury): if he is wealthy and has no need of it, it is possible that it is disliked, lest it constrain those who hold public interests; and it is possible that it is permitted, because he has given himself to this, so he is like the collector of zakat and the kharaj (land tax)."

I say: The root of these issues is the collector of zakat and the guardian of the orphan. Allah the Exalted permitted the collector of zakat a portion of it, so he takes it whether poor or rich.

The Prophet ﷺ prevented him from accepting a gift, and said: "Why did he not sit in the house of his father and mother, to see whether gifts would be sent to him or not?"

In this is evidence that whoever is given a gift at his home, and it was not because of the office of collecting zakat, it is permissible for him to accept it. This indicates that if the judge is given a gift by someone who used to give him gifts before the judgeship, and his office was not the cause of the gift, then he may accept it.

As for the guardian of the orphan: Allah the Exalted commanded him to abstain when wealthy, and permitted him to eat in a reasonable manner when poor, either as a loan or as a permission, according to the disagreement on this. The judge is a branch lying between two roots: the collector of zakat and the guardian of the orphan. So whoever looks to the general need for him and the attainment of public benefit through him, attaches him to the collector of zakat, so he takes his provision even if wealthy, as the collector of zakat takes it. And whoever looks to him as a shepherd placed to manage the affairs of the subjects, for whom they have no share, attaches him to the guardian of the orphan: if he is in need, he takes; if he is wealthy, he refrains.

This is more well-founded, and it is the view of the two Rightly-Guided Caliphs. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I have placed myself in relation to the wealth of Allah in the position of the guardian of the orphan: if he is in need, he eats in a reasonable manner; if he is rich, he refrains."

The difference between him and the collector of zakat is that the collector of zakat is hired by the Imam to collect and gather the wealth due to its beneficiaries, so what he takes, he takes in exchange for his work, like someone a man hires to collect his own dues. As for the judge, he is installed to compel people to abide by the laws and rulings of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, and to convey them to them. He is a messenger from Allah the Exalted through his fatwa, and he is distinguished from the mufti by the binding force of his authority and his power. The one who conveys from Allah the Exalted and binds the nation to his religion does not deserve anything from them. If he is in need, he has from the fay' (public revenue) what meets his need. This is one category, and the collector of zakat is another category. So the judge is a mufti in his reporting of the ruling of Allah and His Messenger, a witness in what is established before him, and binding upon whoever the right is directed against. He must therefore meet the conditions of both the mufti and the witness, and is distinguished by the power to enforce. He occupies the position of the successor of the one who said: ﴿I ask you for no wage for it﴾. These are the judges whose existence is imagined in minds, and who are absent in reality, whom Allah made as shades to which the distressed take refuge, and as watering places from which the thirsty drink.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 59 (part 1 of 7):

He, exalted is He, commanded obedience to Himself and obedience to His Messenger, and He repeated the verb to inform that obedience to the Messenger is obligatory in its own right, without first presenting what he commands to the Book. Rather, when he commands, his obedience is obligatory absolutely, whether what he commands is in the Book or not in it. He was given the Book and its like along with it. He did not command obedience to those in authority (ulu al-amr) in its own right. Instead, He omitted the verb and placed their obedience within the obedience to the Messenger, to indicate that they are obeyed only by following the obedience to the Messenger. Thus, whoever among them commands obedience to the Messenger, his obedience is obligatory, and whoever commands contrary to what the Messenger brought, there is no hearing and no obedience for him. This is as it is authentically related from him (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator."

He also said: "Obedience is only in what is good." And he said concerning the rulers: "Whoever among them commands you to disobey Allah, there is no hearing and no obedience for him."

He (ﷺ) informed about those who wanted to enter the Fire when their commander ordered them to enter it, that "if they had entered it, they would not have come out of it." Yet they were only entering it out of obedience to their commander, and thinking that this was obligatory upon them. But because they fell short in exertion (ijtihad, independent reasoning and effort to know the ruling), and hastened to obey one who commanded disobedience to Allah, and they understood the general command to obey in a way the commander (ﷺ) did not intend, and what was known of his religion was the intention of its opposite, they fell short in exertion and proceeded to torment and destroy themselves without verifying and clarifying whether that was obedience to Allah and His Messenger or not. So what then is the assumption about one who obeys someone other than Him in the clear opposition to what Allah and His Messenger sent?

Then He, exalted is He, commanded that what the believers dispute be referred back to Allah and His Messenger, "if you are believers," and He informed them that this is better for them in the immediate and better in outcome.

[Section: The Address with Faith]

So He commanded obedience to Himself and to His Messenger, and He opened the verse with the address by the name of faith, which indicates that what is required of them is among the requirements of the name by which they were addressed and spoken to. As one says: "O you whom Allah has blessed and enriched from His bounty, be good as Allah has been good to you," and "O scholar, teach people what benefits them," and "O judge, judge with truth," and similar examples.

For this reason, address in the Qur'an frequently occurs with the legal obligations, such as His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fasting has been prescribed for you﴾, ﴿O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer﴾, and ﴿O you who believe, fulfill the contracts﴾. In this there is an indication that if you are believers, then faith requires of you such and such, for it is among the requirements and completion of faith.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those of authority among you﴾. So He linked the obedience to Allah and the Messenger with the obedience to those in authority, and governed them both by a single operator. It might have been thought that the command would imply the opposite of this, since whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah. But what occurs here in the verse is the fitting arrangement.

Beneath this is a subtle secret, which is its indication that what His Messenger commands must be obeyed in it, even if it is not specifically commanded in the Qur'an. The obedience to the Messenger is mentioned both alone and combined. So no one should imagine that what the Messenger commands, if it is not in the Qur'an, then obedience to it is not obligatory. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Soon a man, full-bellied, reclining on his couch, will be approached by a command from my commands, and he will say: 'Between us and you is the Book of Allah, the Exalted. Whatever we find in it we follow.' Indeed, I have been given the Book and its like along with it."

[The Obedience of Those in Authority]

As for those in authority, the obedience to any one of them is not obligatory except when it falls under the obedience to the Messenger, not as independent obedience in its own right. As is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The Muslim must hear and obey in what he likes and dislikes, so long as he is not commanded to disobey Allah the Exalted. If he is commanded to disobey Allah the Exalted, there is no hearing and no obedience."

Reflect how the repetition of this meaning is required by His saying: ﴿then refer it to Allah and the Messenger﴾, and He did not say "and to the Messenger." For referring to the Qur'an is referring to Allah and the Messenger. What Allah has judged is the very judgment of His Messenger, and what the Messenger (ﷺ) judges is the very judgment of Allah. So if you refer to Allah what you dispute, that is, in His Book, you have referred it to His Messenger. Likewise, if you refer it to His Messenger, you have referred it to Allah. This is one of the secrets of the Qur'an.

[Who Are Those of Authority?]

The report from Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, has differed concerning those of authority, and there are two narrations from him about them:
One: that they are the scholars. The second: that they are the rulers.

Both opinions are established from the Companions in the interpretation of the verse. The correct view is that it includes both categories together, for the scholars and the rulers are the guardians of the authority with which Allah sent His Messenger. The scholars are its guardians through preservation, explanation, defense of it, and refutation of whoever deviates from it and turns away from it. Allah has entrusted them with this, as He said: ﴿If these disbelieve in it, We have indeed entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it﴾.

What an entrustment that necessitates their obedience, the submission to their command, and people being followers of them. And the rulers are its guardians through diligent care, striving, enforcing it upon the people, and seizing the hand of whoever departs from it. These two categories are the people, and all of humankind is following them and their subjects.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you dispute over anything, then refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. This is clear proof that it is obligatory to refer the points of dispute, in everything about which people dispute of the whole religion, to Allah and His Messenger, and not to anyone other than Allah and His Messenger. So whoever refers the judgment to other than these two has opposed the command of Allah, and whoever calls, at the time of dispute, to a ruling other than that of Allah and His Messenger, has called with the claim of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). Thus the servant does not enter faith until he refers everything the disputants dispute to Allah and His Messenger. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿if you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. This is what we mentioned just before, that it is a condition, such that the conditioned is negated by the negation of the condition. This shows that whoever makes other than Allah and His Messenger the judge in matters of dispute has left the requirements of faith in Allah and the Last Day. And sufficient for you is this verse, which protects and breaks, as an explanation and cure, for it breaks the backs of those who oppose it, and protects those who hold fast to it and comply with what it commands.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That those who perish might perish upon clear evidence, and those who live might live upon clear evidence. And indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ [al-Anfal: 42].

The early generations (salaf) and the later ones (khalaf) have agreed that referring to Allah is referring to His Book, and referring to the Messenger is referring to him during his lifetime, and referring to his Sunnah after his death.

[The Happiness of Both Abodes]

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is better and more excellent in outcome﴾. That is: what I have commanded you, of obedience to Me and to My Messenger and to those in authority, and referring what you dispute to Me and to My Messenger, is better for you in your livelihood and your return. It is your happiness in both abodes, so it is better for you and more excellent in its consequence.

This indicates that obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and making Allah and His Messenger the judge, is the cause of happiness in the immediate and the eventual. Whoever reflects upon the world and the evils that occur in it will know that every evil in the world is caused by opposing the Messenger and departing from his obedience, and every good in the world is by means of obedience to the Messenger. Likewise, the evils of the Hereafter, its pains and punishments, are only among the requirements and consequences of opposing the Messenger. So the evils of this world and the Hereafter return to opposing the Messenger and what follows from it. If people had obeyed the Messenger with due obedience, there would never have been any evil on earth. This is as it is known in the general evils and calamities that befall the earth, so it is likewise with the evil, pain, and grief that afflict the servant in himself, for it is only due to opposing the Messenger. Moreover, his obedience is the fortress, whoever enters it is among the secure, and the cave, whoever takes refuge in it is among the saved.

Thus it is known that the evils of this world and the Hereafter are nothing but ignorance of what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought and departing from it. This is clear proof that there is no salvation for the servant and no happiness except by striving to know what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought in knowledge and acting upon it in deed.

[The Perfection of Happiness]

The perfection of this happiness is by two other matters:
One of them: calling people to it.
The second: his patience and striving in that call.

[Human Perfection]

Thus human perfection is confined to these four levels:
The first: knowledge of what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought.
The second: acting upon it.
The third: spreading it among people and calling them to it.
The fourth: patience and striving in conveying and implementing it.

Whoever aspires in his resolve to know what the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were upon, and wishes to follow them, then this is truly their path:
"If you wish to reach the people, then take their path, for it has become clear to the travelers, plainly visible."

[Referring to Allah and the Messenger Is a Requirement of Faith]

Among them: He made this referral one of the requirements and necessary consequences of faith. So when this referral is absent, faith is absent, by necessity, since the absence of the necessitated thing follows from the absence of its necessary consequence. This is especially so because the connection between these two matters is mutual, for each of them is negated by the negation of the other. Then He informed them that this referral is good for them, and that its outcome is the best outcome. Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that whoever seeks judgment from, or judges by, other than what the Messenger brought has made the taghut (that which is transgressed beyond its limit, whether worshipped, followed, or obeyed) a judge and sought its judgment. The taghut is everything by which a servant transgresses his limit, whether a deity, a leader, or one obeyed. So the taghut of every people is whoever they seek judgment from other than Allah and His Messenger, or whom they worship besides Allah, or whom they follow without insight from Allah, or whom they obey in what they do not know to be obedience to Allah. These are the taghuts of the world. If you reflect on them and on the conditions of people with them, you will see that most of them have swerved from the worship of Allah to the worship of the taghut, and from seeking judgment by Allah and His Messenger to seeking judgment by the taghut, and from obeying Him and following His Messenger to obeying and following the taghut. These people have not taken the path of the saved and successful of this Ummah, namely the Companions and those who followed them, nor have they aimed at their aim. Rather, they opposed them in both the path and the aim together.

Then Allah the Exalted informed about these people that when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," they turn away from that and do not respond to the caller, and they are content with the judgment of others. Then He threatened them that if a calamity befalls them in their minds, their religions, their insights, their bodies, and their wealth, because of their turning away from what the Messenger brought and their making others judges and seeking judgment from them, as He said: ﴿So if they turn away, know that Allah only intends to afflict them for some of their sins﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 49]. They make excuses that they only intended goodness and success, that is, by doing what pleases both sides and reconciles between them, as one does who seeks to reconcile what the Messenger brought with what opposes it, and claims that by this he is doing good and intending reform and reconciliation. Yet faith requires waging war between what the Messenger brought and everything that opposes it, whether in path, reality, creed, politics, or opinion. So faith permits this war, not reconciliation. And success is from Allah.

Then Allah, glorified is He, swore by Himself that faith is negated from the servants until they make His Messenger judge in everything that is disputed among them, small or great. And He did not suffice with this judgment alone as proof of their faith, until the tightness and constraint regarding his decision and his ruling is removed from their hearts. Nor did He suffice from them even with that, until they submit in full submission and yield in complete compliance.

And Allah said: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair﴾ [al-Ahzab: 36]. So He informed that it is not for a believer to choose after the decision of Allah and His Messenger, and whoever chooses after that has strayed into clear error.

[Section: The Jurists of Islam and Their Rank]

The second category: the jurists of Islam (fuqaha'), those whose fatwas revolve among people by their sayings, who were singled out for deriving rulings and who were concerned with fixing the principles of the lawful and the unlawful. They are on earth like the stars in the sky, by them the bewildered are guided in the darkness. The people's need of them is greater than their need of food and drink, and obedience to them is more obligatory upon them than obedience to mothers and fathers, by the explicit text of the Book. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those of authority among you. And if you dispute over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is better and more excellent in outcome﴾ [al-Nisa': 59]. 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, in one of the two narrations from him, and Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Dahhak, and Mujahid, in one of the two narrations from him, said: those of authority are the scholars. This is also one of the two narrations from Imam Ahmad.

Abu Hurayrah and Ibn 'Abbas in the other narration, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Suddi, and Muqatil said: they are the rulers. This is the second narration from Ahmad.

[The Obedience to Rulers Follows the Obedience to Scholars]

The verified view is that rulers are only obeyed when they command in accordance with knowledge. So their obedience follows the obedience to the scholars, for obedience is only in what is good and what knowledge has made obligatory. Just as the obedience of the scholars follows the obedience to the Messenger, so the obedience of the rulers follows the obedience to the scholars. Since the standing of Islam is by the two groups, the scholars and the rulers, and all people are followers of them, the righteousness of the world is by the righteousness of these two groups, and its corruption by their corruption. As 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak and others among the early generations said: "There are two categories of people: when they are righteous, people are righteous, and when they are corrupt, people are corrupt." It was said: "Who are they?" He said: "The rulers and the scholars." As 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said:

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 59 (part 2 of 7):

I have seen that sins kill the hearts,
and that persistence in them brings humiliation.
Leaving sins is the life of the hearts,
and for your soul, disobedience to them is best.
Has anything corrupted religion but kings
and evil rabbis and monks?

[The prohibition against saying, "This is the ruling of God"]

The Prophet ﷺ, in the authentic hadith, instructed his commander Buraydah that when he besieged an enemy, he should not bring them down to the ruling of God. He said: "You do not know whether you will hit upon the ruling of God regarding them or not. Rather, bring them down to your ruling and the ruling of your companions."

Consider how he distinguished between the ruling of God and the ruling of the commander who exercises ijtihad (independent legal reasoning, the mujtahid being the one who exercises it), and he forbade calling the ruling of the mujtahids the ruling of God.

From this: when a scribe wrote before the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, a ruling that he had issued, the scribe said, "This is what Allah has shown the Commander of the Faithful, Umar." He said: "Do not say it like that. Rather say: This is what the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, has seen."

Ibn Wahb said: I heard Malik say: "Among the affairs of the people, and among those who passed from our predecessors, and whom I encountered and whom I follow, none would say about anything, 'This is halal, and this is haram.' They did not dare to do that. Rather they would say, 'We dislike this, and we see this as good; this should be done, and we do not see this.'" This was related from him by Atiq ibn Ya'qub, who added: "And they would not say halal or haram. Have you not heard the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered what Allah has sent down to you of provision, and you have made from it what is unlawful and lawful? Say: Did Allah permit you, or do you invent against Allah?﴾ [Yunus: 59]"

Halal is what Allah and His Messenger have made lawful, and haram is what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful.

[The term "karahah" (disliking) is applied to what is forbidden]
