The third is like the abstention of one whom neither knowledge, love nor hatred of the thing has ever occurred to, like the abstention of a sleeper or a child.

[Section: The Sunnah in Relation to the Qur'an Has Three Aspects]

The Sunnah (the Prophetic tradition) in relation to the Qur'an has three aspects. The first is that it agrees with the Qur'an in every respect, so that the Qur'an and the Sunnah both bear upon a single ruling, which is a case of evidences converging and reinforcing one another. The second is that it clarifies what is intended by the Qur'an and explains it. The third is that it establishes a ruling on which the Qur'an is silent, or prohibits what the Qur'an is silent about prohibiting. It does not go outside these categories, so it never contradicts the Qur'an in any way. Whatever of it exceeds the Qur'an is original legislation from the Prophet (ﷺ), and obedience to him in it is obligatory, and disobeying him is not permitted. This is not giving the Sunnah precedence over the Book of Allah, but rather carrying out what Allah has commanded regarding obedience to His Messenger. Had the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not been obeyed in this category, there would be no meaning to obeying him, and his distinctive obedience would be void. And if his obedience were obligatory only in what agrees with the Qur'an and not in what exceeds it, he would have no obedience that is specific to him. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 80]. How is it possible for any of the people of knowledge to refuse to accept a hadith that exceeds the Book of Allah? Thus the hadith prohibiting a man from marrying a woman together with her paternal aunt or her maternal aunt would not be accepted; nor the hadith on prohibition through nursing for everything prohibited by lineage; nor the hadith on the option of stipulation (khiyar al-shart); nor the hadiths on pre-emption (shuf'ah); nor the hadith on pledging a pawn (rahn) while resident, although it exceeds what is in the Qur'an; nor the hadith on the inheritance of the grandmother; nor the hadith on a slave woman who is freed while married to a husband, giving her the choice; nor the hadith prohibiting a menstruating woman from fasting and prayer; nor the hadith obligating expiation on one who has intercourse during the day in Ramadan; nor the hadiths on the mourning (ihdad) of a widow, despite their exceeding what the Qur'an mentions of the waiting period (iddah). Why then do you not say that these are abrogation (naskh) of the Qur'an, and that the Qur'an cannot be abrogated by the Sunnah? And how did you make the witr prayer obligatory, though it is a pure addition to the Qur'an, based on a disputed report? And how did you permit performing ablution with date-wine (nabidh al-tamr), based on a weak report, thereby adding to the Book of Allah? And how did you add to the Book of Allah by stipulating that the minimum dowry be ten dirhams, based on a report that is not at all sound, and this is a pure addition to the Qur'an?

The people have acted upon the hadith: "A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor a disbeliever from a Muslim," and it exceeds the Qur'an. All of them have acted upon the hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ) giving the granddaughter through a son one-sixth together with the daughter, and it exceeds what is in the Qur'an. The people have all acted upon the hadith on the ritual of istibra' (ascertaining that a captive woman is not pregnant) by one menstrual cycle, and it exceeds what is in the Book of Allah. They acted upon the hadith: "Whoever kills an enemy has his spoils (salab)," and it exceeds what the Qur'an says about the division of spoils. They all acted upon his (ﷺ) judgment, which exceeds what is in the Qur'an, that full siblings (of the same father and mother) inherit to the exclusion of half-siblings through the father (banu al-'allat); a man inherits from his brother who shares both parents to the exclusion of his brother who shares only the father. If we were to trace this, it would be very long. The Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is greater in our hearts, more magnificent, and more obligatory upon us, so that we must not refuse it when it exceeds what is in the Qur'an; rather, we accept it wholeheartedly. Likewise, it is obligatory upon the Ummah to act upon the judgment by a single witness together with the oath, even though it exceeds what is in the Qur'an. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the majority of the Successors (tabi'un), and the imams acted upon it. It is strange that someone would reject it on the grounds that it exceeds what is in the Book of Allah, and then rule by refusal to swear (nukul), and by the knots of ropes and the faces of bricks in a wall, none of which is in the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger. You, and the majority of the Ummah, have acted upon the hadith: "A father is not retaliated against for killing his child," despite its weakness, and it exceeds what is in the Qur'an. You and the people have acted upon the hadith on taking the jizyah (poll tax) from the Magians, and it exceeds what is in the Qur'an. You and the rest of the people have acted upon amputating the leg of a thief for a second offence, despite its exceeding what is in the Qur'an. You and the people have acted upon the hadith prohibiting retaliation for a wound before it has healed, and it exceeds what is in the Qur'an. The Ummah has acted upon the hadiths on custody (hadanah), and they are not in the Qur'an. You and the majority have acted upon the view that a widow observes her waiting period in her own dwelling, and it exceeds what is in the Qur'an. You and the people have acted upon the hadiths on reaching puberty by age and by the growth of hair, and they exceed what is in the Qur'an, since the Qur'an mentions only the wet dream (ihtilam). You and the people have acted upon the hadith: "Revenue comes with liability (al-kharaj bi'l-daman)," despite its weakness, and it exceeds what is in the Qur'an, and upon the hadith prohibiting the sale of debt for debt (bay' al-kali' bi'l-kali'), and it exceeds what is in the Qur'an. These are multiples upon multiples of what we have mentioned. Indeed, the rulings of the Sunnah that are not in the Qur'an, if they are not more numerous than those that are, are certainly not fewer. So if it were permissible for us to reject every Sunnah that exceeds the explicit text of the Qur'an, all the Sunnahs of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would be invalidated except for a Sunnah that the Qur'an indicates. This is what the Prophet (ﷺ) foretold would occur, and his report must come to pass.

[Types of Signification of the Sunnah That Exceeds the Qur'an]

If it is said: the Sunnahs that exceed what the Qur'an indicates are sometimes a clarification of it, sometimes establish a ruling that the Qur'an does not address, and sometimes change its ruling. Our dispute is not concerning the first two categories, for they are authoritative by consensus. The dispute is concerning the third category, which is what I have framed as the question of addition to the text.

Consider His the Exalted's words regarding the good intercession, ﴿he will have a share of it﴾, and regarding the evil intercession, ﴿he will have a portion of it﴾.

For the word kifl (portion, burden) carries the sense of bearing a load and weight, while the word naseeb (share) carries the sense of the portion of benefit that its seeker toils to obtain. Although each of the two is used for both matters when standing alone, yet when they are paired together, it is fitting that the portion of good be specified by naseeb and the portion of evil by kifl.

Al-Farra' said: "*Arkasahum* means he returned them to disbelief." Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is said *arkasta al-shay'* and *rakastuhu* (two dialect forms) when you return a thing." *Al-raks* is turning a thing upside down, or returning its beginning to its end. *Al-irtikas* is apostasy (*al-irtidad*).

Umayya said:

*So they were turned back into the fire of Hell, for they*
*were sinners, and they spoke falsehood and lies.*

From this root comes the word *al-raks* for animal dung, because it has been returned to a state of impurity. For this reason it is called *rajī'* (returned), and *al-raks*, *al-naks*, *al-markūs* and *al-mankūs* all have one meaning. Al-Zajjaj said: "*Arkasahum* means he overturned them and returned them." The meaning is that He returned them to the ruling of the disbelievers, with their humiliation and abasement.

Allah, glorified is He, informed of His judgment and decree concerning them and of His justice, and that their being returned was due to their earning and their deeds, as He said: ﴿Nay, rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts with rust﴾ (83:14). This is His monotheism and this is His justice, not what the Qadariyya and the Mu'attila say, that tawhid is the denial of the attributes, and justice and belief in predestination are denied.

Question: What is the wisdom in Allah giving His enemies power over His friends, so that they inflict a terrible torment on them?

Answer: Allah has in this empowerment many dazzling wisdoms, among them the attainment of what He loves: the servitude of patience, of striving (jihad), and of bearing harm for His sake, being content with it in ease and in hardship, and remaining steadfast in His worship and obedience despite the strength of the opposition, its dominance, and its might. Also among them is the purification (tamhis) of His friends from the judgments of human nature and the impulses of temperament, through their giving up their souls to Him, and through the harm His enemies inflict on them. And among them is the distinguishing of the truthful from the liar, and of the one who wills Him and worships Him in every state from the one who worships Him only on the edge (harf). Another is the attainment of the rank of martyrdom (shahada), which is among the highest ranks, and nothing is more pleasing to the Beloved than that one spend the love of one's soul in seeking His good pleasure and striving against His enemy. So in this empowerment there is much of Allah's blessing, mercy, and wisdom. If you wish to know this, reflect on the verses at the end of Al ʿImran, from His saying ﴿Indeed, there have passed before you precedents (sunan)﴾ to His saying ﴿It is only Satan who frightens you of his allies, so do not fear them but fear Me, if you are believers﴾, up to His saying ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾.

This distinguishing is among the wisdoms of that empowerment. Had it not been for that empowerment, the excellence of patience, forgiveness, forbearance, and the restraining of anger would not have appeared, nor would the sweetness of victory, triumph, and subjugation. Things are known by their opposites. And had it not been for that empowerment, the enemies would not have deserved destruction, humiliation, and subjugation. That empowerment brought forth from potential into actuality what was in His friends, so they deserved His honour, and what was in His enemies, so they deserved His punishment. Thus this empowerment manifested His wisdom, His might, His mercy, and His blessing toward both groups. And He is the Mighty, the Wise.

[Section: Is there any sin whose repentance is not accepted, or not?]

People have differed over whether there is any sin whose repentance is not accepted or not.

The majority said: repentance applies to every sin, so every sin one can repent from is accepted.

A group said: there is no repentance for the one who kills (al-qatil), and this is the well-known position of Ibn ʿAbbas, and one of the two narrations from Ahmad. His companions debated Ibn ʿAbbas on this, saying: Did not Allah the Exalted say in Surat al-Furqan ﴿And they do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾ [al-Furqan: 68]

up to His saying ﴿except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan: 70]. He said: This verse was about the Jahiliyyah. Some people among the polytheists had killed and committed adultery, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "What you call to is good; if only you would inform us that there is an expiation (kaffarah) for what we have done." So there was revealed ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ [al-Furqan: 68], the verse. So this one is about those people. As for the one in Surat an-Nisa', which is His saying ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding eternally therein; and Allah will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment﴾ [an-Nisa': 93].

So the man who knows Islam and its laws and then kills, his recompense is Hell.

Zayd ibn Thabit said: When the one in al-Furqan was revealed, ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ [al-Furqan: 68],

we were astonished at its leniency, and we remained seven months; then the stern verse came after the lenient one and abrogated the lenient one. By the stern one he meant this verse in Surat an-Nisa', and by the lenient one the verse of al-Furqan. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The verse of al-Furqan is Meccan, and the verse of an-Nisa' is Medinan; it was revealed and nothing abrogated it.

These people said: Also, repentance from intentionally killing a believer is impossible, since there is no way to it except by obtaining his pardon (istihlal) or returning his soul, which one has caused to be lost, to his body; for repentance from a right of the son of Adam is not valid except by one of these two, and both are impossible for the killer. So how can his repentance from a right of a human being be valid when it has not reached him and he has not obtained his pardon?

This is not objected to them regarding wealth, if its owner dies and one has not paid it to him, because one is able to deliver its equivalent to him through charity.

They said: And it is not objected to us that shirk is greater than killing, and repentance from it is valid; for that is purely a right of Allah, so repentance from it is possible. But the right of a human being, repentance is contingent upon paying it to him and obtaining his pardon, and this has become impossible.

The majority argued with His saying ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [az-Zumar: 53]. This is about the one who repents. And with His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa': 48]. This is about one who does not repent; for He distinguished between shirk and what is below it, and tied forgiveness to His will, thus specifying, and He tied [it]

while in the previous one He generalized and made it absolute.

They argued with His saying ﴿And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then is guided﴾ [Ta-Ha: 82].

So if this killer repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Forgiving to him.

They said: It has been authentically related from the Prophet ﷺ the hadith of the one who killed one hundred people and then repented, and his repentance benefited him, and he was joined to the righteous town to which he had set out. And it is authentically related from him ﷺ, from the hadith of ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said while around him a group of his companions: "Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill your children, nor bring a slander you invent between your hands and feet, nor disobey me in what is right. Whoever of you fulfils it, his reward is upon Allah; and whoever is afflicted with any of that and is punished for it in this world, it is an expiation for him; and whoever is afflicted with any of that and Allah conceals it for him, it is up to Allah: if He wills, He pardons him, and if He wills, He punishes him." So we pledged allegiance to him on that.

They said: The Prophet ﷺ has also said, relating from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He:

"O son of Adam, if you meet Me with the earth's fullness of sins, then meet Me without associating anything with Me, I will meet you with its fullness of forgiveness."

He ﷺ also said: "Whoever dies not associating anything with Allah enters Paradise."

And he said: "Whoever's last words are: There is no deity but Allah, enters Paradise."

And he said: "Indeed, Allah has forbidden the Fire to whoever says: There is no deity but Allah, seeking thereby the Face of Allah."

And in the hadith of intercession: "Bring out of the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith."

And in it Allah the Exalted says: "By My might and My majesty, I will surely bring out of the Fire whoever said: There is no deity but Allah."

And the textual evidences similar to these are numerous, indicating that none of the people of tawhid will remain eternally in the Fire.

They said: As for this verse in an-Nisa', it is like its counterparts among the texts of threat, such as His saying ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein eternally, and for him is a humiliating punishment﴾ [an-Nisa': 14];

and His saying ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Jinn: 23];

and His saying ﴿Indeed, those who consume the properties of orphans unjustly, they only consume into their bellies a fire, and they will burn in a blaze﴾ [an-Nisa': 10];

and His saying ﷺ: "Whoever kills himself with an iron object, his iron will be in his hand, stabbing himself with it, abiding eternally and forever in the Fire of Hell." And its counterparts are many.

People have differed regarding these texts in several ways:

One: holding to their apparent meaning and the eternal abiding of the perpetrators of these crimes in the Fire. This is the view of the Kharijites and the Mu'tazilah, though they then differed.

The Kharijites said: They are disbelievers, since none abides eternally in the Fire except a disbeliever. The Mu'tazilah said: They are not disbelievers, but sinners who abide eternally in the Fire. All of this is when they have not repented.

A group said: Rather, this threat concerns one who makes it lawful; for he is a disbeliever. As for one who commits it while believing it to be forbidden, this threat of eternal abiding does not reach him, though the threat of entering [the Fire] may reach him.

Imam Ahmad rejected this view and said: If he made it lawful and did not do it, he would be a disbeliever; but the Prophet ﷺ only said: "Whoever does such and such."

A third group said: The argument from these texts rests on the establishment of generality, and there are no general terms in the language; and from here whoever denied generality denied it. Their aim was to nullify these proofs from being used by the Mu'tazilah and the Kharijites. But that entails nullifying the Law entirely, indeed nullifying the generality of reports. These people rejected falsehood with what is more falsehood than it, and an innovation with what is uglier than it, and they were like one who intended to build a palace and so demolished a city.

A fourth group said: There is an implied element in the speech.

They said: Implication (idmar) is common and well known in their speech.

Then they differed about this implied element. One group said it is an implied condition, the sense being: "his recompense is such-and-such if He requites him, or if He wills."

A fifth group said it is an implied exception, the sense being: "his recompense is such-and-such unless He pardons." This is a claim for which there is absolutely no evidence in the speech, but its establishment is by an external matter outside the wording.

A sixth group said: This is a threat, and failing to carry out a threat is not blameworthy but praiseworthy; and it is permissible for Allah, the Exalted, to fail to carry out a threat, but it is not permissible for Him to fail to carry out a promise. The difference between them is that the threat is His right, so failing to carry it out is pardon, gift, and remission, and that is the requirement of His generosity, bounty, and benevolence; while the promise is a right He made binding upon Himself, and Allah does not break His promise.

They said: For this reason Ka'b ibn Zuhayr praised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he said:

"I was informed that the Messenger of Allah had threatened me, and pardon with the Messenger of Allah is hoped for."

Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd debated this issue. ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd said: "O Abu ʿAmr, Allah does not break His promise, and He has said ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ [an-Nisa': 93], the verse." Abu ʿAmr said to him: "Woe to you, O ʿAmr, you have come from non-Arabic [i.e., ignorance of Arabic usage]. The Arabs do not regard failing to carry out a threat as blame, but as generosity and nobility. Have you not heard the poet's saying:"

"The son of my paternal uncle is not frightened by my assault as long as I live, and he does not fear the force of one who threatens."

"Indeed, if I threaten him, or promise him, I am one who breaks my threat and fulfils my promise."

A seventh group said: These texts and what is like them, in which the cause of punishment is mentioned, [establish only that a thing is a cause and a requirement]; the existence of the requirement of a ruling does not necessitate its existence, for a ruling is only completed by the existence of its requirement and the absence of its impediment. The utmost of these texts is the information that such-and-such is a cause of punishment and a requirement for it; and proof has been established for mentioning impediments: some of them by consensus, and some by text. Repentance is an impediment by consensus; monotheism is an impediment by the mass-transmitted texts that cannot be repelled; great good deeds that erase are impediments; great calamities that expiate are impediments; and the establishment of prescribed punishments in this world is an impediment by text. There is no way to nullify these texts, so the texts must be applied from both sides.

From here arose the weighing between good deeds and evil deeds, considering the requirement of punishment and its impediment, and applying whichever is weightier.

They said: On this is built the welfare and corruption of both abodes, and on this is built the legal rulings and the decreed rulings; it is the requirement of the wisdom that runs through existence, and by it the causes and their effects are connected, in creation and in command. Allah, glorified is He, has made for every opposite an opposite that repels it and counters it, and the ruling is for the stronger of the two. Strength requires health and well-being, while corruption of morals and their excess prevent the nature from acting and strength from doing its work; the ruling is for the stronger of them. So too are the powers of medicines and diseases. The servant has within him a requirement for health and a requirement for ruin, and each prevents the other from full effect and counters it; when one prevails over the other and overpowers it, its effect is what takes place.

From here it is known that people are divided into those who enter Paradise and do not enter the Fire, and the reverse; and those who enter the Fire and then leave it, whose staying therein is according to what there is within them of the requirement of staying, in the swiftness of their exit and its slowness.

And one who has an illuminated insight sees through it all that Allah has informed of in His Book concerning the matter of the Return and its details, until it is as if he witnesses it with his own eye, and he knows that this is the requirement of His divinity, lordship, might, and wisdom, glorified is He, and that the opposite of that is impossible for Him, and attributing the opposite to Him is attributing to Him what does not befit Him. So the relation of that to his insight is like the relation of the sun and stars to his sight. This is the certainty of faith, and it is what burns evil deeds as fire burns firewood.

The person who has reached this station of faith cannot persist in evil deeds, even if they occur from him and become many, for the light of faith he possesses commands him to renew repentance at every moment, returning to Allah with each of his breaths. This is among the most beloved of creatures to Allah.

These are the principal ways of people regarding the texts of threat.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 95:

He, glorified is He, negated equality between the believers who sit back from jihad and those who strive in jihad. Then He informed that the strivers are preferred over those who sit back by a degree. Then He informed that He has preferred them over them by degrees.

The understanding of this verse has been problematic for some people, on the ground that the sitters-back over whom the strivers are preferred by degrees, if they are the same as the sitters-back over whom those with a harm (ulu al-darar) are preferred by degrees, are not those with a harm. Then the strivers would be better than the sitters-back absolutely. In that case, what is the reason for excepting those with a harm from the sitters-back, when they are not equal to the strivers in the first place? Then the ruling of the excepted and the excepted-from would be one.

This is the aspect of the difficulty.

We shall mention what removes the difficulty, by the praise of God. We say:

The readers differed over the grammatical case (i'rab) of "ghayr" (other than/not). It was read in the nominative and in the accusative, and both are in the Seven (readings), and it was read in the genitive in outside the Seven. This is the reading of Abu Haywa.

As for the accusative reading, it is on the basis of exception (istithna'), because "ghayr" takes in exception the case of the noun that follows "illa" (except), which is the accusative. This is the correct view.

A group said: its case is accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: "The sitters-back, not being those with a harm, are not equal" — that is, they are not equal in the state of their health, they and the strivers. But exception is more correct, for "ghayr" hardly occurs as a state in their speech except when it is annexed to an indefinite noun, like His saying, exalted is He: {So whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing} and His saying, mighty and majestic is He: "Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle, except what is recited to you, not lawful to hunt while you are in the state of pilgrimage (ghayr muhillī al-ṣayd)."

And His saying, ﷺ: "Welcome to the delegation, not shamed and not regretful" (marhaban bil-wafd ghayra khazaya wa la nadama).

If it is annexed to a definite noun, it follows what precedes it.

Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned anger (ghayri al-maghdubi 'alayhim)﴾

And if you said: "Welcome to the delegation, other than the shamed and the regretful," you would put "ghayr" in the genitive; this is the well-known usage in their speech.

The discussion concerns the non-definiteness of "ghayr" by annexation, and the goodness of its occurring as a state in that case, is another context.

As for the nominative reading: it is as an adjective (na't) for the sitters-back. This is the correct view.

Abu Ishaq and others said: it is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject, its estimate being: "Those who are not those with a harm."

What led him to this is his thinking that "ghayr" does not accept definiteness through annexation.

So it is not described as an adjective of a definite noun. And there is no proof for what he claimed on which to rely, except that "ghayr" has gone deep into indefiniteness, so it does not become definite by what is annexed to it.

The answer to this: when it falls between two opposites, there is no indefiniteness in it, since it specifies what it is annexed to.

As for the genitive reading: it also has two aspects.

One of them, which is the correct view, is that it is an adjective of "the believers."

The second, which is the view of al-Mubarrad, is that it is a substitute (badal) for it, on the basis that it is indefinite, so it is not described by a definite noun.

According to all the views, it conveys the meaning of exception, and that the negation of equality does not apply to what "ghayr" is annexed to.

His saying: {And God has preferred the strivers with their wealth and their selves over the sitters-back by a degree} clarifies the meaning of the negation of equality.

They said: The meaning is: God preferred the strivers over the sitters-back of those with a harm by one degree, because they are distinguished from them by striving with their persons and their wealth. Then He, glorified is He, informed that both groups are promised the good (al-husna), saying: {And to each God has promised the best} — that is, the striver and the sitter-back who is harmed, due to their sharing in faith.

They said: In this is evidence for the preference of the wealthy who spends over the poor. Because God informed that the striver with his wealth and self is better than the sitter-back, and He placed striving with wealth before striving with the self. As for the poor, He removed blame from him by His saying (9:92): {Nor [is there blame] upon those who came to you that you might provide them mounts, and you said, "I find not that upon which to mount you."}

So where is the station of one who was ruled to be preferred compared with the station of one from whom blame was removed?

They said: This is the ruling for the sitter-back who is one of those with a harm and for the striver.

As for the sitter-back who is not one of those with a harm:

In his commentary on the verse, Ibn al-Qayyim writes:

"His saying 'degrees' (darajat): it is said that it is in the accusative as a substitute (badal) for His saying 'a great reward.' It is also said that it is an emphasis (ta'kid) for it, though not with the same wording, since it is the same in meaning."

Qatada said: "It used to be said: Islam is a degree, emigration within Islam is a degree, jihad within emigration is a degree, and being killed in jihad is a degree."

Ibn Zayd said: "The degrees by which Allah preferred the mujahid over the one who sits back are seven, and they are those that Allah mentioned in Bara'ah (Surah al-Tawbah), when He says: ﴿That is because they are not afflicted with thirst, nor fatigue, nor hunger in the way of Allah, nor do they tread a path that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they inflict on an enemy any injury, but a righteous deed is written for them thereby. Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good﴾. That makes five.

Then He said: ﴿Nor do they spend any expenditure, small or large, nor do they cross a valley, but it is written for them﴾. Those are two more."

It is also said: "The degrees are seventy degrees, the distance between each two degrees being the gallop of a well-bred, trained horse for seventy years."

The correct view is that the degrees are those mentioned in the hadith of Abu Hurairah, which al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said:

"Whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger, establishes the prayer, and fasts Ramadan, it is truly a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise, whether he emigrates in the way of Allah or sits in his land in which he was born."

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not inform the people of this?"

He said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred degrees which Allah has prepared for those who strive in His way. Between every two degrees is as the distance between the heaven and the earth. So when you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth."

They said: "Allah, glorified is He, made the first preference only a single degree, and here He made it degrees, along with forgiveness and mercy. This indicates that He prefers [the mujahid] over those other than those with a legitimate excuse (ghayr uli al-darar)."

This is the statement of this view and its clarification.

However, it remains to be said: if the mujahidun are better than the qa'idun (those who stay behind) absolutely, it follows that a mujahid and a qa'id are never equal in any case, and then restricting the qa'idun to those who are not of those with a legitimate excuse would have no benefit. For the mujahidun and those qa'idun who have excuses are also not equal.

Furthermore, the qa'idun mentioned in the verse, over whom the preference is given, are those other than those with a legitimate excuse, not the qa'idun who are those with excuses. For their ruling is not mentioned in the verse; rather, He made an exception for them and clarified that the preference is over others. So the alif-lam in al-qa'idin (the sitters) is for a known reference (al-'ahd), and what is known is those other than those with legitimate excuses, not those who are excused.

Furthermore, a qa'id among the mujahidin who is prevented from jihad by a necessity has a reward like the mujahid's reward, as it is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When a servant falls ill or travels, there is written for him the deeds that he used to do while healthy and resident."

He (ﷺ) also said: "In Medina there are people whom you did not journey on any journey nor cross any valley except that they were with you." They said: "And they are in Medina?" He said: "And they are in Medina; excuse has held them back."

Accordingly, the correct position is that the verse indicates that those who sit back from jihad without a legitimate excuse are not equal to the mujahidun. It is silent about the ruling for the excused by the explicit wording, and its implicit meaning does not indicate their equality with the mujahidun. Rather, this category divides into those excused from among the people of jihad whose excuse overcame them and kept them back, whose intention was firm and whose capacity was not lacking, and only incapacity kept them back. This is what the texts of the Sharia require: that he has a reward like the mujahid's. This category is not covered by the ruling of the denial of equality.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 100:

Whenever the gnostic (al-'arif) strives in steadfastness (al-istiqamah), in calling to God, and in standing up to carry out His command, the enemy strives all the harder to incite the foolish against him. At this stage he has put on the coat of mail of war and has begun to fight the enemy of God, for God and with God. His servitude in this state is the servitude of the elect among the gnostics, and it is called the servitude of ragham (ʿubudiyyat al-muraghamah, the servitude of enraging the enemy). Only those of perfect insight take note of it. Nothing is more beloved to God than His friend's defiance of His enemy and his enraging him. God, glorified is He, has indicated this servitude in several places in His Book:

The first is His saying: ﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of God will find on earth many a refuge and abundance﴾. He called the emigrant who emigrates to the worship of God "muraghim" (one who enrages), by whom he enrages the enemy of God and his own enemy. God loves from His friend that he enrage His enemy and provoke him, as the Exalted said:

﴿That is because they are not afflicted by thirst, nor fatigue, nor hunger in the way of God, nor do they tread a path that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they inflict on an enemy any harm except that a righteous deed is recorded for them thereby. Indeed, God does not waste the reward of the doers of good﴾ [al-Tawbah: 120]. And the Exalted said, regarding the Messenger of God ﷺ and his followers: ﴿And their likeness in the Gospel is like a seed that sends out its shoot, then strengthens it, so it grows thick and stands upon its stalk, pleasing the sowers—that He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

So enraging the disbelievers is a goal that is beloved to the Lord and desired by Him. Therefore, conforming to Him in it is part of the perfection of servitude. The Prophet ﷺ prescribed for one who forgets in his prayer two prostrations, and said: "If his prayer was complete, the two would humble the nose of Satan" (kanatā turghimāni anfa al-shaytan). In another narration: "As an enraging of Satan" (targhiman lil-shaytan). He named them "al-Murghimatayn" (the two that enrage).

Whoever worships God by enraging His enemy has taken a full share of sincere truthfulness (al-siddiqiyyah), and in proportion to the servant's love for his Lord, his loyalty to Him, and his hostility toward His enemy, will be his share of this enraging. And for the sake of this enraging, strutting between the two ranks (in battle), and the proud strut at secret charity, where no one sees him except God, are praised, because of what they contain of humbling the enemy and of spending what one loves of oneself and one's wealth for God, mighty and majestic.

This is a door of servitude that only a few people know, and whoever has tasted its flavor and sweetness weeps over his earlier days.

And in God is the seeking of help, upon Him is reliance, and there is no power nor might except in God.

The one who holds this station, when he looks at Satan and notices him in a sin, enrages him with sincere repentance (al-tawbah al-nasuhah), and this enraging produces in him another servitude.

This is a sample of some of the subtle secrets of repentance. Do not treat it lightly, for perhaps you will never find it in any other work at all. To God belongs praise and grace, and with Him is success.

**Chapter: Is the prayer of one who prays alone, while able to pray in congregation, valid or not?**

This question rests on two foundations. The first is whether congregational prayer (salat al-jama'ah) is obligatory (fard) or a recommended practice (sunnah). If we say it is obligatory, then the second is whether it is a condition for the validity of the prayer, or whether the prayer is valid without it while the one who abandons it is sinful. These are two questions.

As for the first question: the jurists have differed on it. Those who held it to be obligatory include 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu 'Amr al-Awza'i, Abu Thawr, and Imam Ahmad according to the apparent position of his school. Al-Shafi'i also stated this in Mukhtasar al-Muzani, where he said: "As for congregation, I do not grant a concession to abandon it except for an excuse." Ibn al-Mundhir said in al-Awsat: "Mention of attending congregation for the blind, even if their homes are far from the mosque." This is evidence for it, since attending congregation is an obligation, not a recommendation. He then cited the hadith of Ibn Umm Maktum, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, between me and the mosque are palm trees and trees; is it permissible for me to pray in my house?" He said: "Do you hear the iqamah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then come to it."

Ibn al-Mundhir said: "Mention of the threat of hypocrisy upon those who abandon attending the 'isha' and fajr prayers in congregation." Then he said, within the chapter: "The reports mentioned indicate the obligation of congregational prayer upon one who has no excuse. Among what indicates this is his saying to Ibn Umm Maktum, who was blind: 'I do not find a concession for you.'"

So if the blind man has no concession, the sighted man is more deserving of having no concession.

He said: "In the Prophet's ﷺ concern to burn the houses of people who stayed away from prayer is the clearest proof of the obligation of congregational prayer, for it is not permissible that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ threaten one who stays away from a recommended act, or from what is not obligatory."

He said: "It is supported by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that a man left the mosque after the muezzin had called the adhan, and he said: 'As for this one, he has disobeyed Abu al-Qasim ﷺ.' If a person were free to abandon congregation or attend it, it would not be permissible to disobey one who stays away from what is not required of him to attend. Since Allah, exalted is His remembrance, commanded congregation in a state of fear, this shows that in a state of safety it is more binding. The reports mentioned in the chapters on concession for staying away from congregation for those with excuses indicate the obligation of congregation upon one who has no excuse. Had the state of excuse and the state without excuse been the same, there would be no meaning to granting concession to stay away in the chapters on excuses." The saying of the Prophet ﷺ also confirms the emphasis on the obligation of congregation: "Whoever hears the call and does not answer it, there is no prayer for him."

He then cited the hadith on this, and then said: Al-Shafi'i said: Allah mentioned the adhan for prayer, saying: ﴿And when you call to prayer﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:58]. And He said: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 62:9].

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ established the adhan for the obligatory prayers. Thus it resembles what I have described: it is not lawful for one to pray each obligatory prayer except in congregation, so that a group of residents or travelers does not fail to pray together in congregation. I do not grant a concession to one able to attend congregation to abandon it, except for an excuse. If someone stays away and prays alone, he is not required to repeat it, whether he prayed before or after the imam, except the Friday prayer: whoever prays it as dhuhr before the imam's prayer must repeat it, because attending it is obligatory. This is the whole of Ibn al-Mundhir's wording.

The Hanafis and Malikis said: it is a confirmed sunnah (sunnah mu'akkadah), but they regard the one who abandons confirmed sunnahs as sinful, while they validate the prayer without it. The dispute between them and those who say it is obligatory is verbal. Some of them explicitly stated obligation.

Those who hold it obligatory said: Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons. And when they have prostrated, let them be behind you, and let another group come who have not prayed and let them pray with you﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:102].

The argument from the verse proceeds in several respects:

The first: His command to them to pray in congregation, then He repeated this command a second time regarding the second group, by His saying: ﴿and let another group come who have not prayed and let them pray with you﴾.

This is evidence that congregation is an obligation upon each individual, since Allah did not drop it from the second group by the action of the first. Had congregation been a sunnah, the most deserving of its dropping would have been the excuse of fear. Had it been a collective obligation (fard kifayah), it would have been dropped by the action of the first group. So the verse is evidence of its obligation upon each individual. This therefore has three aspects: He commanded it first, then commanded it again, and He did not grant them a concession to abandon it in a state of fear.

(Benefit)

The obligation of congregation has been argued from the fact that combining the two prayers was legislated in rain for the sake of attaining congregation, even though one of the two prayers occurs outside its time, and the time is obligatory; so if the time was abandoned for it, congregation must be obligatory.

This was objected to on the ground that an obligation may be dropped for something non-obligatory, just as for what is not recommended: the half of the prayer is dropped for the sake of travel, leisure and trade, and washing the feet is dropped for wearing socks, and the best that can be said is that it is permissible.

This objection is unsound. The obligation of the traveler to shorten to two rak'ahs did not drop an obligation for a non-obligatory reason. Moreover, there is no problem in dropping an obligation for the sake of what is permissible, and that is not the issue. What is impossible is that a recommended matter in worship should be given precedence in a way that entails the loss of an obligation, and this is what we know of no precedent for in the Shari'ah at all. With this the answer to the dropping of washing the feet for the sake of socks is also clear.

It has also been argued for its obligation that Allah commanded it in the prayer of fear, which is the locus of relief, of the dropping of what is not dropped elsewhere, and of tolerating what is not tolerated elsewhere; so what then of the prayer of one who is safe and resident?

This was objected to on the ground that the purpose of fear-prayer is assembly: the aim is the gathering of Muslims, the display of their obedience, and the glorification of the symbols of their religion, especially when they were with the Prophet ﷺ. The aim was to show the enemy the obedience of the Muslims to him and their reverence for his station, such that in a state of fear, when no one stays with anyone, they follow him, do not separate from him, and do not leave him in any way. This is like what occurred with them during the 'Umrat al-Qada' with him, until 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud said:

"I have been received by the kings Chosroes and Caesar, but I have not seen a king whom his companions revere as Muhammad's companions revere him."

What shows this is that we see congregation dropped in rain that wets the sandals, and the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ caller would call: "Pray in your dwellings." Friday prayer is dropped out of fear of missing the bread in the oven, and dropped out of fear of meeting a creditor who would harm him, while congregation is a condition for it; and it is known that the excuse of war and facing the disbelievers is greater than all of this, yet its symbol was established in that state. This shows that the purpose is what we have mentioned.

I say: we do not deny that this is also a purpose, added to the purpose of congregation, so there is no contradiction between it and the obligation of congregation. Rather, if this is a sought-after matter, it is among the strongest indicators of the obligation of congregation in that state. This purpose is also present in the gathering of Muslims in prayer behind their imam, and in the causes of acts of worship: those acts were legislated and they persist and endure even after the causes of their legislation cease. This is like the ramal in tawaf and the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah.

(Section)

Allah, glorified is He, has mentioned in His Book the stories of the prophets and their followers, and how He saved them through patience and obedience. Then He said:
﴿Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for people of understanding.﴾ [Yusuf: 111]
The complete discussion of this great matter becomes clear through beneficial, comprehensive principles.

The first: What afflicts the believers of evils, trials and harm is less than what afflicts the disbelievers. Reality bears witness to this.
Likewise, what afflicts the righteous in this world is far less than what afflicts the wicked, the sinners and the oppressors.

The second principle: What afflicts the believers for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, is accompanied by contentment (ridá) and seeking reward (ihtisab). If they lack contentment, their reliance is upon patience and seeking reward, and this lightens for them the weight of the trial and its burden, for whenever they witness the recompense, bearing hardships and afflictions becomes easy for them. The disbeliever has neither contentment nor seeking reward; and if he endures, his endurance is like that of animals. Allah, the Exalted, has alerted to this in His saying:
﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, then indeed they are suffering as you are suffering, but you hope from Allah what they do not hope.﴾ [al-Nisa': 104]
So they share in the pain, but the believers are distinguished by hoping for the reward and nearness from Allah, the Exalted.

The third principle: When the believer is harmed for the sake of Allah, it is borne for him in proportion to his obedience, his sincerity, and the presence of the realities of faith in his heart, to the extent that a harm which, if any part of it fell upon another, he would be unable to bear, is carried for him. This is from Allah's protection of His believing servant: He repels from him much of the trial, and if he must suffer some of it, its weight, its burden, its hardship and its consequence are lifted from him.

The fourth principle: The more love takes root and becomes firmly established in the heart, the harm suffered by the lover in pleasing his Beloved becomes sweet and not resented, and lovers take pride in this before their beloved, to the point that one of them said:
"Though it grieves me that you have touched me with harm,
It gladdens me that I have come to your mind."
So what then is the thought regarding the love of the Supreme Beloved, whose testing of His beloved is mercy from Him and kindness towards him?

The fifth principle: What the disbeliever, the wicked and the hypocrite obtain of might, victory and rank is far less than what the believers obtain; rather, its inner reality is humiliation, breakdown and disgrace, even if outwardly it appears otherwise.

The sixth principle: The believer's trial is like a medicine for him, which extracts from him the diseases which, if they remained within him, would destroy him, or diminish his reward and lower his rank. Trial and testing extract those diseases from him and prepare him for complete reward and elevated station. It is known that the existence of this is better for the believer than its absence, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, Allah does not decree for the believer any decree except that it is good for him, and this is only for the believer: if prosperity befalls him, he gives thanks, and it is good for him; and if adversity befalls him, he is patient, and it is good for him."
Thus this trial and testing are part of his victory, his might and his well-being. For this reason the people most severely tested are the prophets, then those nearest to them, and so on. A person is tested according to his religion: if his religion is firm, the trial is intensified upon him; if his religion is weak, it is lightened for him. Trial does not cease to befall the believer until he walks upon the earth with no sin upon him.

The seventh principle: What befalls the believer in this abode, such as his enemy gaining dominance over him, overpowering him, and harming him at times, is a necessary matter, unavoidable. It is like intense heat, intense cold, sicknesses, worries and griefs. This is a necessity inherent in the nature and creation of man in this abode, even for children and animals, as dictated by the wisdom of the Most Wise of judges. If good in this world were stripped of evil, benefit of harm, and pleasure of pain, it would be a different world and a different creation from this one, and the wisdom for which good and evil, pain and pleasure, beneficial and harmful were mixed together would be lost. The separation of one from the other and their distinction will occur only in another abode, not this one, as Allah, the Exalted, said:
﴿That Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good and place the wicked some of them upon others, heaping them all together, and put them into Hell. Those are the losers.﴾ [al-Anfal: 37]

The eighth principle: The trial of the believers by their enemy's domination over them, subjugation, and defeat of them at times contains a great wisdom which none knows in detail except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
Among it: the drawing forth of their servitude, humility and submission to Allah, their brokenness before Him, their need of Him, and their asking Him for victory over their enemies. Had they been always victorious, dominant and triumphant, they would have become arrogant and haughty; and had they been always subdued, defeated, with their enemy victorious over them, the religion would not have stood and the truth would have had no dominion. So the wisdom of the Most Wise of judges required that He alternate them between victory at one time and being defeated at another. When they are defeated, they humble themselves to their Lord, turn to Him, submit to Him, are broken before Him and repent to Him; and when they are victorious, they establish His religion and its rites, enjoin good, forbid evil, strive against His enemy, and support His allies.
Among it: that had they always been victorious, dominant and conquering, there would have joined them those whose aim is not religion and following the Messenger, for one attaches himself only to the one who holds dominance and honour. Had they always been defeated and subdued, no one would have joined them. So the divine wisdom required that dominance be theirs at one time and against them at another. Thereby is distinguished between those who desire Allah and His Messenger, and those who have no aim except the world and rank.
Among it: that He, glorified is He, loves from His servants the perfecting of their servitude in ease and hardship, in health and trial, and in His giving them dominance and their being dominated. For Allah, glorified is He, the servants have a servitude in both states, according to what each state requires, which is attained only through it, and the heart is not set right without it, just as the bodies are not made right except through heat and cold, hunger, thirst and fatigue, and their opposites. Thus these tribulations and afflictions are a condition for the attainment of human perfection and the required uprightness, and the existence of the necessitated thing without its necessity is impossible.
Among it: that testing them through their enemy's domination over them purifies them, refines them and cleanses them, as Allah, the Exalted, said regarding the wisdom behind the disbelievers' domination over the believers at the Battle of Uhud:
﴿So do not weaken and do not grieve, and you will be superior if you are believers. If a wound has touched you, indeed a wound has touched the people like it. And these days We alternate among the people, that Allah may make evident those who believe and take from among you martyrs, and Allah does not like wrongdoers. And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers. Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who fought and made evident the patient? And you had certainly wished for death before you encountered it; and you have seen it while you were looking on. And Muhammad is not but a messenger; messengers have passed on before him. So if he should die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all; and Allah will reward the grateful.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 139–144]
So He mentioned kinds of wisdom for the sake of which the disbelievers were given dominance over them, after He had steadied them, strengthened them, and given them the good news that they would be superior by the faith they had been given, and consoled them that though the wound touched them in obedience to Him and His Messenger, it had also touched their enemies in enmity to Him and His Messenger.
Then He informed them that by His wisdom He makes the days alternate among the people, so each of them receives his share of them, like provisions and terms of life.
Then He informed them that He did this so that He might make evident those among them who believe, while He, glorified is He, is All-Knowing of everything before its occurrence and after its occurrence; but He willed to make them known to themselves as existing and witnessed, so that He would know their faith as an actuality.
Then He informed that He loves to take martyrs from among them, for martyrdom is a lofty degree with Him and an exalted station, attained only by being killed in His cause. Had the enemy not gained dominance, the degree of martyrdom, which is among the things most beloved to Him and most beneficial to the servant, would not have been attained.
Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that He wills to purify the believers, i.e., to cleanse them of their sins through repentance, returning to Him, and seeking His forgiveness for the sins for which the enemy gained dominance over them; and that, along with that, He wills to destroy the disbelievers through their transgression, tyranny and aggression when they are victorious.
Then He denounced their presumption and their thought that they would enter Paradise without striving and patience. His wisdom refuses that; they will not enter it except through striving and patience. Had they always been victorious and dominant, no one would have fought them, and they would not have been tested with what they must endure of their enemies' harm. This is some of His wisdom in giving their enemy victory over them and His giving them dominance at times.

The ninth principle: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, created the heavens and the earth, created death and life, and adorned the earth with what is upon it only to test His servants and examine them, to know who desires Him and desires what is with Him, from among those who desire the world and its adornment.
He, the Exalted, said:
﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water, that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed.﴾ [Hud: 7]
And He said: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed.﴾ [al-Kahf: 7]
And He said: ﴿He who created death and life that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed.﴾ [al-Mulk: 2]
And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial; and to Us you will be returned.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 35]
And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and the patient, and We will test your reports.﴾ [Muhammad: 31]
And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do the people think they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tested? And We had certainly tested those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 1–3]
So when messengers are sent to people, they are faced with two matters: either one of them says, "I have believed," or he does not believe but continues in misdeeds and disbelief. And the testing of both is inevitable.
As for the one who says, "I have believed," his Lord will surely test and try him, so it becomes evident whether he is truthful in his saying, "I have believed," or a liar. If he is a liar, he turns back on his heels and flees from the test as he flees from the punishment of Allah. If he is truthful, he remains firm in his word, and the trial and testing increase him only in faith upon his faith.
Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly." And it increased them only in faith and submission.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 22]
As for the one who does not believe, he will be tested in the Hereafter with punishment, and he will be afflicted by it, and that is the greater of the two trials, if he is spared being tested with the punishment of this world and its calamities and its penalties which Allah inflicted upon those who did not follow His messengers and disobeyed them. So there is inevitably a trial in this abode, in the barzakh, and on the Day of Resurrection for everyone; but the believer has a lighter trial and an easier affliction, for Allah repels from him through faith, bears for him through it, and grants him of patience, steadfastness, contentment and submission what makes his trial easy for him. As for the disbeliever, the hypocrite and the wicked, their trial is intensified, their affliction is severe and lasting; the believer's trial is light and cut off, while the trial of the disbeliever, the hypocrite and the wicked is severe and continuous.
So pain and trial inevitably befall every soul, whether it believes or disbelieves; but the believer experiences pain in this world at the outset, and then he has the outcome of this world and the Hereafter; while the disbeliever, the hypocrite and the wicked experience pleasure and bliss at the outset, and then they proceed to pain. Thus no one should hope to be entirely free from love and pain. To clarify this:

The tenth principle: Man is by nature civil (madani), he must live with people, and people have wills, perceptions and beliefs, so they ask him to agree with them upon them. If he does not agree with them, they harm and torment him; and if he agrees with them, harm and torment come to him from another direction. So he cannot dispense with people and mixing with them, and he cannot be free of agreeing or disagreeing with them. In agreement there is pain and torment if it is upon falsehood; and in disagreement there is pain and torment if he does not follow their desires, beliefs and wills. And there is no doubt that the pain of disagreeing with them in their falsehood is easier than the pain that follows from agreeing with them.
Consider this with those who ask him to agree to an injustice, an indecency, false testimony, or assistance in something forbidden. If he does not agree with them, they harm, wrong and oppose him; but he has the outcome and victory over them if he is patient and God-fearing. If he agrees with them to flee the pain of disagreement, what follows from that pain is greater than what he fled from; and generally they will be empowered over him, so he will suffer from them pain many times over the pleasure he initially gained by agreeing with them.
So knowing this and observing it is among the most beneficial things for the servant: a small pain that results in a great and lasting pleasure is more deserving of bearing than a small pleasure that results in a great and lasting pain. And success is in the hand of Allah.

The eleventh principle: The affliction that befalls the servant for the sake of Allah does not fall outside four categories.
It is either in his self, or in his wealth, or in his honour, or in his family and those he loves.
That which is in his self may be by its destruction at times, and by its suffering without destruction at others. This is the sum of what the servant is tested with for Allah.
The most severe of these categories is the calamity to the self.
It is known that all creatures die, and the utmost this believer can hope for is to be martyred for Allah, and that is the most noble and easiest of deaths. The martyr feels no pain except like the pinch of an ant-bite, so there is no calamity in the killing of the martyr beyond what is customary for the children of Adam.
Whoever considers the calamity of this killing greater than the calamity of dying on one's bed is ignorant. Rather, the death of the martyr is among the easiest, most excellent and most exalted deaths. But the one who flees thinks that by fleeing his life will be prolonged, so that he enjoys living; but Allah, glorified is He, has refuted this assumption, saying:
﴿Say, "Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 16]
So Allah informed that fleeing from death through martyrdom does not benefit; there is no use in it, and that even if it benefited, it would benefit only a little, since death is necessary for him, and he would lose by this little something better than it and more beneficial than the life of the martyr with his Lord.
Then He said: ﴿Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm or intends for you mercy? And they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 17]
So Allah, glorified is He, informed that no one can protect the servant from Allah if He intends for him harm other than the death from which he fled; for death is what he disliked, and Allah informed that if He intended for him a harm other than that, no one could protect him from Allah; and that he may flee from what displeases him, the killing in the cause of Allah, and thereby fall into what displeases him more greatly.
If this is the case with the calamity to the self, the matter is likewise with the calamity to wealth, honour and body. For whoever withholds his wealth from spending it in the cause of Allah, the Exalted, and exalting His word, Allah will strip him of it, or will assign to him spending it in what benefits him neither in this world nor the next, but rather in what returns to him with harm, immediately and eventually. And if he holds it back and hoards it, Allah prevents him from enjoying it and transfers it to another. So its pleasantness goes to another, and its burden falls on him who leaves it behind.
Likewise, whoever pampers his body and honour and prefers his comfort over toil for Allah and in His cause, Allah, glorified is He, will make him toil many times over in other than His cause and His pleasure. This is a matter people know through experience.
Abu Hazim said: "What the one who does not fear Allah encounters of dealing with creatures is greater than what the one who fears Allah encounters of dealing with piety."
Consider this in the case of Iblis. He refused to prostrate to Adam, fleeing from submitting to him and being humiliated, and sought to exalt himself; so Allah made him the most abased of the abased, and made him a servant to the people of wickedness and debauchery among his descendants. He was not content to prostrate to Adam, yet was content to serve, he and his offspring, the wicked among his progeny.
Likewise the idol-worshippers: they disdained to follow a messenger from among the humans, and to worship one God, glorified is He, and they were content to worship gods of stone.

And likewise, whoever refuses to humble himself before Allah, or to spend his wealth seeking His pleasure, or to exhaust his soul and body in obedience to Him and seeking His pleasure, will be punished for it, as one of the early pious predecessors (salaf) said:
"Whoever refuses to walk a few steps with his brother in the latter's need, Allah will make him walk more than those steps in matters other than His obedience."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 113:

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿He gives wisdom (al-hikmah) to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good.﴾

And He said concerning the Messiah, peace be upon him: ﴿And He will teach him the Book and wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel.﴾

Wisdom (al-hikmah) in the Book of Allah is of two kinds: wisdom mentioned on its own, and wisdom mentioned alongside the Book. As for wisdom mentioned on its own, it has been explained as prophethood, and it has been explained as knowledge of the Qur'an.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It is knowledge of the Qur'an, its abrogating and abrogated verses (naskh), its clear and ambiguous verses (muhkam and mutashabih), its earlier and later revealed parts, its lawful and unlawful matters, and its parables.

Al-Dahhak said: It is the Qur'an and understanding of it.

Mujahid said: It is the Qur'an, knowledge, and jurisprudence (fiqh). In another narration from him: It is being correct in speech and action.

Al-Nakha'i said: It is the meanings of things and understanding them.

Al-Hasan said: It is scrupulousness (wara') in the religion of Allah. It seems that he explained it by its fruit and its requirement.

As for wisdom mentioned alongside the Book, it is the Sunnah. This is what al-Shafi'i and other imams said.

It has been said: It is judgment by revelation. Explaining it as the Sunnah is more general and more well known.

The best of what has been said about wisdom is the saying of Mujahid and Malik: that it is knowing the truth and acting upon it, and being correct in speech and action.

This cannot be achieved except through understanding the Qur'an and comprehension (fiqh) of the laws of Islam and the realities of faith.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 119:

Al-Dahhak said: "*mafrudan* means known (*ma'lumen*)."

Al-Zajjaj said: "That is, a portion that I have prescribed for myself."

Al-Farra' said: "It means what He has given him (Iblis) authority over from among the people, so it is as if it were prescribed (*mafrud*)."

I say: The real meaning of *fard* (prescription) is determination (*taqdir*). The meaning is that whoever follows Satan and obeys him belongs to his prescribed portion and his apportioned share. Everyone who obeys the enemy of Allah is among his prescribed portion. So people are of two kinds: the portion and prescribed share of Satan, and the friends of Allah, His party and His chosen ones.

His words ﴿and I will mislead them﴾ mean from the truth. ﴿And I will beguile them﴾: Ibn Abbas said: "He means obstructing repentance and delaying it."

Al-Kalbi said: "I will beguile them by telling them there is no Paradise, no Fire, and no Resurrection."

Al-Zajjaj said: "Along with misleading them, he combines this by making them imagine that they will still obtain their share of the Hereafter."

It has been said: "*La-umanniyannahum* means the mounting of desires that call to disobedience and innovations."

It has been said: "*Umanniyuhum* means long life in the bliss of this world. He lengthens their hope in it so that they prefer it over the Hereafter."

His words: ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely slit the ears of the cattle﴾ [al-Nisa': 119].

*Al-batk* means cutting. In this context it means slitting the ears of the *bahira* (a she-camel whose ear was slit and released), according to all the exegetes (*mufassirun*). From here, the majority of scholars disliked piercing the ears of an infant for earrings, and some permitted it for girls but not for boys, because girls need adornment. They cited the hadith of Umm Zar', in which she says: "He gave me ornaments of my ears."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "I am to you like Abu Zar' was to Umm Zar'."

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, explicitly stated the permissibility of this for a girl and its disliked status for a boy.

His words: ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely alter the creation of Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 119].

Ibn Abbas said: "He means the religion of Allah."

This is also the view of Ibrahim, Mujahid, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The meaning of this is that Allah, the Exalted, created His servants upon the upright *fitrah* (natural disposition), which is the religion of Islam, as He said: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind. There is no altering of the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know. [Turn] in repentance to Him and fear Him﴾ [al-Rum: 30-31].

For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah. Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a perfect animal. Do you see any mutilation in it? [Mutilation occurs] until you yourselves slit its ears."

Then Abu Hurayrah recited: ﴿the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind﴾ [al-Rum: 30], to the end of the verse. (Agreed upon.)

So the Prophet ﷺ combined both matters: altering the fitrah by Judaizing and Christianizing, and altering the creation by mutilation. These are the two matters that Iblis declared he would certainly alter. He altered the fitrah of Allah through disbelief, which is the alteration of the creation upon which they were created, and he altered the form through mutilation and slitting. So they altered the fitrah into polytheism and the creation into slitting and cutting. This is the alteration of the creation of the spirit, and this is the alteration of the creation of the form.

Then He said: ﴿He promises them and beguiles them﴾. His promise reaches the heart of a person, such as: "Your life will be long, you will obtain your fill of this world, you will rise above your peers, you will triumph over your enemies, and the worldly turns of fortune will be yours just as they were for others." His hope is lengthened, and he promises them good on account of their shirk and sins, and he gives them false wishes in their various forms. The difference between his promise and his beguiling is that the promise concerns good, while the beguiling concerns desire and will. So he promises them falsehood that has no reality, which is delusion (*ghurur*), and he gives them wishes for what has no outcome. Whoever reflects on the states of most people will find them attached to his promise and his beguiling, while they do not realize that he promises falsehood and gives false hopes. The base soul that has no worth feeds on his promise and his beguiling, as the poet said:

"A wish, if it is true, is the best of wishes, and if not, we have lived by it for a time in comfort."

So the base and wretched soul delights in false wishes and false promises, and rejoices in them, just as women and children rejoice in them and are moved by them. False statements originate from the promise and beguiling of Satan, for Satan gives their proponents the wish of attaining the truth and reaching it, and promises them arrival at it without its path. So every falsifier has a share in His words: ﴿He promises them and beguiles them, and Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾.

[Section: Sins bring the servant under the curse of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ]

Among them: sins bring the servant under the curse of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He cursed for sins, and others that are greater than them, so the one who commits them is more deserving of being under the curse.

He cursed the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed, the woman who joins hair (with extensions) and the one who has it joined, the woman who plucks eyebrows and the one who has them plucked, and the woman who files teeth for beauty and the one who has them filed.

He cursed the one who consumes usury, the one who feeds it, its writer, and its witness.

He cursed the one who performs a *tahlil* marriage (a marriage contracted to make a divorced woman lawful to her former husband) and the one for whom it is performed.

He cursed the thief.

He cursed the drinker of wine, its server, its presser, the one who has it pressed, its seller and buyer, the one who consumes its price, its carrier, and the one to whom it is carried.

He cursed the one who alters the boundary markers of the land, which are its signs and limits.

He cursed the one who curses his parents.

He cursed the one who takes a living thing as a target to shoot at with an arrow.

He cursed effeminate men and masculine women.

He cursed the one who slaughters for other than Allah.

He cursed the one who commits an offense or shelters an offender.

He cursed the makers of images.

He cursed the one who does the deed of the people of Lot.

He cursed the one who curses his father and mother.

He cursed the one who misleads a blind man from the road.

He cursed the one who has intercourse with an animal.

He cursed the one who brands an animal on its face.

He cursed the one who harms a Muslim or deceives him.

He cursed the women who visit graves, and those who take mosques and lamps upon them.

He cursed the one who corrupts a woman against her husband, or a slave against his master.

He cursed the one who has anal intercourse with a woman.

He informed that a woman who spends the night abandoning her husband's bed, the angels curse her until morning.

He cursed the one who claims lineage to other than his father.

He informed that the one who points at his brother with an iron tool, the angels curse him.

He cursed the one who curses the Companions.

Whom Allah has cursed.

Allah has cursed the one who spreads corruption on the earth, severs his kinship ties, and harms Him and His Messenger ﷺ.

He cursed the one who conceals what Allah, glorified is He, has sent down of clear proofs and guidance.

He cursed those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women of unchastity.

He cursed the one who makes the path of the disbeliever more guided than the path of the Muslim.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the man who wears the dress of a woman, and the woman who wears the dress of a man.

He cursed the briber, the one who takes the bribe, and the *ra'ish*, who is the intermediary in bribery.

He cursed for other things besides these.

So if there were in committing such acts nothing but the approval of the one who commits them of being among those cursed by Allah, His Messenger, and His angels, that alone would be enough to call one to abandon them.

Among them: deprivation of the supplication of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the supplication of the angels. Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Prophet to ask forgiveness for the believing men and women, and He said: ﴿Those who carry the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blaze. Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them, and whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. Indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And protect them from evil deeds; and whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day, You have had mercy upon him. And that is the great attainment"﴾ [Ghafir: 7-9].

This is the supplication of the angels for the believers who repent, who follow His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and who have no way other than these two. So no one other than these may hope for the answer to this supplication, since he has not characterized himself with the qualities of the one for whom it is made. And Allah is the One sought for help.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 4, verse 125:**

As for *khullah* (intimate friendship), it is the *tawhid al-mahabbah* (the unity of love). The *khalil* (intimate friend) is one whose love is singled out for his Beloved. This is a rank that does not admit of sharing, and for this reason two men in the world were singled out for it: Ibrahim and Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them both, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah took Ibrahim as an intimate friend﴾.

It is authentically related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Indeed Allah has taken me as an intimate friend just as He took Ibrahim as an intimate friend."
