And in the Sahih, from him: "If I were to take an intimate friend from among the people of the earth, I would have taken Abu Bakr as my intimate friend. But your companion is the intimate friend of the Most Merciful." Also in the Sahih: "Indeed I disown before Allah every intimate friend of his friendship."

Since *khullah* is a rank that admits of no sharing, Allah the Exalted tested Ibrahim, the intimate friend, by ordering him to slaughter his son, when a portion of his heart had gone to him. Allah wanted to purify that portion for Himself, so that it would belong to no one else. He tested him by slaughtering his son, and the intended slaughter was the slaughter of the heart, not slaughter with a knife. When the two of them submitted to the command of Allah and he placed the love of Allah above the love of his son, the station of *khullah* was made pure, and the son was ransomed with a great sacrifice. It has also been said that it was named *khullah* because love permeates (*takhallul*) all parts of the spirit. The poet said:

*"You have penetrated the pathway of my spirit,*
*and thus the Khalil was named Khalil."*

The word *khalil* is used for both masculine and feminine, because in origin it is a verbal noun (*masdar*) of your saying *khallahu*, meaning friendship (*khullah*) and close companionship (*khulluwah*). The poet said:

*"Let my friend Jabir be told*
*that your friend has not been killed."*

Its plural is *khilal*, like *qullah* and *qilal*. *Al-khall* means affection and a friend. *Al-khilal* is also a verbal noun meaning *al-khullah*, and from it is His saying the Exalted: ﴿There is no trading in it, nor any intimate friendship﴾ [Ibrahim: 31]. In the other verse He said: ﴿There is no trading in it, nor any friendship﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 254]. Imru' al-Qays said:

*"And I am not one who is weary of friendship, nor one who is forsaken."*

*Al-khalil* is the close friend, its feminine is *khalilah*. *Al-khalalah*, *al-khalalah* and *al-khalalah*, with the *kha'* vowelled with kasra, fatha or damma, all mean friendship and affection. The poet said:

*"How can one keep in contact with one whose friendship has become like that of Abu Marhab?"*

Some who have no knowledge have supposed that the beloved (*habib*) is superior to the intimate friend (*khalil*), and they say: Muhammad is the beloved of Allah, and Ibrahim is the intimate friend of Allah. This is false for many reasons. Among them: *khullah* is particular, while *mahabbah* (love) is general, for Allah loves those who turn in repentance and loves those who purify themselves. He also said of His believing servants: ﴿He loves them and they love Him﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 54].

Among them: the Prophet ﷺ denied that he had any intimate friend among the people of the earth, and he informed that the most beloved of women to him was Aisha, and among men her father. Among them: he said, "Indeed Allah has taken me as an intimate friend just as He took Ibrahim as an intimate friend." Among them: he said, "If I were to take an intimate friend from among the people of the earth, I would have taken Abu Bakr as my intimate friend, but (what binds us is) the brotherhood and affection of Islam."

**[Section: Love and Intimate Friendship]**

As for what some of the deluded suppose, that love (*mahabbah*) is more complete than intimate friendship (*khullah*), and that Ibrahim is the intimate friend of Allah while Muhammad is the beloved of Allah, this comes from their ignorance. Love is general, while intimate friendship is particular, and intimate friendship is the utmost degree of love. The Prophet ﷺ informed that Allah had taken him as an intimate friend just as He had taken Ibrahim as an intimate friend, and he denied that he had any intimate friend other than his Lord, while he also informed of his love for Aisha, her father, Umar ibn al-Khattab and others.

Also, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed Allah loves those who turn often (in repentance) and He loves those who purify themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 222].

And: ﴿Allah loves those who are patient﴾ [Al-Imran: 146].

And: ﴿Allah loves the good-doers﴾ [Al-Imran: 148].

And: ﴿Allah loves those who act justly﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 42].

The young man who repents is a beloved of Allah, but intimate friendship is particular to the two intimate friends. This claim arises only from a lack of knowledge and understanding of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

**(Chapter: On the mention of Ibrahim, the Intimate Friend of the Most Merciful ﷺ)**

This name is of the pattern mentioned earlier, for *Ibrahim* in Syriac means "a merciful father." Allah the Exalted made Ibrahim the third father of the world, for our first father is Adam, the second father is Nuh, and all the people of the earth are from his progeny, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And We made his progeny the survivors﴾ [As-Saffat: 77].

By this the lie of the fabricators among the non-Arabs (*'ajam*) becomes clear, those who claim that they do not know Nuh or his son, and do not trace their lineage to him, and who trace their kings back to Adam without mentioning Nuh in their genealogies. Allah the Mighty and Majestic has refuted them in this.

So the third father is the father of fathers, the pillar of the world, and the imam of the *hunafa'* (upright monotheists), whom Allah the Exalted took as an intimate friend, and placed prophethood and the Book in his progeny. He is the Intimate Friend of the Most Merciful and the elder of the prophets, as the Prophet ﷺ named him. When he entered the Ka'bah, he found that the polytheists had painted in it the images of himself and his son Isma'il, while they were casting divining arrows. He said: "May Allah destroy them! They knew that our Shaykh never sought decision by divining arrows." Allah the Exalted did not command His Messenger ﷺ to follow the religion of any prophet except him, so He said: ﴿Then We revealed to you, "Follow the religion of Ibrahim, a *hanif*, and he was not of the polytheists"﴾ [An-Nahl: 123].

And He commanded his community to do the same, so He said: ﴿He has chosen you and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion, the religion of your father Ibrahim. He named you "the Muslims" before (this)﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78]. The word *millata* (religion) is in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning: follow and hold fast to the religion of your father Ibrahim. What indicates the omitted verb is what precedes it: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78]. This is what is called *al-igra'* (urging). It has also been said that it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (*masdar*), and its governing element is the meaning of what came before it.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to instruct his companions that when they reached the morning and when they reached the evening, they should say:

"We have entered the morning upon the *fitrah* of Islam, the word of sincerity (*ikhlas*), the religion of our Prophet Muhammad, and the religion of our father Ibrahim, a *hanif*, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists."

Consider how these words make the *fitrah* belong to Islam, for it is the *fitrah* of Allah upon which He created mankind. The word of sincerity is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. The religion (*millah*) is that of Ibrahim, for he is its possessor, and it is *tawhid* and the worship of Allah alone, with no partner, and loving Him above every love. The religion (*din*) is that of the Prophet ﷺ, which is his perfect religion and his complete law, comprising all of that.

Allah named him imam, *ummah*, *qanit* and *hanif*. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when his Lord tested Ibrahim with words, and he fulfilled them, He said, "Indeed I will make you an imam for the people." He said, "And from my descendants?" He said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 124].

So He informed that He made him an imam for the people, and that the wrongdoer among his descendants does not attain the rank of imamate. The wrongdoer is the polytheist. He informed that His covenant of imamate is not attained by those who associate partners with Him. He also said: ﴿Indeed Ibrahim was an *ummah*, devoutly obedient to Allah, a *hanif*, and he was not of the polytheists, grateful for His favours. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and in the Hereafter he is surely among the righteous﴾ [An-Nahl: 120-122].

So the *ummah* is the exemplar, the teacher of good. The *qanit* is the one who is obedient to Allah and constant in His obedience. The *hanif* is the one who turns towards Allah and turns away from all else. Whoever explained *hanif* as "inclining" has not explained it by the literal meaning of the word, but by its necessary implication, for *al-hanaf* is turning, and whoever turns towards something inclines away from other things. In the case of the feet, *al-hanaf* is when one foot turns towards the other, and it necessarily implies its inclining away from its direction.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So set your face towards the religion as a *hanif*, the *fitrah* of Allah upon which He created mankind﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30].

So "*hanifan*" (as a *hanif*) is a state (*hal*) that establishes the content of His saying: ﴿set your face towards the religion﴾.

For this reason *hanif* has been explained as "sincere (*mukhlis*)", and the verse thus includes truthfulness and sincerity. For setting the face towards the religion is singling out its pursuit such that no desire for anything else remains in the heart. The one who is *hanif* and singled out does not desire anything other than Him. Truthfulness is that your pursuit is not divided, and singling out is that your object of pursuit is not divided. The first is the unity of the seeking, and the second is the unity of the sought.

The point is that Ibrahim, upon him be peace, is our third father, he is the imam of the *hunafa'*, and the People of the Book call him the pillar of the world. All the followers of religions agree on honouring him, loving him and being loyal to him, and the best of his progeny was the master of the descendants of Adam, Muhammad ﷺ, who revered him, exalted him, honoured him and respected him.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Mukhtar ibn Falfal, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O best of creation!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "That is Ibrahim," and he named him by his title, as mentioned earlier.

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed you will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised." Then he recited: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us; indeed We will do it﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 104]. "The first to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Ibrahim."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most resembling of all creation to him, as in the two Sahihs, where he said: "I saw Ibrahim, and the closest of people in resemblance to him is your companion," meaning himself ﷺ.

In another wording: "As for Ibrahim, look at your companion."

The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge for the two sons of his daughter, Hasan and Husayn, with the same formula that Ibrahim used for Isma'il and Ishaq.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and he would say: "Indeed your father used to seek refuge for them, Isma'il and Ishaq: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from every devil, every poisonous creature, and every evil eye.'"

The Prophet ﷺ was the first to host the guest, the first to be circumcised, and the first to see grey hair. He said, "What is this, O Lord?" He said, "Dignity." He said, "O Lord, increase me in dignity."

Allah the Exalted has testified that he fulfilled what he was commanded, as He said: ﴿Has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Musa and of Ibrahim, who fulfilled (his trust)?﴾ [An-Najm: 36-37].

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: "He fulfilled all the laws of Islam, and fulfilled what he was commanded regarding conveying the message."

And He the Exalted said: ﴿And when his Lord tested Ibrahim with words, and he fulfilled them, He said, "Indeed I will make you an imam for the people"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 124].

So when he completed what he was commanded of the words, Allah made him an imam for all creation, to be followed by them.

The Prophet ﷺ, as it has been said, had a heart for the Merciful, a son for the sacrifice, a body for the fires, and wealth for the guests.

When his Lord took him as an intimate friend, and *khullah* is the perfection of love, a rank that does not admit of sharing or competition, he had asked his Lord to grant him a righteous son, and He granted him Isma'il. This son took a portion of his heart, and the Intimate Friend became jealous over the heart of his intimate friend, that there should be any place in it for another. So He tested him by slaughtering him, to manifest the secret of *khullah* in his preferring the love of his Intimate Friend over the love of his son. When he submitted to the command of his Lord and resolved to carry it out, and the authority of *khullah* appeared in his proceeding to slaughter the son, preferring the love of his Intimate Friend over his own love, Allah abrogated (*naskh*, abrogation) that command for him and ransomed him with a great sacrifice. This is because the benefit of the slaughter lay in the resolve and the readiness of the soul to do what was commanded. When this benefit was achieved, the slaughter became a corruption, so it was abrogated in his case. Thus the sacrifices and offerings, the gifts and sacrificial animals, became a sunnah among his followers until the Day of Resurrection.

It was he who opened to the community the door of debating the polytheists and the people of falsehood, and breaking their arguments.

Allah the Exalted mentioned his debates in the Qur'an, with the leader of the deniers (*mu'attilin*), and his debate with his polytheist people, and the breaking of the arguments of both groups with the finest debate and the one closest to understanding and to the attainment of knowledge.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that was Our argument, which We gave to Ibrahim against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will﴾ [Al-An'am: 83].

Zayd ibn Aslam and others said: "By the argument and knowledge."

When the enemies of Allah were overcome by him through argument, and his argument became manifest over them, and he broke their idols, breaking their arguments and their deity, they resolved to punish him and throw him into the fire. This is the way of falsifiers: when they are overcome and the proof is established against them, they resort to punishment, as Pharaoh said to Musa, upon him be peace, when Musa had established the proof against him: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 29]. Then they kindled a fire for him and threw him into the catapult. That journey was one of the greatest journeys he undertook, and the most blessed for him, for he never undertook a journey more blessed, greater, or more elevating to his station, or more pleasing to his eye than it. During that journey Jibril appeared to him between the heaven and the earth and said: "O Ibrahim, do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no."

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it increased them in faith, and they said, "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs"﴾ [Al-Imran: 173]: "Your Prophet said it, and Ibrahim said it when he was thrown into the fire, and Allah the Exalted made the fire cool and safe for him."

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Umm Sharik, that the Prophet ﷺ ordered the killing of the gecko and said: "It used to blow on Ibrahim."

It was he who built the House of Allah and proclaimed to the people the pilgrimage. So every one who makes the pilgrimage (*hajj*) or the lesser pilgrimage (*'umrah*) gains for Ibrahim an increase in the reward and honour of Allah, in proportion to the number of pilgrims and those performing *'umrah*.

(Benefit)

Abu 'Umar, the client (ghulam) of Shu'bah, said: Abu Musa asked Abu al-'Abbas, meaning Tha'lab, whether there is a difference between "yatafarraqan" and "yaftariqan."

He said: "Yes. Ibn al-A'rabi related to us from al-Mufaddal, who said: It is said iftaraqa in reference to speech, and tafarraqa in reference to bodies."

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah 4, verse 135:

This verse contains great secrets, some of which must be pointed out because of the great need for them.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow your desires, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse to give it, then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.﴾

So He, glory be to Him, commanded standing firm in justice, which is fairness, in this verse. This is a command to uphold it toward every person, whether an enemy or a friend. Most deserving of what the servant stands for with sincere intent are statements, opinions and doctrines, since they are connected to the command and report of God.

Standing for them by following desire and disobedience opposes the command of God and contradicts what His Messenger was sent with.

Standing for them with justice is the duty of the Messenger's successors in his community and his trustees among his followers. The name of trustworthiness is deserved only by one who stands in them with pure justice, sincerely for God, His Book, His Messenger and His servants. Those are the true inheritors, not one who makes his companions, sect and school the criterion of truth and its measure, opposing whoever differs from him and loyal to whoever agrees with him merely by agreement or disagreement. How far is this from standing in justice, which God has made obligatory on everyone!

In this matter, its obligation is greater and its duty more emphatic.

Then He said: ﴿witnesses for Allah﴾. The witness is the one who informs. If he informs of the truth, he is a just, acceptable witness; if he informs of falsehood, he is a false witness. God, the Exalted, commanded that one be a witness for Him together with standing in justice. This implies that the testimony should be in justice, and that it should be for God, not for other than Him. In the other verse He said: ﴿Be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice﴾ (5:8). So the two verses include four matters:

First: standing in justice.
Second: that it be for God.
Third: testimony in justice.
Fourth: that it be for God.

Surah al-Nisa' embraced justice and testimony for God, and Surah al-Ma'idah embraced standing for God and testimony in justice, for a wondrous secret of the Qur'an whose place is not here.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives﴾. He commanded that justice be upheld and testimony given against everyone, even if that person is the most beloved to the servant. So he stands in justice against himself, his parents, who are his origin, and his relatives, who are closest to him, and a friend among the rest of people. If what the servant has of love for himself, his parents and relatives prevents him from standing against them with the truth, especially when the truth is for one who hates and opposes him before them, then he will not stand for it in this situation except one for whom God and His Messenger are more beloved than everything else. By this the servant is tested in his faith, so he knows the rank of faith in his heart and its place in it. The opposite of this is the servant's justice toward his enemies and those who treat him harshly. His hatred of them should not lead him to deviate against them, just as his love for himself, parents and relatives should not lead him to abandon standing against them in justice. That hatred should not draw him into falsehood, and that love should not keep him from truth. As the early generation said: "The just person is one whom his anger does not drive into falsehood, and whose contentment does not take him out of the truth."

The two verses include these two rulings: standing in justice and bearing witness to it against friends and enemies alike.

Then He said: ﴿Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both﴾, meaning: He is their Lord and Master, and they are His servants, just as you are His servants. So do not favor the rich for his wealth, nor the poor for his poverty, for Allah is more worthy of both than you are.

It may also be said that there is another meaning better than this: that they might fear standing in justice and giving testimony regarding the rich and the poor. As for the rich, out of fear for his wealth; as for the poor, because he has nothing, so souls become lax in standing against him with the truth. So it was said to them: Allah is more worthy of the rich and the poor than you are, He knows this and is more merciful to this, so do not abandon giving the truth and testimony regarding the rich or the poor.

Then He said: ﴿So do not follow your desires lest you not be just﴾. He forbade them from following desire, which drives one to abandon justice. His saying ﴿lest you not be just﴾ is in the accusative of place because it is an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi). Its estimate according to the Basrans is: out of aversion to being just, or fearing to be just, so that your following of desire is aversion to justice or flight from it. According to the Kufans, the estimate is: lest you not be just. The Basran view is better and clearer.

Then He said: ﴿And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse to give it, then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted﴾. He mentioned the two causes that necessitate concealing the truth, warning against them and threatening them:

The first: distortion (al-lay). The second: refusal (al-i'rad). When the proof of the truth becomes manifest and one who wants to repel it finds no way to repel it, he turns away from it and withholds mention of it, and so becomes a mute devil. Other times he twists it and alters it. Al-lay is an example of twisting, which is alteration, and it is of two kinds: twisting in wording and twisting in meaning. Twisting in wording is to utter it in a way that does not necessitate the truth, either by adding a word, omitting one, or replacing it with another, or by twisting in the manner of its delivery, giving the listener a wording while intending something else, as the Jews used to twist their tongues with the greeting upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and others. This is one of the two kinds of twisting.

The second kind is twisting of meaning, which is distorting it and interpreting the wording contrary to what the speaker intended, through ignorance attributing to it what he did not intend, or dropping part of what he intended, and similar twisting of meanings. So God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse to give it, then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted﴾.

Since the witness is required to give testimony in its proper form, neither concealing it nor altering it, refusal is the counterpart of concealment, and distortion is the counterpart of altering and changing it. So reflect on the treasures of knowledge beneath this verse.

The aim is this: the obligation without which faith is not complete, indeed without which the name of faith is not attained, is to receive the texts with acceptance, submission and proclamation, and to call people to them, and not to meet them sometimes with objection and other times with distortion.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 142:

Frequent remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is a safeguard against hypocrisy (nifaq), for the hypocrites remember Allah only rarely. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said about the hypocrites: ﴿And they do not remember Allah except a little﴾.

Ka'b said: "Whoever remembers Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, often is free of hypocrisy." For this reason, and Allah knows best, Allah, Exalted is He, closed Surah al-Munafiqun with His words: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers﴾.

In this there is a warning against the trial (fitnah) of the hypocrites, who were heedless of the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and so fell into hypocrisy.

Some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were asked about the Khawarij (the seceding sect): "Are they hypocrites?" He said: "No. The hypocrites do not remember Allah except a little."

So rare remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is a sign of hypocrisy, and frequent remembrance of Him is a safeguard against hypocrisy. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is too generous to afflict a heart that remembers Him with hypocrisy. It is only hearts that have become heedless of the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that are so afflicted.

[Section: The one who adorns himself with what is not in him, and his punishment]

As for his saying (ﷺ): "Whoever adorns himself with what is not in him, Allah will disgrace him": since the one who adorns himself with what is not in him is the opposite of the sincere person, for he displays to the people a matter whose inner reality is contrary to it, Allah deals with him in the opposite of his intention. Punishment by the opposite of one's intention is established both by the Law (shar') and by Divine decree (qadar). And since the sincere person is hastened, as a reward for his sincerity, the sweetness, love, and awe in the hearts of the people, the one who adorns himself with what is not in him is hastened, as his punishment, to be disgraced among the people, because he disgraced his inner self before Allah. This requires the Most Beautiful Names of the Lord, His Sublime Attributes, and His wisdom in His decree and His law.

Furthermore, since whoever adorns himself before the people with what is not in him, such as humility, religiosity, devotion, knowledge, or other things, has set himself up to bear the requirements and demands of these qualities, he will inevitably be asked for them. When they are not found in him, he is exposed, and that disgraces him from the very direction in which he thought it would adorn him. Also, he concealed from the people what he displayed to Allah in contrary fashion, so Allah exposes to the people the faults he had concealed from them, as a recompense of the same kind as his deed. Some of the Companions used to say: "I seek refuge in Allah from the humility of hypocrisy." They said: "And what is the humility of hypocrisy?" He said: "That you see the body humble while the heart is not humble." The foundation and root of hypocrisy is adorning oneself before the people with what is not in the inner self of faith. Thus it is known that these two statements are derived from the speech of prophethood, and they are among the most beneficial of speech and the most healing for ailments, and they come from the words of the Commander of the Faithful.

[Section heading] The disobedient person misses the reward of the believers

Whoever misses the company of the believers and the excellent protection of Allah over them (for Allah defends those who believe), and misses every good that Allah has arranged in His Book for faith, which is about one hundred qualities, each one of which is better than the world and whatever is in it.

Among them is the great reward: ﴿And Allah will soon give the believers a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa': 146].

Among them is the defense against the evils of this world and the Hereafter: ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who believe﴾ [al-Hajj: 38].

Among them is the forgiveness sought for them by the bearers of the Throne: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise, believe in Him, and seek forgiveness for those who believe﴾ [Ghafir: 7].

Among them is Allah's loyalty toward them, and whoever Allah takes as an ally is not humiliated. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah is the Ally of those who believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257].

Among them is His command to His angels to strengthen them: ﴿When your Lord inspired the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who believe"﴾ [al-Anfal: 12].

Among them is that they have high ranks with their Lord, forgiveness, and a generous provision.

Among them is honour: ﴿Honour belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8].

Among them is Allah's companionship with the people of faith: ﴿And that Allah is with the believers﴾ [al-Anfal: 19].

Among them is elevation in this world and the Hereafter: ﴿Allah will raise those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 11].

Among them is that He gives them a double portion of His mercy, gives them a light by which they walk, and forgives their sins.

Among them is the affection that He, glory be to Him, places for them: He loves them and makes them beloved to His angels, His prophets, and His righteous servants.

Among them is their security from fear on the day when fear becomes severe: ﴿So whoever believes and does righteous deeds, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾ [al-An'am: 48].

Among them is that they are those upon whom favour has been bestowed, whom we are commanded to ask Allah to guide us to the path of, every day and night, seventeen times: ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾ (al-Fatihah: 6–7).

Among them is that the Qur'an is only guidance and healing for them: ﴿Say, "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing; and as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a distant place"﴾ [Fussilat: 44].

The point is that faith is the cause that brings every good, and every good in this world and the Hereafter has faith as its cause, while every evil in this world and the Hereafter has the absence of faith as its cause. How then can it be easy for a servant to commit something that takes him out of the circle of faith and bars him from it? However, he does not leave the circle of the general body of Muslims. If he persists in sins and insists upon them, it is feared that they will cover his heart with rust, and this will take him entirely out of Islam. For this reason the fear of the earlier generations (al-Salaf) was intense, as one of them said: "You fear sins, and I fear disbelief."

Consider His words, glorified is He: ﴿Why would Allah punish you if you are grateful and believe?﴾ and ﴿Allah is ever Appreciative and Knowing.﴾ See how, within this address, you find that His gratitude (shukr) rejects punishing His servants in vain, without any crime, just as it rejects wasting their striving for nothing. The Appreciative (al-Shakur) does not waste the reward of one who does good, nor punish one who does not do wrong.

This is also a refutation of those who claim that He burdens a person with what he cannot bear and then punishes him for what lies beyond his capacity, exalted is Allah far above that false assumption and vain supposition. His gratitude requires that He not punish the believing, grateful servant or waste his deeds, and this is among the necessary implications of this attribute. He is free of anything contrary to that, just as He is free of all defects and deficiencies that contradict His perfection, self-sufficiency and praiseworthiness.

Among His gratitude, glorified is He, is that He brings a servant out of the Fire for even the weight of an atom's worth of good, and does not waste this measure for him. Among His gratitude is also that when a servant of His takes a stand that pleases Him among people, He thanks him for it, raises his mention, and informs His angels and believing servants of it. Thus He thanked the believer of the family of Pharaoh for that stand and praised him for it, raising his mention among His servants. Likewise was His gratitude to the man of Ya-Sin for his stand and his call to it. So none is destroyed by it except one who is destroyed, for He is Forgiving and Appreciative: He forgives much of error and appreciates little of deed.

Since He is truly the Appreciative, the dearest of His creation to Him is the one who embodies the attribute of gratitude, just as the most hateful of His creation to Him is the one who abandons it and embodies its opposite. This is the case with His beautiful names: the dearest of His creation to Him is whoever embodies what they require, and the most hateful to Him is whoever embodies their opposites. For this reason He hates the ungrateful wrongdoer, the ignorant, the hard-hearted, the miser, the coward, the contemptible and the base. He is Beautiful and loves beauty; Knowing and loves the learned; Merciful and loves the merciful; Good and loves the good; Appreciative and loves the appreciative; Patient and loves the patient; Generous and loves the generous; Concealing and loves those who conceal; Powerful and blames incapacity.

The strong believer is more beloved to Him than the weak believer; Pardoning and loves pardon; Odd (al-Witr) and loves the odd. Everything He loves is among the effects of His names and attributes and their implications, and everything He hates is what opposes them and contradicts them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 148:

The well-known reading is ẓulima (ظلم), in the passive voice. On this basis there are two opinions regarding the exception.

The first: it is disjunctive (munqaṭi'), meaning "but whoever has been wronged." For when he complains about his wrongdoer and openly speaks of the wrong done to him, he is not sinful. The inclusion of this exception within the first statement under this view is clear, for the meaning of "Allah does not love such-and-such" is that He hates it and hates its doer, except for one who has been wronged, for his openly speaking out and complaining about his wrongdoer is permissible for him, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The one who is able to pay (a debt) justifies (the creditor's) censure and punishment."

So his "censure" (ʿirḍ) is the complaint of the rightful claimant about him, saying: "He wronged me, he delayed me, he withheld my right from me." And his "punishment" ('uqūbah) is the ruler's beating him until he pays what he owes, according to the more correct of the two opinions in the school of Aḥmad, and this is the view of Mālik.

It has also been said that the punishment is his imprisonment.

The second: it is connected (muttaṣil), and the "openly speaking evil" is his openly calling upon God to remove the harm from him and to take his right for him, or his complaining of that to the ruler so that he may take his right for him. On this basis, it is permissible to read the word as nominative (rafʿ) as a substitute (badal) for one of the elements implied by "openly speaking," meaning: Allah does not love that anyone openly speak evil except the one who has been wronged. It is also permissible to read it in the accusative (naṣb) as a substitute for "openly speaking," and the meaning is: except the openly speaking of one who has been wronged.

It was also read as "min ẓalama" with a fatḥah (on the ẓa and lām, i.e., active voice). On this reading, the exception is disjunctive only, meaning: but the wrongdoer openly speaks evil words.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 4, verse 157 (part 1 of 7):

Ibn al-Sarraj said: "When the exception is disjunctive (al-istithnā' al-munqaṭi', i.e., an exception whose excluded item does not belong to the category of what precedes it), the preceding statement that comes before *illā* ('except') must indicate what is excluded. On the first view, no supposition is needed, but on the second, a supposed element must be inserted. Let us mention examples of this.

The first example: God's words, ﴿They have no knowledge of it, except following conjecture﴾ [4:157]. Whoever does not require a supposed element treats it as an exception with an omitted antecedent (al-istithnā' al-mufarragh, i.e., an exception where the governing noun is absent), and the meaning is: 'What they have, or what belongs to them, is only the following of conjecture.' Following conjecture is not connected to knowledge at all. Whoever requires a supposed element says the meaning is: 'They have no awareness, except the following of conjecture.' Conjecture, although it is not included in knowledge in actuality, is included in it by supposition, since it is brought to mind by its mention and stands in its place in many contexts. So the wording implies it, and by this its inclusion and exclusion are valid. However, after this explanation, there is more to be said about it, for what is excluded is the *following* of conjecture, not conjecture itself, so it is not included in the excluded item either in actuality or by supposition. The best reading in my view is that the supposition is: 'They have no knowledge of it, so they follow it and cast themselves into it; they follow only conjecture.' Thus the following of conjecture is not an exception from knowledge; rather, it is an exception from what is meant by knowledge, and what is meant by it is following it. Reflect on this.

Scholars differed regarding God's words, ﴿but it was made to appear so to them﴾ [4:157]. It was said that the meaning is: 'But it was made to appear so to them, to those who crucified him, in that his likeness was cast upon another, so they crucified the likeness.'

It was also said that the meaning is: 'But it was made to appear so to the Christians,' that is, doubt arose for them concerning his affair, while they had no knowledge that he was neither killed nor crucified. When his enemies said that they had killed him and crucified him, and his being raised from the earth happened to coincide with this, doubt fell upon their affair, and the Christians confirmed their claim about his crucifixion, so that the infamy might be complete against them.

However it was, the Messiah, peace and blessings of God be upon him, was not killed and was not crucified, with a certainty that admits no doubt. Then, after his being raised, the disciples (al-Ḥawāriyyūn) spread out into the lands, upholding his religion and his method, calling the nations of the Children of Israel to the Oneness of God, His religion, and belief in His servant, His Messenger, and His Messiah. Many people entered his religion, some openly and some in secret: some well known and some concealed.

The enemies of God, the Jews, may God curse them, were extreme in severity and harm toward his companions and followers.

The students and followers of the Messiah met from the Jews and from the Romans severe hardship: killing, torture, displacement, imprisonment, and other things.

(A precious section)

If the one who reproaches the Muslims is from the nation of error, the worshippers of the cross and of painted images on walls and ceilings, then it is said to him: Is he not ashamed, whose religion's foundation, which he adheres to and believes in, is that the Lord of the heavens and the earth, blessed and exalted, descended from the seat of His majesty and His throne, entered the womb of a woman who eats, drinks, urinates and defecates, and so became joined to her belly, and remained there for nine months, struggling amid excrement, urine, and menstrual blood; then he came out into the swaddling clothes and the cradle, and whenever he cried his mother put her breast into his mouth; then he moved on to the schoolroom among the boys; then his affair ended with the Jews slapping his cheeks, slapping the back of his neck, spitting in his face, placing a crown of thorns on his head and a reed in his hand, in mockery of him and violation of his sanctity; then they brought him near to a wooden structure singled out for affliction, bound him to it, tied him with ropes, and nailed his hands and feet, while he cried out, wept, and begged for relief from the heat of the iron and the pain of the cross.

This is while, by their own claim, he is the One who created the heavens and the earth and apportioned provisions and lifetimes; yet His wisdom and mercy required that He enable His enemies over Himself, so that they could inflict upon Him what they inflicted, thereby deserving punishment and imprisonment in Hellfire, and so that He might ransom His prophets, messengers, and friends, bringing them out of the prison of Iblis. For the souls of Adam, Abraham, Noah, and all the prophets were, in their view, in the prison of Iblis in the Fire, until He freed them from his prison by enabling His enemies over His crucifixion.

As for their statement about Mary: they say that she is the mother of the Messiah, the son of God, in truth, and his real mother; that there is no mother of the son of God except her, that there is no mother for him other than her, and no father except God, and no father for him besides Him. They say God chose her for Himself, and for the birth of His child and son from among all women. Had she been like other women, she would have given birth only through men's intercourse with her, but she was distinguished from women in that she conceived the son of God and bore his son, who has no son in truth other than him, and no father besides Him. They say she is seated on the Throne, on the left of the Lord, the Exalted, the father of her son, while her son is on His right. The Christians call upon her and ask her for abundance of provision, health of body, long life, forgiveness of sins, and that she be for them, with her son and his father, whom most of them believe to be her husband, and they do not deny that about them, a protector, a support, a treasure, an intercessor, and a pillar. In their supplication they say:

"O Mother of God, intercede for us!"

They magnify her and elevate her above the angels and above all the prophets and messengers, and they ask her for what is asked of God: well-being, provision, and forgiveness.

To the point that the Jacobites say in their private invocation to her: "O Mary, O Mother of God, be for us a protector, a support, a treasure, and a pillar."

The Nestorians say: "O Mother of the Messiah, be for us likewise."

They say to the Jacobites: "Do not say 'O Mother of God'; say 'O Mother of the Messiah.'" The Jacobites replied to them: "The Messiah is God in truth, both for us and for you; so what difference is there between us and you in that?" But you wanted reconciliation with the Muslims and to approach them in Oneness.

Yet these vile, filthy people of this misguided nation believe that God, glory be to Him and exalted, chose Mary for Himself, and passed her over as a man passes over a woman.

An-Nazzam, after relating that about them, said: "They declare this openly before those they trust." Ibn al-Ikhshid also mentioned this about them in *al-Ma'ūna* (The Helper). He said: "To it they allude. Do you not see that they say: 'Whoever is not a father is barren, and barrenness is a defect and a flaw'?"

This is the statement of all of them, and to intercourse they allude. Whoever mixed with these people, associated with them, and was intimate with them, knows this from them.

This is their disbelief and their polytheism against the Lord of the worlds, and their insult to Him. For this reason one of the Rightly Guided Caliphs said about them: "Humiliate them but do not wrong them, for they have insulted God with an insult that no human has ever uttered."

The Prophet (ﷺ) related from his Lord in the authentic hadith that He said: "The son of Adam has insulted Me, and it was not for him to do so; and the son of Adam has denied Me, and it was not for him to do so. As for his insult to Me, it is his saying: 'God has taken a son,' while I am the One, the Eternal Refuge, who did not beget and was not begotten, and to whom no one is equal. As for his denial of Me, it is his saying: 'He will not bring me back as He originated me,' and the first creation is no easier for Me than its return."

Thus, if those who affirm God's Oneness (al-muwaḥḥidūn) were to commit every sin, do every ugly deed, and commit every act of disobedience, it would not amount to an atom's weight beside this great disbelief in the Lord of the worlds, their insult to Him in this manner, and their uttering of monstrous things about Him. What, then, is the assumption of this group regarding the Lord of the worlds, as to what He will do with them when they meet Him on the day when some faces will be white and some faces will be black, and the Messiah will be questioned before the witnesses while they listen: "O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" Then the Messiah will reply, denying them: "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul. Indeed You are the Knower of the unseen. I said to them only what You commanded me: 'Worship God, my Lord and your Lord.' I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are a witness over all things." [5:116–117]

(Section)

This is the root and foundation of their religion upon which it stands.

As for its branches and its laws, they oppose the Messiah in all of them, and most of that is by their own testimony and acknowledgment. But they refer it to the patriarchs (al-baṭārika) and bishops. The Messiah, peace and blessings of God be upon him, practiced purity, performed ritual washing from major impurity (janābah), and required the ritual bath of a menstruating woman. But the sects of the Christians hold that all of that is not obligatory, and that a person may rise from upon a woman's belly, urinate and defecate without touching water or cleaning himself, the urine and feces running down his leg and thigh, and pray in that state, and his prayer is valid and complete. Even if he defecates and urinates while praying, it does not harm him, let alone passing wind or breaking wind.

They also say that prayer with urine and excrement is better than prayer in purity, because in that state it is further from the prayer of the Muslims and the Jews, and closer to opposing the two communities.

They begin the prayer by making the sign of the cross between the eyes. This prayer is one from which the Lord of the worlds is free, and so is the Messiah and all the faithful disciples; for this resembles mockery more than worship. Far be it from the Messiah that this be his prayer or the prayer of any of the disciples.

The Messiah used to recite in his prayer what the prophets and the Children of Israel used to recite in their prayers from the Torah and the Psalms.

As for the sects of the Christians, they recite in their prayers words that were set to melody for them by those who lead them in prayer, moving in the manner of lamentation and songs, and they say: "This is the Qurban (Eucharist/liturgy) of So-and-so," attributing it to those who composed it for them.

They pray facing east, but the Messiah never prayed facing east at all. Until God took him, he prayed only toward Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), which was the qiblah of David and the prophets before him, and the qiblah of the Children of Israel.

The Messiah was circumcised and enjoined circumcision as Moses, Aaron, and the prophets before him had enjoined it.

The Messiah forbade the pig, cursed one who eats it, and was extreme in condemning it, and the Christians persist in that. Indeed, he was raised up to God and never ate of its flesh the weight of a barleycorn; yet the Christians draw near to God by eating it.

The Messiah never prescribed for them this fast which they observe, nor did he fast it once in his life, nor did any of his companions. The virgins did not fast during his lifetime, nor did he eat what they eat during fasting, nor did he forbid what they forbid. He did not abandon the Sabbath for a single day until he met God, nor did he ever take Sunday as a festival.

The Christians acknowledge that he exorcised Mary of Magdala, expelling seven devils from her, and that the devils said to him: "Where will you take refuge?" He said to them: "Enter this unclean beast," meaning the pig. This is the account of the Christians about him.

Yet they claim that the pig is among the purest, most beautiful, and most delicious of animals.

The Messiah followed, in slaughtered animals, marriage, divorce, and inheritance, the way of the prophets before him. Among the Christians there is no legal punishment in this world for one who fornicates, commits sodomy, or becomes drunk, ever, nor any punishment in the Hereafter, because the priest and the monk forgive them. So whenever one of them commits a sin, he gives the priest a gift and gives him a dirham or something else so that he will forgive him. If the wife of one of them sins, she spends the night with the priest so that he may purify her for him. When she leaves him and tells her husband that the priest has purified her, he accepts that from her and seeks blessing through it.

They acknowledge that the Messiah said: "I have come to you only to act upon the Torah and the commandments of the prophets before me. I have not come to abolish, but to fulfill. Heaven and earth passing away is easier for God than that I should abrogate any part of the law of Moses, and whoever abrogates any of it will be called an abrogator in the kingdom of heaven."

He and his companions continued thus until he departed from the world. He said to his companions: "Act as you have seen me act, enjoin upon the people what I have enjoined upon you, be with them as I was with you, and be for them as I was for you."

The companions of the Messiah remained upon this for nearly three hundred years after him. Then the people began to alter and change (the religion) and to draw close to people by what they desired and by what the Jews disliked, and to oppose the Jews by abandoning the religion of the Messiah and departing from it entirely. They saw that the Jews had said of the Messiah that he was a sorcerer and a charlatan, the son of fornication, so they said: he is the Ratam, and he is the son of God! They saw the Jews circumcising, so they abandoned circumcision! They saw them being excessive in purity, so they abandoned it entirely! They saw them avoiding eating with a menstruating woman and touching her, so they had intercourse with her themselves! They saw them prohibiting the pig, so they permitted it and made it an emblem of their religion. They saw them prohibiting many slaughtered animals and creatures, so they permitted what is less than the elephant down to the mosquito, and they said: eat what you wish and leave what you wish, there is no blame.

They saw them facing Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) in prayer, so they faced the East. They saw them forbidding God from abrogating a law He had enacted, so they permitted their bishops and patriarchs to abrogate whatever they wished, to permit whatever they wished, and to prohibit whatever they wished.

They saw them prohibiting the Sabbath and observing it, so they prohibited Sunday and permitted the Sabbath, while admitting that the Messiah used to glorify the Sabbath and observe it.

They saw them shunning the cross, for in the Torah that is in their hands it is written: cursed is whoever is hanged on a tree. The Christians acknowledge this, so they themselves worshipped the cross. Likewise, the Torah explicitly prohibits the pig, so they worshipped by eating it.

The Torah also commands circumcision, so they worshipped by abandoning it, even though the Christians acknowledge that the Messiah said to his companions: I have only come to you to act in accordance with the Torah and the commandments of the prophets before me, and I have not come to abrogate but to complete; and it is easier before God for the heavens to fall upon the earth than for me to abrogate anything of the law of Moses.

So the Christians proceeded to abrogate it law by law, out of spite and enmity toward the Jews. To this cause was added what is in their book known to them as Ifrakis (Acts).

(That a group of Christians went out from Bayt al-Maqdis and came to Antioch and other places in al-Sham, and they called the people to the true religion of the Messiah. They called them to act upon the Torah, to prohibit the slaughter of those who are not its people, to circumcision and observing the Sabbath, to prohibiting the pig, and to prohibiting what the Torah prohibited. This was hard for the nations, and they found it burdensome. So the Christians gathered at Bayt al-Maqdis and consulted on what they might devise against the nations, so that they would answer them to the religion of the Messiah and enter it. Their opinion agreed upon mixing with the nations, granting them concessions, associating and intermingling with them, eating their slaughtered animals, descending to their desires, adopting their manners, and establishing a law that would lie between the law of the Injil (Gospel) and what the nations followed. They composed a book on this. This is one of their great councils, for whenever they wished to introduce something they would gather a council, and they would fabricate upon it what they wished to introduce, until they gathered the council which no greater one ever gathered for them, in the time of Constantine the Roman, son of Helena the Harranite, the Fandaqite.)

In his time the religion of the Messiah was altered. It was he who established the innovated religion of Christianity, and upon which he stood and sat. Their number was about two thousand men. They framed a formulation and then rejected it and were not satisfied with it. Then three hundred and eighteen men of them gathered, whom the Christians call the Fathers, and they framed this formulation which they hold today. It is the root of roots for all their sects, and no one among them is a complete Christian without it. They call it Sanhudus (Synod), which means the Creed. Its wording is:

"We believe in God the Father, the one, creator of what is seen and what is not seen, and in the one Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the firstborn of his Father, not made, true God from true God, of the substance of his Father, by whose hand the worlds were perfected and the creator of every thing; who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and of Mary the virgin, and the virgin Mary conceived him; and he was seized and crucified in the days of Pilate the Roman, and died and was buried, and rose on the third day, as it is written, and ascended to heaven and sat at the right hand of his Father, and he is ready to come again to judge between the dead and the living; and we believe in the one Lord who proceeds from his Father, the spirit of his love, and in one baptism for the forgiveness of sins, and in one holy, apostolic, catholic church, and in the resurrection of our bodies, and in eternal life forever and ever."

In it they declared that the Messiah is Lord, that he is the Son of God, that he is his firstborn, that he has no son other than him, and that he is not made, meaning he is not a created servant but rather a Lord and Creator. He is true God, born and begotten from true God, equal to his Father in substance. By his hand the worlds were perfected, and this hand by which the worlds were perfected is, in their view, the very hand that tasted the heat of the nails, as they declared in their books. These are their words:

They said: our authority has said: the hand that the Jews nailed to the wood is the hand that kneaded the clay of Adam and created him, and it is the hand that spanned the heaven, and it is the hand that wrote the Torah for Moses. They said: they described the Jews' treatment of him, and these are their words: they slapped God and struck him on the head.

They said: in the prophecies about him, God is conceived by a virgin woman, bears him, and he is seized, crucified and killed.

They said: as for the Synod apart from the nations, seven hundred of the Fathers, who are the authorities, gathered upon it, and in it is: that Mary conceived God, bore him, nursed him, gave him drink and fed him.

They said: and with us, the Messiah is the son of Adam, and he is his Lord, Creator and Provider; and the son of his offspring Abraham, and his Lord, Creator and Provider; and the son of Israel, and his Lord, Creator and Provider; and the son of Mary, and her Lord, Creator and Provider.

They said: our scholars have said, and who is the authority for all our sects: Yasu' (Jesus), in the beginning was always the Word, and the Word was always God, and God is the Word. That one whom Mary bore, whom people saw and who was among them, is God, and he is the Son of God, and he is the Word of God.

These are their words. They said: the Eternal, Primordial, creator of the heavens and the earth, is the one whom people saw with their eyes and touched with their hands, and he is the one whom Mary conceived and who spoke to people from her womb, when he said to the blind man: do you believe in God? The blind man said: and who is he that I should believe in him? He said: he is the one speaking to you. He said: I believe in you, and he fell down prostrate.

They said: the one whom Mary conceived is God, the Son of God, and the Word of God. They said: he is the one who was born, suckled, weaned, seized, crucified, slapped, had his hands bound, was nailed in his face, died and was buried, and tasted the pain of the crucifixion, nailing and killing for the sake of the salvation of the Christians from their sins.

They said: according to our three sects, the Messiah is not a prophet nor a righteous servant, but rather he is the Lord of the prophets, their Creator, their sender, their dispatcher, their supporter, their confirmer, and the Lord of the angels.

They said: his mother is not with him in the sense of creation, management, kindness or aid, for she has no special status over other women or animals. Rather, he is with her by her conceiving him and the womb containing him. For this reason she was distinguished from all female animals, and her son was distinguished from all creation. Thus God and his son who came down from heaven, whom Mary conceived and bore, became one God, one Messiah, one Lord and one Creator, with no distinction between them, and the union between them is never annulled in any way: not in conception, nor in birth, nor in sleep, nor in sickness, nor in crucifixion, nor in death, nor in burial. Rather, he is united with him in the state of conception, so in that state he is one Messiah, one Creator, one God, one Lord; and in the state of birth it is likewise, and in the state of crucifixion and death it is likewise.

They said: among us are those who utter this meaning literally in their speech and expression, saying: Mary conceived God, bore God, God died. And among us are those who refrain from this expression because of its ugliness, but give its meaning and reality, saying: Mary conceived the Messiah in reality, bore the Messiah in reality, she is the mother of the Messiah in reality, the Messiah is God in reality, Lord in reality, Son of God in reality, and Word of God in reality; there is no son of God in reality other than him, and no father of the Messiah in reality except him.

They said: these agree in meaning with the one who says: he conceived God, bore God, God was killed, God was crucified and God was buried, even if they deny the wording and expression.

They said: we only refused this expression which our brothers used, lest it be supposed of us, when we say: conceived God, bore God, mother of God, that all this descended and happened to God who is the Father. Rather we say: all this happened and descended upon the Messiah, and the Messiah with us and with our sects is complete God from complete God, of the substance of his Father. So we and our brothers are in reality one thing, with no difference between us except in expression only. They said: this is the reality of our religion and our faith, and the Fathers and the authorities have said it before us, established it for us and paved the way for it, and they know the Messiah better than we do.

The Trinitarians, the worshippers of the cross, from first to last, do not differ that the Messiah is not a prophet nor a righteous servant, but rather he is true God from true God, of the substance of his Father, and he is complete God from complete God, and he is the creator of the heavens and the earth, of the first and the last, their provider, their giver of life, their giver of death, their resurrector from the graves, their gatherer, their reckoner, their rewarder and their punisher.

The Christians believe that the Father stripped himself of all his kingdom and gave it to his son, so he is the one who creates, provides, causes death, gives life, and manages the affairs of the heavens and the earth.

Do you not see them saying in their creed: the Son of God and firstborn of his Father, not made, up to their saying: by his hand the worlds were perfected and every thing was created, up to their saying: he is ready to come again at another time to judge between the dead and the living?

And they say in their prayers and supplications: you, O Messiah Jesus, give us life and cause us to die, provide for us and create our children, raise our bodies, resurrect us and recompense us.

All this contains their clear denial of the Messiah, even if their false assumptions make them think they believe him. For the Messiah said to them: indeed God is my Lord and your Lord, and my God and your God.

So he testified against himself that he is a servant of God, a created and fashioned being, just as they are, and that he is like them in servitude, need and dependence upon God, exalted is He.

He also mentioned that he is the Messenger of God to his creation, just as He sent the prophets before him.

In the Gospel of John, the Messiah said in his supplication: eternal life is only due to people by their testifying that you are the one true God, and that you sent Jesus the Messiah.

This is the reality of the testimony of the Muslims: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God. He also said to the Children of Israel: but you want to kill me, and I am a man who told you the truth which I heard from God. Thus he mentioned his limit, that he is a man who conveyed to them what God said, and he did not say: and I am a god or a son of a god in the sense of begetting. He said: I have not come to act by my own will, but by the will of the one who sent me. He said: the words you hear from me are not mine, but are of the one who sent me. Woe to me if I say anything of my own accord, but only by the will of the one who sent me.

He used to continue worship with prayer and fasting, and he said: I did not come to be served, but to serve. Thus he placed himself in the station in which God placed him, which is the station of servants of God. He said: I do not judge the servants by their deeds, nor do I reckon them by their deeds, but the one who sent me is the one who deals with that for them.

All of this is in the Gospel (Injil, the Gospel) that is in their hands. In it, the Messiah said: "O Lord, they have known that You sent me, and I have made Your name known to them." Thus he declared that God is his Lord, that he is His servant and His messenger.

In it also: "God, the One, the Lord of everything, sent whomever He sent from among mankind to the whole world, that they might turn to the truth." In it he also said: "The works that I do bear witness for me that God sent me to this world." In it also: "How far I am from, and how weary I am of, creating anything on my own accord! Rather, I speak and answer with what my Lord has taught me." And he said: "God anointed me and sent me, and I only worship the One God for the Day of Salvation."

He said: "God, Mighty and Majestic, has not eaten, and does not eat; He has not drunk, and does not drink; He has not slept, and does not sleep; He has not begotten, and is not begotten; and no one has seen Him and survived."

By this, the secret of His statement, exalted is He, in the Great Qur'an becomes clear to you: "The Messiah, son of Maryam, was only a messenger; messengers had passed away before him, and his mother was a truthful woman. Both of them used to eat food." (This is) a reminder to the Christians of what the Messiah had told them.

He also said in his supplication when he asked his Lord to revive the dead: "I thank You and praise You, for You answer my prayer at this time and at every time. So I ask You to revive this dead man, that the Children of Israel may know that You sent me and that You answer my prayer."

In the Gospel also: when the Messiah left Samaria (al-Samiriyyah) and reached Jaljal, he said: "No prophet is honored in his homeland." Thus he did not go beyond claiming prophethood.

In the Gospel of Luke: "No prophet is accepted in his homeland. So how will you accept me?" In the Gospel of Mark: a man came to the Messiah and said: "Good Teacher, what good shall I do to inherit eternal life?" The Messiah said to him: "Why do you call me good? No one is good but God alone. You know the commandments: Do not steal, do not commit adultery, do not bear false witness, do not defraud, and honor your father and mother."

In the Gospel of John: when the Jews wanted to seize him, he raised his eyes to heaven and said: "The time has come, O my God; so exalt me in Your presence, and make for me a way that I may grant eternal life to everyone You have given me. Eternal life is that they believe in You as the one God, and in the Messiah whom You sent. I have glorified You over the people of the earth, and I have borne what You commanded me; so exalt me."

He claimed nothing beyond being a servant, a sent one, commanded and dispatched. In the Gospel of Matthew: "Do not call anyone on earth your father, for your Father is one, who is in heaven alone. And do not be called teachers, for your Teacher is the Messiah alone."

In their language, "Ab" means the Lord who nurtures. That is, "Do not say: your God and your Lord is on earth; rather He is in heaven." Then he lowered himself to the station to which his Lord and Owner had lowered him: his aim was that he teaches on earth, while their God is the One who is in heaven.

In the Gospel of Luke, when he called upon God and brought the woman's son back to life, they said: "This prophet is truly great, and God has visited His people."

In the Gospel of John, the Messiah raised his voice in the house and said to the Jews: "You know me and my place. I did not come of my own accord; the Truth has sent me, and you do not know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. I know that I am from Him, and He sent me."

Thus he added nothing to his claim beyond what the prophets claimed. Yet the Trinitarians held on to his saying "I am from Him" and said: "A true God from a true God." In the Qur'an: "A messenger from God." And Hud said: "But I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds," and Salih said the same! But the nation of misguidance, as God described them, follow the ambiguous (mutashabih, ambiguous verses) and reject the clear (muhkam, decisive verses).

Also in the Gospel: he said to the Jews, when they said to him: "We are the sons of God," "If your father were God, you would have obeyed me, for I am a messenger from Him. I came forth and did not come of my own accord, but He sent me. But you do not accept my counsel, and you are unable to hear my words. You are only sons of Satan, and you want to fulfill his desires."

In the Gospel also: the Jews surrounded him and said: "How long will you keep your matter hidden? If you are the Messiah whom we await, then tell us plainly."

They did not say: "If you are God or the son of God," for he had not claimed that, and none of his enemies or followers understood it from him.

Also in the Gospel: the Jews wanted to seize him, so they sent the officers, and the officers returned to their commanders. They said to them: "Why did you not take him?" They said: "We have never heard a man speak as justly as he does." The Jews said: "Are you also deceived? Do you think any of the commanders or chief priests believed in him?" One of their elders said to them: "Does our Scripture judge anyone before hearing him?" They said to him: "Search the Scriptures and you will see that no prophet comes from Jaljal." The Jews did not say this except after he had lowered himself to the station to which his Lord and Owner had lowered him, that he is a prophet. Had they known of a claim to divinity from him, they would have mentioned it to him and denounced it. It would have been the greatest reason to turn people away from obeying him, because his lie would have been known through the senses, reason, human nature, and the agreement of the prophets.

Indeed, it would have been necessary for God, glory be to Him, if it had been decreed in His wisdom that He would appear to His servants, descend from the throne of His greatness, and deal with them Himself, that He not enter a woman's womb and remain in her belly among urine, feces, and blood for months. Yet He did all that. He did not come out as a child who nurses and cries. Yet He did all that. He did not eat with people, drink with people, or sleep with them. Yet He did all that. And so He does not urinate or defecate. He refrains from excrement, which is a deficiency that man is afflicted with in this abode because of his lack and need. He, exalted is He, is the One specially characterized by attributes of perfection, described with the descriptions of majesty, whom neither His heavens nor His earth could contain. His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth. How then could a woman's womb contain Him? Exalted is the Lord of the worlds! Yet all of you agree that the Messiah ate, drank, urinated, defecated, and slept.

O assembly of Trinitarians and worshippers of the Cross, tell us: who was holding up the heavens and the earth when their Lord and Creator was tied to a wooden cross, His hands and feet bound with ropes, and the hand that perfected the worlds was nailed? Did the heavens and the earth remain empty of their God and Originator?

And did this great matter befall Him? Or do you say that He appointed someone else to manage them, and descended from His throne in order to tie Himself to a wooden cross, to taste the heat of the nails, and to bring the curse upon Himself, since He said in the Torah (Tawrah, the Torah): "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree"? Or do you say (and this, in reality, is your saying): "We do not know, but this is in the Books, and the fathers said it, and they are the example." The answer to them is as follows.

So we say to you: and if not, O assembly of Trinitarians, worshippers of the Cross, what is it that led you to the divinity of the Messiah?

(The First Doubt)

If you derived it from his being seized by his enemies, as you claim, and dragged to the wooden cross, with a crown of thorns on his head, while they spat in his face and slapped him, then they mounted him on that shameful vehicle, bound his hands and feet with ropes, drove nails into them, and he cried out and hung there, then his soul departed and he was placed in his tomb, then how sound is such reasoning among people like you, who are more astray than cattle, and who are a disgrace to all mankind!

And if you say: "We only derived his being God from the fact that he was not born of a human, and if he were created, he would have been born of a human. If this reasoning is sound, then Adam is the God of the Messiah, and he is more worthy of being God than him, for he has neither mother nor father, while the Messiah has a mother."

"Also make Eve a fifth god, for she has no mother, and she is more wondrous than the creation of the Messiah."

God, glory be to Him and exalted, has varied the creation of Adam and his descendants to demonstrate His power and that He does what He wills. He created Adam neither from a male nor from a female; He created his spouse Eve from a male and not from a female; He created His servant the Messiah from a female and not from a male; and He created the rest of the species from male and female.

And if you say: "We derived his being God from the fact that he raised the dead, and none can raise the dead except God, so make Moses another god, for he brought about something the Messiah never brought, nor anything close to it, namely turning a staff into a great living serpent. This is more far-reaching than restoring life to a body that once had life in it. If you say: 'This is not the raising of the dead,' then Elisha the Prophet raised the dead, and they acknowledge this."

Likewise, Elijah the Prophet also brought a child back to life by God's permission, and Moses also brought back to life, by God's permission, the seventy men of his people who had died.

In your Books there is much of this concerning the prophets and the disciples. Has any of them become God because of it?

And if you say: "We made him God because of the miracles that appeared at his hands," then the miracles of Moses are more wondrous, and more wondrous still.

And this Elijah the prophet blessed the flour and oil of an old woman, and the flour in her sack and the oil in her jar did not run out for seven years.

And if you made him God because he fed thousands of people from a few loaves, then Moses fed his nation for forty years with manna and quail! And this Muhammad (ﷺ), son of 'Abd Allah, fed the entire army from very little food until they were satisfied and filled their containers, and he gave drink to all of them from a little water that did not cover the hand, until they filled every waterskin in the army. This is transmitted from him through mass transmission (tawatur).

And if you say: "We made him God because he cried out to the sea and its waves became still," then Moses struck the sea with his staff, and it split into twelve paths, and the water stood between the paths like walls, and he caused twelve springs to gush forth from the hard rock.

And if you made him God because he healed the blind and the leper and raised the dead, then the signs of Moses and Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them all, are more wondrous than that.

And if you made him God because he claimed it, then the matter is either as you say about him, or he only claimed servanthood and need, and that he is a nurtured, created, made being. If it was as you claim about him, then he is the brother of the False Messiah (al-Masih al-Dajjal), and not a believer nor truthful, let alone a noble prophet, and his recompense is Hell, and evil is the destination, as God, exalted is He, said: "And whoever among them says, 'I am a god besides Him,' that is who We will recompense with Hell."

And whoever claims divinity other than God is among the greatest enemies of God, like Pharaoh, Nimrod, and their likes, the enemies of God. Thus you have removed the Messiah from God's honor, His prophethood, and His messengership, and made him the greatest of God's enemies. For this reason you were the most hostile of people toward the Messiah, in the guise of a loving ally!

Among the clearest signs by which the falsehood of the False Messiah is known is that he claims divinity, so God sends against him His servant and messenger, the Messiah of guidance, son of Maryam, who kills him and shows the creatures that he was a liar and a fabricator. Had he been God, he would not have been killed, let alone crucified, nailed, and spat upon!

And if the Messiah only claimed that he is the servant and messenger of God, as all the Gospels testify, and reason and human nature indicate, and you yourselves bore witness to his divinity, which is the reality, then you have not presented any proof of his divinity except denying his claim. You have mentioned in your Gospels, in many places, what explicitly affirms his servanthood, that he is a nurtured, created being, that he is the son of man, and that he claimed nothing but prophethood and messengership. Yet you denied him in all of that, and you believed the one who lied about God and about him!

And if you say: "We made him a god because he informed about what would happen after him of matters," then the prophets were likewise. Indeed, many people inform about what will happen after them of matters, and they inform about particular future events, and it comes to pass as they said.

Much of this occurs for soothsayers (kuhhan), astrologers (munajjimin), and sorcerers (saharah)!

And if you say: "We made him a god because he called himself the Son of God in more than one place in the Injil (Gospel), such as his saying: 'I am going to my Father,' and 'I am asking my Father,' and similar things, and the son of God is God." It is said to them: "Then make yourselves all gods, for in the Injil, in more than one place, he calls [God] his Father and your Father, such as his saying: 'I am going to my Father and your Father.'"

And in it: "Do not call your father on earth, for your Father who is in heaven is one." This is abundant in the Injil, and it indicates that "the Father" for them means "the Lord."

And if you make him a god because his disciples claimed that, and they were the people most knowledgeable about him, then your Gospels that are in your hands refute you, and all of them are most explicit in clarity that they claimed for him nothing except what he claimed for himself, that he is a servant ('abd).

Thus Matthew says in the ninth chapter of his Gospel, citing the prophecy of Isaiah about the Messiah on behalf of God, Mighty and Majestic: "This is My servant whom I have chosen, My beloved in whom My soul delights."

And in the eleventh chapter of his Gospel: "I thank You, O Lord of heaven and earth."

And here Luke says at the end of his Gospel: The Messiah met him and another of his disciples on the road, a angel (malak), while they were grieved, and he said to them while they did not recognize him: "Why are you grieved?" They said: "It is as if you were a stranger in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), since you do not know what happened in it in these days concerning the matter of Jesus of Nazareth, for he was a man, a prophet, mighty and pious in his words and deeds before God and before the community. They seized him and killed him." And this is very abundant in the Injil!

And if you say: "We made him a god because he ascended to heaven," then Enoch (Akhnukh) and Elijah (Ilyas) have ascended to heaven, and they are alive, honored, no power has harmed them, and no one covets them.

And the Muslims are unanimous that Muhammad (ﷺ) ascended to heaven, and he was a pure servant. And these angels ascend to heaven, and these souls of the believers ascend to heaven after separating from their bodies, and they do not thereby leave servitude.
